doc_description: MGM Resorts International’s Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2022, highlighting its asset‑light pivot via VICI’s acquisition of MGP (deconsolidation) and resulting ~$1.7B annual triple‑net rent, portfolio reshaping (acquisition of The Cosmopolitan operations, sale of The Mirage), digital expansion (LeoVegas acquisition and BetMGM JV), Macau concession renewal with accelerated amortization of the prior subconcession, a strong Las Vegas rebound, significant share repurchases, and comprehensive risk and lease disclosures.

structure.title: Preface
structure.summary:
- Document type: MGM Resorts International Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2022, with standard SEC cover disclosures (registrant info, NYSE listing under “MGM,” well-known seasoned issuer, large accelerated filer, auditor attestation of internal control, market value of non-affiliate shares, shares outstanding, and incorporation by reference of the proxy statement for Part III).
- Table of Contents: Lists Parts I–IV, including Business, Risk Factors, Properties, Legal Proceedings, MD&A, Market Risk, Financial Statements, Controls and Procedures, and other required items.
- Business overview (Item 1): MGM Resorts is a holding company operating a global gaming and entertainment portfolio, including hotels, casinos, convention spaces, entertainment, restaurants, nightlife, retail, and online sports betting/iGaming. The company emphasizes reinvestment to maintain premier resort quality and scaling its online gaming business.
- Operations footprint: 17 domestic casino resorts and two Macau resorts via a 56% controlling interest in MGM China (MGM Grand Paradise). Online operations include consolidated LeoVegas AB and BetMGM, LLC, a 50% joint venture with Entain. Domestic real estate is leased under triple-net agreements; prior to the VICI transaction, MGP served as landlord under a master lease.
- Strategy and business developments: Execution of an asset-light model to monetize real estate and redeploy capital to balance sheet strength, growth initiatives, and shareholder returns. Focus areas include U.S. online sports betting and iGaming (BetMGM), global online expansion (LeoVegas), digital capabilities, and Asia diversification (development efforts in Japan).
- Key transactions highlighted:
  - 2018: Formation of BetMGM with Entain; MGM provided U.S. market access, Entain provided technology.
  - 2019: Acquisition of Empire City Casino’s real property and operations; subsequent sale of developed real property to MGP and addition to the master lease.
  - March 2019: Amendment to MGP master lease related to Park MGM/NoMad Las Vegas rebranding improvements.

structure.summary:
- Identifies MGM Resorts International, its subsidiaries, and naming conventions (MGM Resorts, MGM China, MGP).
- Corporate overview: Delaware holding company operating a global gaming and entertainment portfolio, including hotels, casinos, meeting/conference venues, live entertainment, dining/nightlife/retail, and sports betting/online gaming.
- Strategic focus: operate premier, high-quality resorts; continual reinvestment in properties and amenities; aim to build a scaled global online gaming business.
- Scope of operations as of December 31, 2022: 17 domestic casino resorts; 56% controlling interest in MGM China operating two Macau resorts; online gaming via consolidated LeoVegas and 50% JV BetMGM.
- Real estate/lease structure: domestic resort real estate leased under triple-net agreements; prior to the VICI Transaction, MGP (then consolidated) acted as landlord through a master lease.
- Asset-light business model: monetizing real estate to redeploy capital toward balance sheet strength, growth initiatives, and shareholder returns; emphasis on U.S. online sports betting and iGaming (BetMGM), expansion of digital capabilities, LeoVegas acquisition, and Asia diversification including development efforts in Japan.
- Key business developments/transactions:
  - 2018: Formation of BetMGM with Entain, granting BetMGM exclusive access to MGM’s U.S. sports betting, poker, and online gaming operations and to Entain’s U.S. technology.
  - 2019: Acquisition of Empire City Casino (operations and real property) for approximately $865 million; subsequent transfer of developed real property to MGP and addition to the master lease.
  - 2019: Amendment to the MGP master lease for improvements tied to the Park MGM and NoMad Las Vegas rebranding.

structure.title: Business
structure.heading: Item 1. Business
structure.start_phrase:
MGM Resorts International is referred to as the “Company,” “MGM Resorts,” or the “Registrant,” and together with its subsidiaries may also be
referred to as “we,” “us” or “our.”
structure.summary:
- Overview: MGM Resorts International is a Delaware holding company operating a global gaming and entertainment portfolio, including 17 domestic casino resorts and two Macau resorts via 56% ownership of MGM China; digital operations include consolidated LeoVegas and 50% JV BetMGM. Most domestic real estate is leased under triple-net agreements; former subsidiary MGP was deconsolidated after the VICI transaction.

- Asset-light strategy and key transactions (2018–2023): Formation of BetMGM with Entain; acquisition and subsequent real estate monetization of Empire City; Bellagio sale-leaseback to BREIT venture; sale of Circus Circus; contribution of MGM Grand Las Vegas and Mandalay Bay real estate to a VICI/BREIT venture with related lease; multiple redemptions of MGP OP units; acquisition of remaining 50% of CityCenter and sale-leaseback of Aria/Vdara; selection as Osaka IR partner and submission of Japan development plan; sale of MGM Springfield real estate to MGP; VICI’s acquisition of MGP and amended master lease; acquisition of The Cosmopolitan operations and related lease; acquisition of LeoVegas; renewal of Macau gaming concession; sale of The Mirage operations; sale of Gold Strike Tunica operations. COVID-19 impacts referenced.

- Segments and operations: Three reportable segments—Las Vegas Strip Resorts; Regional Operations; MGM China. Las Vegas derives over half of net revenue from non-gaming; Regional primarily from gaming. Operations run largely 24/7, with performance influenced by conventions, events, and holiday play. Broad gaming offerings with premium rooms and lounges.

- MGM China: Operates MGM Macau and MGM Cotai under a Macau concession; strategic focus on main floor/premium mass gaming; VIP junket promoter operations suspended; competition includes five other Macau concessionaires and regional Asian markets.

- Customers, competition, and marketing: Competes with domestic and international gaming/hospitality offerings and non-gaming destinations. Competitive focus on prime locations, high-quality amenities, service, unique entertainment, digital offerings, and loyalty. Marketing leverages data-driven analytics and regional offices. MGM Rewards is a tiered, cross-resort loyalty program integrated with gaming and non-gaming; Golden Lion Club and M life Rewards in Macau.

- Strategy: Vision to be the premier global gaming entertainment company, guided by five pillars—people/culture, customer-centricity, operational excellence, disciplined capital allocation, and gaming entertainment innovation. Growth priorities include Japan integrated resort, leadership in U.S. online sports betting and iGaming via BetMGM (omni-channel integration with MGM Rewards and on-property sportsbooks), international digital expansion via LeoVegas, and pursuing a full-scale New York license. Ongoing operating model optimization and cost initiatives.

- Technology: Emphasis on digital experience, data/analytics, e-commerce, and integration of physical resorts with digital casino/sports betting; deployment of a new loyalty tech platform and bundling capabilities; aims to enhance customer engagement, decision-making, and operational efficiency.

- ESG and sustainability: Board-level CSR/Sustainability governance; reporting aligned with GRI, SASB, and TCFD. Energy and carbon goals supported by the Mega Solar Array: 45% Scope 1&2 intensity reduction by 2025 (vs. 2007), 50% absolute Scope 1&2 reduction by 2030 (vs. 2019), 100% U.S. renewable electricity and 80% global by 2030; 30% Scope 3 reduction goal by 2030. Water stewardship policy and CDP Water Security “A” score.

- Trademarks: Extensive portfolio (e.g., Aria, Bellagio, The Cosmopolitan, Mandalay Bay, MGM brands, LeoVegas) registered in relevant jurisdictions; pursued and maintained for brand value.

- Human capital: Culture anchored by values (Captivate Our Audience, Inspire Excellence, Champion Inclusion, Win Together) and robust talent development (tuition reimbursement, student loan support, free online degrees, sabbaticals, recognition/onboarding). DE&I framework with 2025 goals (leadership access, 10% diverse supplier spend, supplier mentorship expansion, management training). Health, safety, and wellness initiatives (World of Wellbeing). Community engagement via MGM Resorts Foundation (employee emergency and community grants, volunteer programs). Workforce: ~46k full-time and 18k part-time U.S., ~10k at MGM China, ~1k at LeoVegas; ~38k under CBAs with multiple agreements expiring in 2023; MGM China and LeoVegas non-union.

- Regulation and compliance: Subject to extensive gaming regulation and general business laws (alcohol, smoking, AML, employment, ADA, zoning, environmental). Environmental liabilities monitored with no identified material issues. Detailed gaming regulations summarized in an incorporated exhibit.

- Forward-looking statements and risks: Caution regarding uncertainties; key risks include high leverage and fixed rent obligations; liquidity and covenant constraints; lease-related risks and landlord dependencies; Las Vegas concentration; credit and impairment risks; macroeconomic and travel sensitivity; co-investment risks (e.g., BetMGM); construction and insurance risks; trademark protection; labor relations; energy costs; expansion/divestiture execution; cybersecurity/data privacy; ESG execution/reputation; climate and water risks; regulatory and policy changes; international operations and FCPA; tax matters; litigation; continued COVID-19 impacts on Macau; restrictions on China-area gaming interests outside MGM China; Macau concession termination/redemption/extension risk; potential director/officer conflicts with MGM China.

- Executive leadership: CEO/President William J. Hornbuckle; COO Corey I. Sanders; CFO/Treasurer Jonathan S. Halkyard; Chief Legal & Administrative Officer/Secretary John M. McManus; President, Interactive Gary M. Fritz; brief backgrounds provided.

- Investor information: SEC filings accessible via company website and SEC EDGAR; website also used for timely MGM China information; web content not incorporated by reference.

structure.title: Risk Factors
structure.heading: Item 1A. Risk Factors
structure.start_phrase:
You should be aware that the occurrence of any of the events described in this section and elsewhere in this report or in any other of our filings with the
SEC could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial position, results of operations and cash flows.
structure.summary:
The excerpt is Item 1A (Risk Factors) from an annual report, presenting a summary and detailed discussion of risks that could materially affect the company’s business, financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows. Main points covered:

Overall structure
- A summarized list of principal risks followed by detailed discussions across four categories: (1) Substantial Financial Commitments, (2) Business, Industry, and Market Conditions, (3) Legal and Regulatory Matters and Public Policy, and (4) Macau Operations. Item 1B notes there are no unresolved SEC staff comments.

Risks related to substantial financial commitments
- High leverage and fixed obligations: Approximately $8.8B total debt (including $4.2B at MGM China); sensitivity to interest rates; reliance on distributions and credit facilities; significant maturities and refinancing risk.
- Large, escalating lease obligations: About $1.7B in annual triple‑net rent plus required capex; lease financial covenants may require cash collateral/letters of credit upon breach; inability to abate rent even during disruptions.
- Guarantees: Shortfall guarantees on Bellagio BREIT Venture ($3.01B) and VICI BREIT Venture ($3.0B) debts could require material payments if collateral is insufficient.
- Capital intensity: Ongoing maintenance/refurbishment needs; potential large investments (e.g., Japan integrated resort), BetMGM funding, and international digital initiatives may require additional capital and debt.

Risks related to business, industry, and market conditions
- Intense competition: From destination resorts, expanded U.S. retail gaming, peer‑to‑peer lodging, and rapidly growing online sports betting/iGaming; BetMGM faces strong competitors; potential cannibalization of land‑based operations; heightened mass‑market competition in Macau after junket retrenchment.
- Macroeconomic sensitivity: Inflation, recessions, supply chain and labor constraints, travel costs; dependence on U.S. (notably California) and Far East economic conditions.
- Dividend suspension: Regular dividends suspended in favor of share repurchases; uncertainty about resumption.
- Lease‑specific risks: Triple‑net terms shift maintenance, insurance, taxes, utilities, and capex to the tenant; limited ability to cease operations.
- Geographic concentration: Significant exposure to the Las Vegas Strip; dependence on air travel and constrained highway access from Southern California.
- Credit extension risk: Large casino credit/marker exposure, particularly to high‑end customers; collection challenges domestically and internationally.
- Asset impairment risk: Potential write‑downs of goodwill, intangibles, and long‑lived assets.
- Travel disruption risks: Terrorism, war/hostilities, and infectious disease outbreaks (e.g., COVID‑19) affecting visitation; limited insurance availability for certain perils.
- Co‑investment/JV risks: Shared control, funding needs, and governance challenges (e.g., BetMGM with Entain; potential Japan consortium), including counterparty financial issues.
- Development/construction risks: Financing, permitting, inflation, labor/material shortages, delays, regulatory deadlines/penalties; revenue displacement during renovations.
- Insurance limitations: Potential underinsurance, exclusions, higher costs, and lease‑mandated coverage requirements that may be hard to meet.
- Trademark protection: Enforcement challenges, especially internationally; potential brand/reputation harm.
- Labor relations: Large union workforce; expiring CBAs; risk of strikes, higher wages/benefits; multiemployer pension plan exposures.
- Energy costs: Sensitivity to electricity/fuel prices impacting operations and customer travel.
- M&A and divestitures: Integration, synergy realization, retention, unexpected costs, and execution risks.
- Cybersecurity and data privacy: Evolving U.S. and international laws (e.g., CCPA/CPRA, GDPR, China); prior breaches; third‑party vendor risk; potential fines, litigation, and operational disruptions; insurance may not be sufficient.
- ESG/reputation: Risks tied to diversity, sustainability, responsible gaming, supply chain, workplace conduct; potential effects on demand and talent.
- Climate and water: Extreme weather, drought (notably Las Vegas), supply interruptions, rising compliance costs, and water scarcity affecting operations and reputation.

Risks related to legal and regulatory matters and public policy
- Extensive gaming regulation: Suitability requirements; potential to be forced to disassociate from partners; changing rules, including for iGaming and online betting; need for approvals for financings and transactions.
- Non‑gaming regulations: Alcohol, environment, smoking bans (e.g., Macau indoor smoking room rules), labor, advertising, zoning/building codes; COVID‑19 related restrictions.
- AML/Bank Secrecy Act: Significant cash handling, reporting, and examination risk; potential penalties for violations.
- Anti‑corruption: FCPA and similar laws; risk of severe sanctions for violations by the company or non‑controlled ventures.
- Taxation: Potential increases in gaming and other taxes; uncertainty around foreign tax credit deferred tax asset valuation.
- Litigation: Exposure to current and future claims that could materially affect results and reputation.

Risks related to Macau operations
- COVID‑19 impacts: Prior property closures/suspensions; changing travel/entry restrictions; uncertainty of future measures and financial effects.
- Regional non‑compete: No gaming interests in China, Macau, Hong Kong, or Taiwan outside MGM China under the non‑compete deed.
- Concession risks: Macau government can terminate without compensation under certain circumstances, redeem after year eight with indemnity, or decline extension beyond 2032; loss of concession would transfer casino premises/equipment to the government without compensation.
- Investment commitments: Required MOP 16.7B (majority non‑gaming) with potential increases tied to market GGR; financing and compliance risks.
- Evolving regulation and approvals: Obligation to comply with future laws; limited recourse during disputes; potential adverse effects on construction/operations.
- International operating risks: Legal, regulatory, economic, labor, tax, FX, political, and health risks inherent in non‑U.S. operations.
- Conflicts of interest: Overlapping directors/officers between the company and MGM China may create fiduciary conflicts.

structure.title: Unresolved Staff Comments
structure.heading: Item 1B. Unresolved Staff Comments
structure.start_phrase: null.
structure.summary:
- Reliance on Macau gaming concession for MGM Grand Paradise, with obligations to comply with government interpretations and no precedent on termination outcomes; loss of the concession would materially harm business, financial condition, results, and cash flows.
- Concession expires December 31, 2032; uncertainty around obtaining an extension or new concession and the potential for unfavorable terms, added fees, or inadequate compensation if the concession is redeemed.
- Risks of operating outside the U.S., particularly in Macau/China: regulatory and policy changes; government program shifts; anti-bribery compliance (e.g., FCPA and similar laws); China’s economic conditions and travel/currency controls; challenges in staffing and managing foreign operations; differing labor and environmental/health/safety regulations; disease outbreaks (including COVID-19); tax law changes; political/military instability; economic volatility (inflation, recession, interest rates); and judicial uncertainty. These could adversely affect performance and cash flows.
- Foreign exchange exposure: a stronger U.S. dollar can reduce reported income from non-USD revenues.
- Potential conflicts of interest due to overlapping directors/officers between the company and MGM China, creating dual fiduciary duties and possible conflicts in decisions and intercompany arrangements.
- Unresolved SEC staff comments: none.

structure.title: Reserved
structure.heading: Item 6. Reserved
structure.summary:
- Item 6 is reserved; Item 7 provides MD&A comparing year ended December 31, 2022 to 2021, with prior-year comparisons referenced to the 2021 Form 10-K.
- Business overview: operates premium casino resorts offering gaming, hotel, convention, dining, entertainment, retail, and other amenities; continually reinvests to maintain competitiveness.
- Revenue and cash flows: predominantly cash-based (gaming and non-gaming), with operating cash flow used to pay rent, fund capex, repay debt, pursue development, and return capital to shareholders.
- Asset/lease structure: domestic resort real estate is leased under triple-net agreements; ongoing investments in room remodels, restaurants, entertainment, and amenities.
- Digital strategy: offers online gaming and sports betting via LeoVegas (consolidated) and BetMGM (equity affiliate), with intent to access new iGaming and online sports betting markets.
- Capital allocation: focus on maintaining a strong balance sheet and liquidity, returning capital to shareholders, and pursuing strategic development initiatives; results influenced by access to and cost of capital.
- Seasonality and variability: operations not inherently seasonal, but interim results vary with convention timing, Far East baccarat volumes, marketing/special events for high-end customers, and major holidays (e.g., New Year, Lunar New Year). A meaningful share of operating income comes from high-end/VIP play, adding variability. Performance depends on success with convention/business travelers and specific regional high-end customer segments.
- COVID-19 impact: significant effects on business, financial condition, results, and cash flows across 2020–2022.
  - U.S. operations: full closures in March 2020; phased reopenings through 2020–early 2021 with capacity and amenity restrictions that eased and were largely removed by mid-2021. As of December 31, 2022, all domestic properties were open without operating restrictions, though Omicron pressured travel and volumes early Q1 2022.
  - Macau operations: temporary closure on February 5, 2020 and reopening February 20, 2020 with health safeguards (reduced table seating, slot spacing, limited restaurant/bar hours, temperature checks, masks). Tourist visa issuance from mainland China resumed in stages Aug–Sep 2020, but various travel/entry restrictions (e.g., suspended Hong Kong–Macau ferries, testing requirements) persisted.

structure.title: Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations
structure.heading: Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations
structure.start_phrase: This management’s discussion and analysis of financial condition and results of operations includes discussion as of and for the year ended December 31, 2022 compared to December 31, 2021.
structure.summary:
- Scope: Management’s Discussion and Analysis (MD&A) comparing year ended Dec 31, 2022 to 2021; prior 2021 vs 2020 discussion referenced in the 2021 Form 10-K.

- Business overview and KPIs:
  - Operates casino resorts with gaming, hotel, convention, dining, entertainment, and retail; domestic real estate largely under triple-net leases.
  - Cash-based revenue model; depends on operating cash flow to fund rent, capex, debt service, and shareholder returns.
  - iGaming and online sports betting via consolidated LeoVegas and unconsolidated BetMGM.
  - Performance drivers include conventions, high-end gaming volumes, holiday periods, and marketing events; results can be volatile due to VIP/high-end mix.
  - KPIs: table drop/slots handle and hold; hotel occupancy, ADR, REVPAR; MGM China VIP turnover and win rates.

- COVID-19 impact:
  - U.S. properties reopened through 2020-2021 with restrictions easing by mid-2021; omicron dampened early 2022.
  - Macau faced stringent travel/testing/quarantine rules, periodic suspensions (notably July and late Oct/Nov 2022 at MGM Cotai), with visa resumption in Nov 2022 and broad lifting of restrictions by Jan–Feb 2023.

- Visitation trends:
  - Las Vegas visitor volume up 21% in 2022, supported by conventions and events.
  - Macau visitor arrivals down 26% in 2022 due to travel restrictions.

- Major strategic and portfolio actions:
  - 2020: Contributed MGM Grand Las Vegas/Mandalay Bay real estate to VICI BREIT Venture; related lease arrangements and shortfall guarantee.
  - 2020–2021: Redemptions of MGP OP units for cash.
  - 2021: Acquired remaining 50% of CityCenter (now consolidated); sold Aria/Vdara real estate in sale-leaseback; added MGM Springfield to MGP master lease.
  - 2022: Completed VICI Transaction (deconsolidated MGP; retained ~1% VICI OP interest; new master lease with VICI); acquired operations of The Cosmopolitan (and leased its real estate); acquired LeoVegas; sold The Mirage operations.
  - 2023: Sold Gold Strike Tunica operations; VICI master lease amended to remove Mirage and Gold Strike with corresponding rent reductions.
  - Macau: New gaming law (June 2022) shortened concession terms, ended subconcessions; accelerated amortization of MGM Grand Paradise subconcession (expired Dec 31, 2022); awarded new concession effective Jan 1, 2023.

- 2022 consolidated results:
  - Net revenues: $13.1B (+36% YoY), driven by Las Vegas strength and The Cosmopolitan/Aria contributions; Macau significantly weaker.
  - Operating income: $1.4B (down 37%) as higher rent and amortization (notably $2.5B accelerated Macau subconcession amortization) offset gains.
  - Key gains: $2.3B net gain on REIT transactions (VICI) and $1.1B gain on Mirage operations sale; 2021 included $1.6B gain on CityCenter consolidation.
  - Net income attributable to MGM Resorts: $1.47B.

- Segment performance:
  - Las Vegas Strip Resorts: Net revenues $8.4B (+77%); casino +36%; rooms +95% (occupancy 89%, ADR $229, REVPAR $203); F&B +109%; entertainment/retail/other +87%. Adjusted Property EBITDAR $3.14B (+81%), margin 37.4%.
  - Regional Operations: Net revenues $3.82B (+12%); casino +7% with higher table and slots win; rooms +29%; F&B and other +~40%; Adjusted Property EBITDAR $1.29B (+6%), margin 33.9%.
  - MGM China: Net revenues $674M (-44%); VIP turnover and main floor drop declined; Adjusted Property EBITDAR loss of $203M vs +$25M in 2021.

- Non-GAAP measures:
  - Definitions and rationale for Adjusted Property EBITDAR (segment GAAP measure), Adjusted EBITDAR (valuation metric), and Same-Store Adjusted Property EBITDAR.
  - Same-store disclosures exclude The Cosmopolitan and Aria post-acquisition and The Mirage pre-disposition to facilitate period comparisons.

- Other financial items:
  - Property transactions, net, primarily $1.07B gain on Mirage operations sale.
  - Unconsolidated affiliates: BetMGM loss widened; VICI BREIT Venture income through April 2022; CityCenter no longer equity-accounted post-2021 acquisition.
  - Interest expense decreased to $596M (from $800M) due to deconsolidation of MGP OP notes; other income included higher interest income and swap impacts.
  - Income taxes: 2022 effective rate 77.1% (unbenefited Macau losses and state deferred items; partially offset by Macau-related benefits); low cash taxes due to refunds.

- Guarantor information:
  - Most material domestic subsidiaries guarantee principal debt (with notable exclusions: MGM Grand Detroit, MGM National Harbor, MGM Springfield, foreign subs including LeoVegas and MGM China); summary combined financials provided.

- Liquidity and capital resources:
  - 2022 cash flows: Operating $1.76B; Investing +$2.12B (VICI proceeds and Mirage sale, offset by Cosmopolitan/LeoVegas acquisitions, $765M capex, BetMGM contributions); Financing -$3.02B (net debt +$78M; $2.8B share repurchases; distributions to NCI).
  - Capital allocation: Repurchased $2.8B shares in 2022; remaining $475M under March 2022 $2B program at year-end; new $2B program announced Feb 2023; minimal dividends in 2022; dividend suspended Feb 2023 in favor of buybacks.
  - Balance sheet: $5.9B cash and equivalents (incl. $860M at MGM China) plus $124M restricted cash at MGM China; $8.8B total debt; no draws on corporate revolver; $1.3B maturities in next 12 months expected to be repaid with cash.
  - Lease obligations: ~$1.7B annual cash rent over next 12 months under triple-net leases.
  - 2023 plans: Capex ~$795–$835M domestically and ~$110–$150M in Macau; ~$75M contributions to BetMGM; exploring NY commercial gaming and Japan opportunities; continue share repurchases.

- Critical accounting policies and estimates:
  - Casino receivables loss reserves: methodology, judgments, and 2022 balances ($501M receivables; $98M reserve; 20% reserve ratio).
  - Fixed asset capitalization judgments and useful lives.
  - Impairment testing for long-lived assets, goodwill, and indefinite-lived intangibles; significant assumptions and sensitivities (including Empire City dependent on NY license outcomes).
  - Macau subconcession: unit of account determination, recoverability testing, and accelerated amortization due to legal changes and expiration.
  - Investments in unconsolidated affiliates: no material impairments in 2022.
  - Income taxes: valuation allowances ($2.6B domestic; $245M foreign), audit uncertainties, and factors affecting realization of deferred tax assets.

structure.title: Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk
structure.heading: Item 7A. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk
structure.start_phrase: In addition to the inherent risks associated with our normal operations, we are also exposed to additional market risks.
structure.summary:
- Focus: Item 7A—Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk.
- Primary market risks: interest rate risk on debt and foreign currency risk related to MGM China (MGM Macau and MGM Cotai).
- Interest rate risk management: company manages mix of long-term fixed-rate and short-term borrowings; fixed-rate debt shields current earnings/cash flow but exposes future periods as it matures; no speculative derivative positions.
- Debt profile at December 31, 2022:
  - Variable-rate borrowings were ~17% of total, about $1.51 billion, with an overall average interest rate of ~7.0%, largely maturing in 2024.
  - Fixed-rate debt totaled about $7.25 billion (fair value ~$6.85 billion); average interest rates by maturity range roughly 4.8%–6.0% (overall ~5.5%).
- Foreign currency risk: exposure mainly from Hong Kong dollar (functional currency of MGM China) versus U.S. dollar.
  - Potential changes in policies or economic conditions in the U.S., China, Macau, or Hong Kong, including any change to the HKD/USD peg, could create exchange rate volatility.
  - U.S. dollar–denominated debt at MGM China heightens exposure; a 1% weakening of HKD to USD would have resulted in a ~$28 million foreign currency transaction loss as of year-end 2022.

structure.title: Financial Statements and Supplementary Data
structure.heading: Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data
structure.start_phrase: Financial statement schedules have been omitted because they are not applicable, or the required information is included in the consolidated financial statements or the notes thereto.
structure.summary:
- Item 8 presents MGM Resorts International’s audited consolidated financial statements and notes for the years ended December 31, 2022, 2021, and 2020; required schedules are omitted as not applicable.
- Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm: Deloitte & Touche LLP (PCAOB ID: 34) issued:
  - An unqualified opinion on internal control over financial reporting (ICFR) as of December 31, 2022, under COSO 2013.
  - An unqualified opinion on the consolidated financial statements for 2022, 2021, and 2020.
  - Management’s ICFR assessment excluded The Cosmopolitan of Las Vegas (acquired May 17, 2022), representing ~11% of total assets and ~6% of total revenues for 2022; ICFR audit scope similarly excluded it.
  - Reports dated February 24, 2023; auditor of the Company since 2002.
- Critical Audit Matters:
  1) The Cosmopolitan acquisition (Notes 1 and 4):
     - Purchase price ≈ $1.7 billion; PPA recognized intangibles (trademarks $130m indefinite-lived; customer lists $95m amortized 7 years) and goodwill ≈ $1.3b.
     - Auditing focused on management forecasts (revenues/expenses) and discount rates used in fair value measurements; involved testing controls, benchmarking forecasts, and using fair value specialists.
  2) MGM Grand Paradise gaming subconcession in Macau (Notes 1 and 7):
     - New Macau gaming law (June 21, 2022) discontinued subconcessions and changed concession rights/obligations.
     - Company determined separate units of account for the old subconcession and new concession; revised the subconcession’s useful life to end December 31, 2022, resulting in accelerated amortization and full amortization by year-end.
     - Audit work included controls testing, inspection of laws/agreements, technical accounting evaluation under ASC 350-30, and recalculation of amortization.
- Consolidated Balance Sheets highlights (December 31, 2022 vs. 2021):
  - Total assets increased to $45.7b from $40.9b.
  - Cash and cash equivalents rose to $5.9b (from $4.7b); restricted cash reduced to $0 (from $500m).
  - Assets held for sale introduced at $608m.
  - Property and equipment, net decreased to $5.2b (from $14.4b), while operating lease right-of-use assets increased to $24.5b (from $11.5b), reflecting significant lease-related changes.
  - Goodwill increased to $5.0b (from $3.5b); other intangible assets, net decreased to $1.6b (from $3.6b).
  - Investments in and advances to unconsolidated affiliates declined to $173m (from $967m).
- Liabilities and Equity:
  - Total current liabilities increased to $4.5b; includes $540m liabilities related to assets held for sale.
  - Long-term debt, net decreased to $7.4b (from $11.8b); operating lease liabilities increased to $25.1b (from $11.8b).
  - Deferred income taxes increased to $3.0b (from $2.4b).
  - Total stockholders’ equity declined to $5.2b (from $11.0b), driven largely by a reduction in noncontrolling interests to $379m (from $4.9b).
  - MGM Resorts International stockholders’ equity was $4.8b; retained earnings increased to $4.79b; AOCI improved to a $33.5m gain; capital in excess of par reduced to $0.
  - Common shares outstanding decreased to ~379.1m (from ~453.8m), indicating significant share repurchases or equity transactions.

structure.title: Consolidated Financial Statements
structure.heading: Consolidated Financial Statements
structure.summary:
- Contents: Consolidated Balance Sheets (Dec 31, 2022 and 2021), Statements of Operations, Comprehensive Income (Loss), Cash Flows, Stockholders’ Equity for 2020–2022, and Notes (Organization and major 2022 transactions).
- Balance sheet highlights:
  - Total assets rose to $45.7B from $40.9B; cash and cash equivalents increased to $5.9B.
  - Property and equipment, net, declined sharply (to $5.2B from $14.4B), while operating lease right-of-use assets and liabilities increased significantly (ROU assets to $24.5B; lease liabilities to $25.1B), reflecting REIT/lease transactions.
  - Long-term debt decreased (to $7.4B from $11.8B).
  - Assets and liabilities held for sale recognized, tied to divestitures.
  - Stockholders’ equity decreased (to $5.2B from $11.0B) due to deconsolidation of MGP and substantial share repurchases; noncontrolling interests declined markedly.
- Results of operations:
  - Revenues rebounded strongly in 2022 to $13.1B (from $9.7B in 2021 and $5.2B in 2020), with growth across casino, rooms, food & beverage, and other categories.
  - Significant gains recognized in 2022: property transactions and REIT-related gains; elevated depreciation and amortization.
  - Operating income of $1.44B in 2022 (vs. $2.28B in 2021, which included a large CityCenter consolidation gain).
  - Net income attributable to MGM Resorts International of $1.47B in 2022; diluted EPS $3.49; weighted average diluted shares declined due to buybacks.
- Comprehensive income:
  - Positive other comprehensive income in 2022 driven by foreign currency translation and cash flow hedge gains.
- Cash flows:
  - Operating cash flow strong at $1.76B in 2022.
  - Investing provided net cash of $2.12B, with large proceeds from real estate transactions and a resort sale, offset by acquisitions (The Cosmopolitan operations and LeoVegas).
  - Financing used $3.02B, dominated by share repurchases, debt activity, and distributions; ending cash and restricted cash ~$6.04B.
- Stockholders’ equity activity:
  - Shares outstanding decreased (379.1M at 12/31/22 vs. 453.8M at 12/31/21); capital in excess of par reduced to zero; continued modest dividends; substantial impact from deconsolidation of MGP on noncontrolling interests and AOCI.
- Organization and key 2022 transactions (Notes):
  - MGM is a global gaming and entertainment company with extensive U.S. properties and a 56% controlling interest in MGM China; 98% controlling interest in LeoVegas; 50% JV interest in BetMGM.
  - VICI Transaction (Apr 29, 2022): VICI acquired MGP; MGM deconsolidated MGP, received an interest in VICI OP, and entered an amended and restated master lease with VICI.
  - The Cosmopolitan operations acquired May 17, 2022, with a related lease of the real estate assets.
  - LeoVegas acquired Sept 7, 2022.
  - Dispositions: The Mirage sold in Dec 2022; Gold Strike Tunica sold in Feb 2023 (subsequent event).

nodes.summary:

An amended and restated master lease with VICI was executed (see Notes 4, 11, 18).

nodes.title: The Mirage transaction.
nodes.heading: 1.5 The Mirage transaction.
nodes.start_phrase: On December 19, 2022, the Company completed the sale of the operations of The Mirage to an affiliate of Seminole Hard Rock Entertainment, Inc. (“Hard Rock”).
nodes.summary:
- Dispositions: 
  - Sold the operations of The Mirage to an affiliate of Seminole Hard Rock Entertainment, Inc. on December 19, 2022.
  - Sold the operations of Gold Strike Tunica to CNE Gaming Holdings, LLC (a Cherokee Nation Businesses subsidiary) on February 15, 2023.
- CityCenter:
  - Acquired the remaining 50% interest in CityCenter Holdings, LLC from Infinity World on September 27, 2021 (CityCenter includes Aria and Vdara).
  - Sold the real estate of Aria (including Vdara) to Blackstone-managed funds for $3.89 billion on September 28, 2021 and entered into a leaseback.
- MGM Grand Las Vegas and Mandalay Bay:
  - On February 14, 2020, contributed the real estate of MGM Grand Las Vegas and Mandalay Bay to the newly formed VICI BREIT Venture.
  - Received $4.6 billion total consideration: $2.5 billion cash, $1.3 billion of debt assumed by the venture, and a 50.1% equity interest in the venture; also received ~3 million MGP OP units (5% of the venture’s equity value).
  - Recognized a $1.7 billion net gain on the MGM Grand Las Vegas real estate sale and a $252 million net loss on the Mandalay Bay real estate sale, both within “Gain on REIT transactions, net.”
  - Provided a shortfall guarantee on the venture’s indebtedness; BREIT purchased ~5 million MGP Class A shares for $150 million at closing.
  - Modified the MGP master lease to remove Mandalay Bay and entered into a new lease with the venture for Mandalay Bay and MGM Grand Las Vegas.
- Macau gaming concessions:
  - MGM Grand Paradise acquired a gaming subconcession from SJM in 2005; term extended to June 26, 2022, then to December 31, 2022 (MOP 47 million payment).
  - A new Macau gaming law (June 2022) ended subconcessions and allows up to six concessions for up to 10 years (possible 3-year exceptional extension), preceding a public tender for new concessions.

nodes.title: MGM Grand Las Vegas and Mandalay Bay transaction.
nodes.heading: 1.8 MGM Grand Las Vegas and Mandalay Bay transaction.
nodes.start_phrase: On February 14, 2020, the Company completed a series of transactions (collectively the “MGM Grand Las Vegas and Mandalay Bay transaction”) pursuant to which the real estate assets of MGM Grand Las Vegas and Mandalay Bay (including Mandalay Place) were contributed to the newly formed VICI BREIT Venture.

- MGM Grand Las Vegas and Mandalay Bay transaction (February 14, 2020): Contributed the real estate of MGM Grand Las Vegas and Mandalay Bay (including Mandalay Place) to the VICI BREIT Venture. Received $4.6 billion in total consideration ($2.5 billion cash, $1.3 billion debt assumed, and a 50.1% equity interest in the venture); additionally received ~3 million MGP OP units representing 5% of the venture’s equity value. Recognized a $1.7 billion gain on the MGM Grand Las Vegas real estate sale and a $252 million loss on the Mandalay Bay real estate sale, both within “Gain on REIT transactions, net.” Provided a shortfall guarantee on the venture’s indebtedness (see Note 12). BREIT purchased ~5 million MGP Class A shares for $150 million at closing. The master lease with MGP was modified to remove Mandalay Bay, and a new lease was entered for Mandalay Bay and MGM Grand Las Vegas with a Company subsidiary (see Note 11).
- Macau operations and regulation: Outlines MGM Grand Paradise’s gaming subconcession history—acquired in 2005 from SJM Resorts S.A., extended in 2019 to June 26, 2022, and further extended to December 31, 2022 with a MOP 47 million (~$6 million) payment (see Note 7). Summarizes the 2022 Macau gaming law reform that discontinued subconcessions and established up to six concessions with terms up to 10 years (plus a possible 3-year extension under exceptional circumstances), preceding the public tender process.

nodes.title: Principles of consolidation.
nodes.heading: 2.1 Principles of consolidation.
nodes.start_phrase: The Company evaluates entities for which control is achieved through means other than voting rights to determine if it is the primary beneficiary of a variable interest entity (“VIE”).

- Basis of presentation and significant accounting policies:

nodes.title: Reclassifications.

nodes.summary:

- Outlines consolidation policy for non-VIEs: consolidate 100%-owned entities; for less-than-100% ownership, consolidate under the voting interest model when the Company has a controlling financial interest (e.g., MGM China), recording noncontrolling interests and eliminating intercompany balances.
- Explains equity method accounting when the Company has significant influence but not control (e.g., BetMGM with joint control and substantive participating rights under ASC 810), and ASC 321 accounting when it lacks significant influence (e.g., VICI OP).
- Notes certain reclassifications made to conform prior period presentation.
- Emphasizes management’s use of estimates under U.S. GAAP, affecting reported assets, liabilities, contingencies, revenues, and expenses; actual results may differ.

nodes.title: Management’s use of estimates.
nodes.heading: 2.3 Management’s use of estimates.
nodes.start_phrase: The consolidated financial statements have been prepared in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America.
nodes.summary:
- Bellagio BREIT Venture: A variable interest entity (VIE) 5% owned by the Company and 95% by BREIT. The Company is not the primary beneficiary because BREIT, as managing member, controls significant activities; therefore, the venture is not consolidated. The Company’s maximum loss exposure equals its $56 million investment at December 31, 2022, plus an immaterial debt guarantee (see Note 12).

- Consolidation policy: 
  - Consolidate entities that are not VIEs when 100% owned, or under the voting interest model when the Company has a controlling financial interest (e.g., MGM China), with noncontrolling interests recognized and intercompany items eliminated.
  - Use the equity method when the Company has significant influence but not control (e.g., BetMGM with joint control via substantive participating rights under ASC 810).
  - Account for investments without significant influence under ASC 321 (e.g., VICI OP).

- Reclassifications: Certain prior-period reclassifications made for consistency.

- Use of estimates: Financial statements prepared under U.S. GAAP require estimates affecting reported assets, liabilities, revenues, expenses, and contingencies; actual results may differ.

- Fair value measurements: Applied to long-lived assets, investments, business combinations (assets acquired/liabilities assumed), goodwill/intangibles, and certain financial instruments. Fair value follows a hierarchy:
  - Level 1: Equity investments recorded at fair value.
  - Level 2: Long-term debt fair value disclosures (see Note 9); also used for some debt investments.
  - Levels 1–3: Used in acquisition accounting (see Note 4).

- Equity investments: 
  - Measured at fair value using quoted prices when elected under ASC 825 (e.g., LeoVegas pre-consolidation) or under ASC 321 with readily determinable values (e.g., VICI OP).
  - Fair values were $461 million (2022) and $66 million (2021), presented in Other long-term assets, net.
  - Gains/losses recorded in Other, net: $10 million gain (2022) and $28 million gain (2021).

- Debt investments: Classified as trading securities at fair value with gains/losses in Other, net; classified as cash equivalents if criteria met, otherwise as short-term investments within Prepaid expenses and other.

nodes.title: Fair value measurements.

nodes.summary:
- Bellagio BREIT Venture: Company owns 5% (BREIT owns 95%); classified as a VIE because equity holders lack power to direct key activities. Company is not the primary beneficiary since BREIT, as managing member, has decision-making power; therefore, the venture is not consolidated. Maximum loss exposure equals the $56 million carrying value at December 31, 2022 plus an immaterial debt guarantee (see Note 12).
- Consolidation policy: 
  - Non-VIEs: consolidate 100% owned entities; for less-than-100% ownership, consolidate under the voting interest model when the Company has a controlling financial interest (e.g., MGM China), with noncontrolling interests recorded and intercompany activity eliminated.
  - Equity method: used when the Company has significant influence but not control (e.g., BetMGM, due to joint control via substantive participating rights under ASC 810).

- Reclassifications: certain prior period amounts reclassified to conform to current presentation.

- Fair value measurements: applied to long-lived assets, unconsolidated investments, acquisitions (assets/liabilities), goodwill/intangibles, and certain financial instruments. Fair value follows a hierarchy:
  - Level 1: quoted prices in active markets (used for certain equity investments; also part of debt investments and acquisition accounting).
  - Level 2: observable market data for identical/comparable instruments (used for long-term debt disclosures; also part of debt investments and acquisition accounting).

- Equity investments:

- Debt investments:
