- Cash and cash equivalents comprise cash, investments, and highly liquid interest‑bearing instruments with original maturities of 90 days or less; book overdrafts from cash management are recorded in Accounts and construction payable.
- Restricted cash: prior escrow for a reverse termination fee related to The Cosmopolitan acquisition was classified as Restricted Cash at December 31, 2021; MGM China’s $124 million pledged cash securing bank guarantees is restricted and classified in Other long‑term assets, net. Amounts reconcile to “Cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash” on the statements of cash flows for the respective periods.
- Accounts receivable and credit risk: primary concentration in casino receivables (approximately 52% of gross receivables in 2022 and 53% in 2021). Receivables are non‑interest bearing, recorded at cost, written off when uncollectible, with recoveries recognized when received. An allowance is maintained based on specific account reviews, historical experience, and current/expected conditions; no unreserved significant concentrations at year‑end 2022.
- Inventories: primarily food and beverage, retail merchandise, and operating supplies; carried at lower of cost or net realizable value. Cost determined by average cost for food, beverage, and operating supplies; retail merchandise uses the cost method.
- Property and equipment: recorded at cost, with assets from business combinations recognized at fair value on acquisition; gains/losses on disposals recognized in earnings; maintenance costs expensed as incurred.

nodes.title: Property and equipment.
nodes.heading: 2.11 Property and equipment.
nodes.start_phrase: Property and equipment are stated at cost.
nodes.summary:
- Fair value disclosures at December 31, 2022 (in thousands), including Level 1 and Level 2 classifications:
  - Cash and cash equivalents: Money market funds (Level 1 $12,009), commercial paper and CDs (Level 2 $5,992), total $18,001.
  - Short-term investments: U.S. government securities (Level 1 $56,835), U.S. agency securities (Level 2 $9,530), commercial paper and CDs (Level 2 $4,466), corporate bonds (Level 2 $213,875), total $284,706.
  - Total debt investments: $302,707.
- Cash and cash equivalents policy: highly liquid instruments with maturities of 90 days or less; book overdrafts recorded in Accounts and construction payable.
- Restricted cash: escrow related to The Cosmopolitan acquisition (2021) and MGM China pledged cash of $124 million securing bank guarantees; reconciliation of restricted cash with cash flow presentation for 2021 and 2022.
- Accounts receivable and credit risk:
  - Casino receivables comprise ~52% (2022) and 53% (2021) of gross receivables.
  - Non-interest bearing; write-off and recovery practices.
  - Loss reserve methodology based on specific reviews, historical experience, and current/expected conditions; no unreserved significant concentrations as of December 31, 2022.
- Inventories: primarily F&B, retail merchandise, and operating supplies; stated at lower of cost or net realizable value; average cost for F&B and supplies; cost method for retail.
- Property and equipment:
  - Stated at cost; assets from business combinations recorded at fair value at acquisition; maintenance expensed; gains/losses on disposition recognized in income.
  - Depreciation (straight-line): buildings/improvements 15–40 yrs; land improvements 10–20 yrs; furniture/fixtures 3–20 yrs; equipment 3–15 yrs.
  - Impairment:
    - Held for sale: lower of carrying value or fair value less costs to sell.
    - Held and used: test on indicators; compare undiscounted cash flows to carrying value; if impaired, measure fair value typically via discounted cash flow.
- Macau gaming assets (MGM Cotai and MGM Macau):
  - Gaming subconcession expired Dec 31, 2022; casino areas reverted to Macau government.
  - As of Jan 1, 2023, assets temporarily transferred back for concession term with annual payments.
  - Company continues to recognize and depreciate assets, assuming continued operation and economic benefits.
- Capitalized interest: interest on major development projects capitalized using specific debt or weighted average borrowing cost; ceases when substantially complete or if activity is suspended beyond a brief period.
- Investments in and advances to unconsolidated affiliates:
  - Accounted for under the equity method; carrying value adjusted for share of earnings/losses, basis difference amortization, contributions/distributions.
  - Distributions exceeding equity earnings treated as return of investment and investing cash inflows.
  - Classification of related results as operating or non-operating based on alignment with core operations.
  - Impairment assessment when indicators arise; fair value estimated via DCF and market multiples; evaluate other-than-temporary nature.
- Goodwill and other intangible assets: goodwill from business combinations; indefinite-lived intangibles include trademarks and certain gaming licenses; required annual (and interim upon triggering events) impairment reviews.

nodes.title: Capitalized interest.
nodes.heading: 2.12 Capitalized interest.
nodes.start_phrase: The interest cost associated with major development and construction projects is capitalized and included in the cost of the project.
nodes.summary:
- Depreciation policy: Straight-line over estimated useful lives—Buildings and improvements (15–40 years), Land improvements (10–20 years), Furniture and fixtures (3–20 years), Equipment (3–15 years).
- Long-lived asset impairment:
  - Held for sale: Recognized at lower of carrying value or fair value less costs to sell, based on comparable sales, offers, or discounted cash flows; classification requires a committed plan to sell and active marketing at a reasonable price.
  - Held and used: Test when indicators arise by comparing undiscounted future cash flows of the asset group to carrying value; if not recoverable, record impairment to fair value (typically via discounted cash flow). Development assets’ cash flows include remaining construction costs. All impairments recorded in operating expenses.
- Macau gaming assets: Upon subconcession expiration (Dec 31, 2022), casino areas at MGM Cotai and MGM Macau reverted to the Macau government; effective Jan 1, 2023, assets temporarily transferred back for the concession term with annual payments. Company continues to recognize these assets in Property and equipment and depreciate over remaining lives, as it operates them, receives substantially all benefits, bears risks, and assumes success in obtaining a new concession.
- Capitalized interest: Interest on major development/construction capitalized; if no project-specific debt, use weighted average cost of outstanding borrowings. Capitalization ceases when substantially complete or if development is suspended beyond a brief period.
- Investments in unconsolidated affiliates: Accounted for under the equity method; carrying value adjusted for share of earnings/losses, basis difference amortization, contributions/distributions. Distributions exceeding equity earnings treated as return of investment and shown as investing cash inflows. Operating results and related gains/impairments classified in operating income; non-operating items classified in non-operating income/loss.
- Impairment of unconsolidated affiliates: Test when indicators exist; determine other-than-temporary impairment by comparing estimated fair value (via discounted cash flow and market multiples from peers) to carrying value, considering intent/ability to hold.
- Goodwill and indefinite-lived intangibles (e.g., trademarks and certain gaming licenses): Subject to at least annual impairment review and interim testing upon triggering events.

nodes.title: Investments in and advances to unconsolidated affiliates.
nodes.heading: 2.13 Investments in and advances to unconsolidated affiliates.
nodes.start_phrase: The Company has investments in unconsolidated affiliates accounted for under the equity method.
nodes.summary:
- Depreciation policy for property and equipment on a straight-line basis with estimated useful lives: buildings and improvements (15–40 years), land improvements (10–20 years), furniture and fixtures (3–20 years), and equipment (3–15 years).
- Long-lived asset impairment:
  - Held for sale: classification requires a committed plan to sell at a reasonable price and active marketing; assets measured at the lower of carrying value or fair value less costs to sell based on comparable sales, offers, or discounted cash flows.
  - Held and used: impairment review when indicators exist; compare undiscounted future cash flows of the asset group to carrying value; if not exceeded, record impairment to fair value, typically via discounted cash flow; include remaining construction costs for in-development assets. All impairments recorded as operating expenses.
- Macau gaming assets: upon subconcession expiry (Dec 31, 2022), casino areas of MGM Cotai and MGM Macau reverted to the Macau government; effective Jan 1, 2023, assets temporarily transferred back to MGM Grand Paradise for the concession term with annual payments. The Company continues to recognize these assets within Property and equipment and depreciates them over remaining useful lives, as it operates them, obtains substantially all economic benefits, and bears related risks, assuming success in securing a new concession after the current term.
- Capitalized interest: interest on major development/construction projects is capitalized; if no project-specific debt, capitalization uses the weighted average cost of outstanding borrowings; capitalization stops when the project is substantially complete or when development is suspended for more than a brief period.
- Investments in and advances to unconsolidated affiliates: accounted for under the equity method; carrying value adjusted for share of earnings/losses, basis difference amortization, and capital contributions/distributions. Distributions exceeding equity method earnings are treated as returns of investment and shown as investing cash inflows. Operating components (income/losses, gains/impairments) related to these investments are classified as operating; non-operating components are classified as non-operating.
- Impairment of investments in unconsolidated affiliates: tested upon triggering events; compare estimated fair value to carrying value; assess other-than-temporary nature considering intent and ability to retain the investment. Fair value estimated using discounted cash flows with terminal capitalization rates and market multiples from peers.
- Goodwill and other intangible assets: goodwill equals purchase price over fair value of net assets acquired; indefinite-lived intangibles include trademarks and certain gaming licenses; both are reviewed for impairment at least annually and more frequently if warranted.

nodes.title: Goodwill and other intangible assets.
nodes.heading: 2.14 Goodwill and other intangible assets.
nodes.start_phrase: Goodwill represents the excess of purchase price over fair market value of net assets acquired in business combinations.
nodes.summary:
- Property and equipment: Straight-line depreciation over estimated useful lives—buildings and improvements (15–40 years), land improvements (10–20 years), furniture and fixtures (3–20 years), equipment (3–15 years).
- Long-lived asset impairment: 
  - Held for sale—recognized at lower of carrying value or fair value less costs to sell; criteria include approved plan, reasonable price, active marketing.
  - Held and used—test when indicators exist; compare undiscounted cash flows to carrying value; if not recoverable, record impairment to fair value (typically via discounted cash flow). Construction-in-progress cash flows include remaining build costs. Impairments recorded in operating expenses.
- Macau gaming assets: Upon subconcession expiration (Dec 31, 2022), casino areas of MGM Cotai and MGM Macau reverted to the Macau government and were temporarily transferred back to MGM Grand Paradise from Jan 1, 2023 for annual payments. Company continues to recognize these assets in Property and equipment and depreciate over remaining useful lives, as it operates them, receives benefits, bears risks, and assumes renewal success.
- Capitalized interest: Capitalize interest on major development/construction, using project-specific debt or weighted average borrowings; cease when substantially complete or activity pauses beyond a brief period.
- Investments in unconsolidated affiliates: Equity method accounting with adjustments for share of earnings/losses, basis difference amortization, contributions/distributions. Excess distributions treated as return of investment (investing cash inflow). Operating vs non-operating classification reflects core business nature. Impairment testing when indicators arise using fair value from DCF and market multiples; assess other-than-temporary nature considering intent and ability to hold.
- Goodwill and other intangibles:
  - Goodwill and indefinite-lived intangibles (trademarks, certain gaming licenses) tested at least annually (Q4) and on triggering events; no material impairments in 2022, 2021, 2020.
  - Optional qualitative “step zero” assessment considers macro, industry, performance, entity events, asset composition, and prior excess fair value; proceed to quantitative test if more likely than not impaired.
  - Quantitative tests: Goodwill—DCF plus market multiples at reporting unit level; record impairment if fair value < carrying value. Indefinite-lived intangibles—licenses via DCF; trademarks via relief-from-royalty; record impairment if fair value < carrying amount.
  - Finite-lived intangibles (e.g., gaming subconcession, certain gaming rights, customer lists, technology) amortized straight-line; impairment test based on undiscounted cash flows vs carrying value.
- Note receivable: From 2019 sale of Circus Circus Las Vegas and adjacent land—secured note due 2024, face $163M, initial fair value $134M; interest 3% (years 1–2), 4% (years 3–4), 4.5% (year 5), effective rate 7.31%, secured by adjacent land; interest income recognized via effective interest method. Carrying value $167M (2022) and $155M (2021), recorded in Other long-term assets, net.
- Accounts payable: Accrued purchases of property and equipment within Accounts and construction payable of $80M (2022) and $59M (2021).
- Revenue recognition:
  - Revenue streams: casino wagers (net win), hotel rooms, food and beverage, entertainment, retail.
  - Casino: Transaction price is net win; marker discounts and MGM China commissions reduce casino revenue; portfolio approach by gaming day. Discretionary comps allocated from casino wager to goods/services at standalone selling price (SSP); third-party comps recorded as operating expense. Loyalty incentives: allocate portion of net win to incentives at SSP (less breakage), defer and recognize when redeemed.

nodes.title: Note receivable.
nodes.heading: 2.15 Note receivable.
nodes.start_phrase: In connection with the sale of Circus Circus Las Vegas and the adjacent land in December 2019, the Company received a secured note due in 2024 with a face value of $163 million and fair value of $134 million.
nodes.summary:
- Impairment testing policies:
  - Annual goodwill and indefinite-lived intangible impairment tests performed in Q4; no material impairments in 2020–2022.
  - Qualitative “step zero” option applied considering macro/industry factors, performance, entity events, changes in net asset composition, prior fair value cushion, and time since last quantitative test; proceeds to quantitative testing if more likely than not impaired.
  - Quantitative methods: goodwill tested using DCF with market discount/terminal rates and market multiples; license rights via DCF; trademarks via relief-from-royalty; impairments recognized when fair value < carrying amount.
- Finite-lived intangible assets:
  - Assets include MGM Grand Paradise’s gaming subconcession, other gaming rights where renewal is uncertain, customer lists, and technology.
  - Amortized straight-line over useful lives; recoverability tested using undiscounted cash flows; impairment recorded if not recoverable.
- Note receivable from Circus Circus Las Vegas sale (Dec 2019):
  - Secured note due 2024; face value $163m, initial fair value $134m; interest 3% (years 1–2), 4% (years 3–4), 4.5% (year 5); effective rate 7.31%; collateralized by adjacent land.
  - Interest recognized via effective interest method; carrying value $167m (2022) and $155m (2021), classified in Other long-term assets, net.
- Accounts payable:
  - Accrued purchases of property and equipment of $80m (2022) and $59m (2021) within Accounts and construction payable.
- Revenue recognition:
  - Revenue streams include casino, hotel rooms, food and beverage, entertainment, and retail.
  - Casino revenue recognized as net win; discounts on markers and commissions to MGM China gaming promoters/VIP players reduce casino revenue.
  - Casino wagers accounted for on a portfolio basis.
  - For discretionary comps provided to incentivize gaming, allocates portion of casino transaction price to goods/services at SSP; third-party comps recorded as operating expense.
  - Loyalty program incentives: allocate portion of net win at SSP (less breakage), defer and recognize upon redemption.

nodes.title: Accounts payable.
nodes.heading: 2.16 Accounts payable.
nodes.start_phrase: As of December 31, 2022 and 2021, the Company had accrued $80 million and $59 million, respectively, for purchases of property and equipment within “Accounts and construction payable” on the consolidated balance sheets.
nodes.summary:
- Annual impairment testing: Conducted in Q4 each year; no material impairments for goodwill or indefinite-lived intangibles in 2020–2022. Allows a qualitative “step zero” assessment considering macro/industry factors, performance, entity events, asset composition, and prior fair value cushions; proceeds to quantitative testing if likely fair value is below carrying value.
- Quantitative impairment methods: Goodwill tested via discounted cash flow (DCF) and market approach using peer multiples; impairment recorded if reporting unit fair value is below carrying value. Indefinite-lived intangibles: license rights via DCF; trademarks via relief-from-royalty; impairment recognized if fair value is below carrying amount.
- Finite-lived intangible assets: Examples include MGM Grand Paradise’s gaming subconcession, certain gaming rights with uncertain renewals, customer lists, and technology; amortized straight-line over useful lives. Impairment testing triggered by indicators; recoverability assessed using undiscounted cash flows at the asset group level; impair if not recoverable.
- Note receivable: From the 2019 sale of Circus Circus Las Vegas—secured note due 2024, face value $163m, initial fair value $134m; stated interest 3% (years 1–2), 4% (years 3–4), 4.5% (year 5); effective rate 7.31%; secured by adjacent land. Interest recognized using the effective interest method. Carrying value $167m (Dec 31, 2022) and $155m (Dec 31, 2021), reported in Other long-term assets, net.
- Accounts payable: Accrued purchases of property and equipment of $80m (2022) and $59m (2021) within Accounts and construction payable.
- Revenue recognition: Covers casino, hotel, food and beverage, entertainment, and retail. Casino revenue recognized as net win; marker discounts and MGM China commissions reduce casino revenue. Portfolio approach by gaming day. For discretionary comps, allocates transaction price based on standalone selling price (SSP); third-party comps recorded as operating expense. Loyalty program incentives: allocate portion of net win at SSP less estimated breakage, defer, and recognize upon redemption.

nodes.title: Revenue recognition.
nodes.heading: 2.17 Revenue recognition.
nodes.start_phrase: The Company’s revenue from contracts with customers consists of casino wagers transactions, hotel room sales, food and beverage transactions, entertainment shows, and retail transactions.
nodes.summary:
- Impairment testing policies:
  - Annual impairment tests for goodwill and indefinite-lived intangibles in Q4; no material impairments in 2020–2022.
  - Qualitative “step zero” assessment factors: macroeconomic and industry conditions, performance forecasts, entity-specific events, changes in reporting unit net assets, prior quantitative headroom, and time since last test; proceed to quantitative testing if more-likely-than-not fair value is below carrying amount.
  - Quantitative methods: for goodwill, discounted cash flow (DCF) and market approach using peer multiples; for license rights, DCF; for trademarks, relief-from-royalty; recognize impairment if fair value < carrying value.

- Finite-lived intangible assets:
  - Assets (e.g., MGM Grand Paradise gaming subconcession, certain gaming rights, customer lists, technology) amortized straight-line over estimated useful lives.
  - Impairment testing based on recoverability using undiscounted cash flows at the asset group level; record impairment if undiscounted cash flows < carrying amount.

- Note receivable (Circus Circus Las Vegas sale, Dec 2019):
  - Secured note due 2024; face $163 million; initial fair value $134 million.
  - Stated interest: 3% (years 1–2), 4% (years 3–4), 4.5% (year 5); effective interest rate 7.31%.
  - Interest income recognized via effective interest method; carrying value $167 million (2022) and $155 million (2021), recorded in Other long-term assets, net.

- Accounts payable:
  - Accrued purchases of property and equipment: $80 million (2022) and $59 million (2021) in Accounts and construction payable.

- Revenue recognition:
  - Revenue streams: casino wagers (net win), hotel rooms, food & beverage, entertainment, retail.
  - Casino revenue recognized on a portfolio basis as net win; marker discounts and Macau commissions reduce casino revenue.
  - Allocation of casino transaction price to discretionary comps and loyalty incentives based on standalone selling price (SSP); loyalty incentives deferred (net of breakage) and recognized upon redemption in the providing department; third-party redemptions reduce loyalty liability with payments to the third party.
  - Rooms, F&B, retail recognized when goods/services are transferred; sales/usage taxes excluded.
  - Principal vs agent assessments for certain entertainment shows and BetMGM online sports betting/iGaming (agent in some jurisdictions).
  - Multi-element packages allocated by relative SSP based on standalone pricing.

- Contract and contract-related liabilities:
  - Types: outstanding chip liability, loyalty program obligations, customer advances and other (including casino front money and prepayments).
  - Generally recognized as revenue within one year; recorded in Other accrued liabilities.
  - Balances and changes (in thousands): 
    - Outstanding chips: $185,669 (2022) vs $176,219 (2021); change +$9,450.
    - Loyalty: $183,602 (2022) vs $144,465 (2021); change +$39,137.
    - Customer advances/other: $816,376 (2022) vs $640,001 (2021); change +$176,375.
  - 2022 balances exclude liabilities related to assets held for sale.

- Reimbursed costs:
  - Recognized as revenue when incurred; primarily related to CityCenter management (agreement terminated Sept 2021).

- Revenue disaggregation:
  - Presented by type (casino, room, F&B, entertainment/retail/other) and geography in a separate note.

- Lease accounting:
  - Identification of leases based on control of identified assets; classification as operating or finance for terms >12 months.
  - Recognition of right-of-use assets and lease liabilities at commencement based on present value of future lease payments; ROU assets include prepaid lease amounts (policy discussion continues beyond excerpt).

nodes.title: Contract and Contract-Related Liabilities.
nodes.heading: 2.18 Contract and Contract-Related Liabilities.
nodes.start_phrase: There may be a difference between the timing of cash receipts from the customer and the recognition of revenue, resulting in a contract or contract-related liability.
nodes.summary:
- Revenue recognition for casino-related transactions: revenue allocated to other goods/services included in wagers, with the residual recorded as casino revenue; loyalty incentives redeemed at third-party outlets reduce loyalty liabilities, and any discount retained is recorded as other revenue.
- Rooms, food and beverage, and retail: transaction price is the net amount collected; revenue recognized over the hotel stay or upon delivery for F&B/retail; sales and usage-based taxes excluded; in certain arrangements (e.g., some entertainment shows and BetMGM in some jurisdictions) the Company acts as an agent rather than principal.
- Bundled offerings (e.g., packages combining rooms, F&B, entertainment, convention services): revenue allocated to each performance obligation based on relative standalone selling prices (SSP), primarily using observable separate selling prices.
- Contract and contract-related liabilities: three primary types—outstanding chip liability (chips held by customers), loyalty program obligations (deferred revenue for earned incentives), and customer advances and other (casino front money, advance ticket sales, room/convention deposits, unpaid wagers). These are generally recognized as revenue within one year and reported in Other accrued liabilities.
- Summary of liability activity: table provided for 2021 and 2022 showing beginning balances, ending balances, and changes for the three liability categories; 2022 balances exclude liabilities related to assets held for sale (see Note 4).
- Reimbursed costs: amounts reimbursed under management services recognized as revenue when costs are incurred; primarily related to CityCenter management prior to its acquisition in September 2021.
- Revenue by source: disaggregated by type (casino, room, F&B, entertainment/retail/other) and geography as referenced in Note 17.
- Lease accounting: identification of leases based on control of an identified asset; classification as operating or finance for leases over 12 months; recognition of right-of-use assets and lease liabilities at commencement based on the present value of future minimum lease payments; initial ROU asset measurement includes prepaid lease amounts (discussion continues beyond excerpt).

nodes.title: Reimbursed cost.
nodes.heading: 2.19 Reimbursed cost.
nodes.start_phrase: Costs reimbursed pursuant to management services are recognized as revenue in the period it incurs the costs as this reflects when the Company performs its related performance obligation and is entitled to reimbursement.
nodes.summary:
- Revenue recognition for casino-related transactions: loyalty incentives are allocated to the department providing the related goods/services; redemptions at third-party outlets reduce loyalty liabilities with any discount recognized as other revenue. After allocating to bundled goods/services, the residual is recorded as casino revenue.
- Rooms, food & beverage, and retail revenue: transaction price is the net amount collected and is recognized when goods/services are transferred (over the hotel stay or upon delivery). Sales and usage taxes are excluded. The Company sometimes acts as an agent (e.g., certain entertainment shows and, in some jurisdictions, BetMGM online sports betting and iGaming), recognizing revenue accordingly.
- Multiple-element arrangements (e.g., packages bundling rooms with food, beverage, or entertainment): revenue is allocated to each component based on relative standalone selling prices (SSP), primarily determined from observable separate sales.
- Contract and contract-related liabilities: defined as (1) outstanding chip liability, (2) loyalty program obligations (deferred revenue for incentives), and (3) customer advances and other (casino front money and advance payments for tickets, rooms, convention space, or unpaid wagers). These are generally recognized as revenue within one year and recorded in Other accrued liabilities.
- Summary of liabilities activity: table presents balances and changes for 2021–2022; balances increased year over year for chip liabilities, loyalty obligations, and customer advances. December 31, 2022 balances exclude liabilities related to assets held for sale (see Note 4).
- Reimbursed costs: costs incurred under management services are recognized as revenue when incurred; primarily related to CityCenter management (agreement terminated upon CityCenter acquisition in September 2021).
- Revenue disaggregation: revenues are presented by source (casino, room, food and beverage, entertainment/retail/other) and by geographic region (see Note 17).
- Lease accounting: assessment of whether an arrangement contains a lease based on identified assets and control over their use; classification as operating or finance for terms over 12 months. At commencement, recognize right-of-use assets and lease liabilities measured at the present value of future minimum lease payments; initial ROU asset includes prepaid lease amounts.

nodes.title: Revenue by source.
nodes.heading: 2.20 Revenue by source.
nodes.start_phrase: The Company presents the revenue earned disaggregated by the type or nature of the good or service (casino, room, food and beverage, and entertainment, retail and other) and by relevant geographic region within Note 17.
nodes.summary:
- Revenue recognition policies for casino wager transactions, including allocating consideration to other goods/services in the transaction and recording the residual as casino revenue.
- Accounting for loyalty programs, including treatment of redemptions at third-party outlets (deducted from loyalty liability, payments to third parties, discounts recognized as other revenue).
- Recognition of room, food and beverage, and retail revenues at the net transaction price when services are provided (over the hotel stay or upon delivery), with sales and usage-based taxes excluded.
- Principal vs. agent considerations, noting agent treatment for certain entertainment shows and, in some jurisdictions, arrangements with BetMGM for online sports betting and iGaming.
- Revenue allocation for bundled or multi-element arrangements (e.g., packages combining hotel, food, beverage, entertainment, convention services) based on relative standalone selling prices (SSP), with SSP determined from separate sales to similar customers.
- Contract and contract-related liabilities:
  - Types: outstanding chip liability, loyalty program obligations (deferred revenue for incentives), and customer advances/other (casino front money, advance payments for rooms, convention space, tickets, unpaid wagers).
  - Generally recognized as revenue within one year; recorded in Other accrued liabilities.
  - A table summarizes 2021–2022 beginning and ending balances and changes; 2022 excludes liabilities related to assets held for sale (referenced to Note 4).
- Reimbursed costs under management services recognized as revenue when incurred; primarily related to CityCenter management (agreement terminated upon CityCenter acquisition in September 2021).
- Disclosure that revenue is disaggregated by source (casino, room, food and beverage, entertainment/retail/other) and by geography (referenced to Note 17).
- Lease accounting policy: identifying whether arrangements contain a lease based on control of an identified asset; classifying leases >12 months as operating or finance; recognizing right-of-use assets and lease liabilities at commencement based on the present value of future minimum lease payments, with initial ROU measurement including prepaid lease amounts (policy text continues beyond excerpt).

nodes.title: Leases.
nodes.heading: 2.21 Leases.
nodes.start_phrase: The Company determines if an arrangement is or contains a lease at inception or modification of the arrangement.
nodes.summary:
- Revenue recognition:
  - Loyalty incentives redeemed at third-party outlets reduce loyalty liabilities; related third-party payments are made and any discounts are recorded as other revenue.
  - For casino wager transactions, revenue for other goods/services is allocated first; the residual is recorded as casino revenue.
  - Rooms, food & beverage, and retail revenue are recognized at transfer of goods/services (over hotel stay or upon delivery); sales and usage-based taxes excluded.
  - In certain arrangements (some entertainment shows and, in some jurisdictions, BetMGM online sports betting and iGaming), the Company acts as an agent rather than principal.
  - Bundled packages (e.g., room with food, beverage, entertainment, convention services) use relative standalone selling price (SSP) based on similar standalone sales.

- Contract and contract-related liabilities:
  - Three main types: outstanding chip liability, loyalty program obligations, and customer advances/other (including casino front money and advance payments for tickets, rooms, and convention space or unpaid wagers).
  - Typically recognized as revenue within one year and recorded in Other accrued liabilities.
  - Table shows year-over-year increases in 2022 vs. 2021 for all three categories; balances at December 31, 2022: chips $185.7m, loyalty $183.6m, advances/other $816.4m (excludes assets held for sale).

- Reimbursed costs:
  - Costs reimbursed under management services recognized as revenue when incurred; primarily tied to CityCenter management (terminated upon its acquisition in Sept 2021).

- Revenue disaggregation:
  - Presented by source (casino, room, food & beverage, entertainment/retail/other) and geography in a separate note.

- Lease accounting:
  - Lease identification and control assessed at inception/modification; leases >12 months classified as operating or finance.
  - Right-of-use assets and lease liabilities measured at present value of lease payments; use implicit rate when available, otherwise incremental borrowing rate.
  - Renewal options included only when reasonably certain; operating lease expense straight-line; finance leases: ROU depreciation plus interest accretion.
  - As lessor, lease revenues classified by tenant activity; disclosed amounts for 2022/2021/2020 within food & beverage and entertainment/retail/other; hotel room rentals reported as rooms revenue.

- Advertising:
  - Expensed as incurred; disclosed annual amounts for 2022, 2021, and 2020.

- Corporate expense:
  - Unallocated payroll, professional fees, other corporate costs, and expenses for evaluating/pursuing new business opportunities.

- Preopening and start-up:
  - Expensed as incurred; include payroll, outside services, advertising, and other start-up costs.

- Property transactions, net:
  - Includes write-downs/impairments, demolition costs, and gains/losses on asset sales; further detail provided elsewhere.

- Redeemable noncontrolling interests (MGM National Harbor):
  - Non-voting interests receive preferred distributions based on a percentage of annual net gaming revenue; accrued quarterly and paid 90 days after year-end.
  - Holders have put rights; classified in mezzanine equity as redemption not solely within Company control.
  - Initially recorded at fair value; subsequently adjusted to maximum redemption value (not below initial), with changes recorded in additional paid-in capital; preferred distribution accruals impact NCI in net income.

- Income per share:
  - Basic and diluted EPS reconciliations; diluted EPS reflects effects of redeemable NCI and potential dilution from stock-based awards.

nodes.title: Advertising.
nodes.heading: 2.22 Advertising.
nodes.start_phrase: The Company expenses advertising costs as incurred.
nodes.summary:
- Lease accounting as lessee: use rate implicit in the lease when available (e.g., certain triple-net leases); otherwise use incremental borrowing rate (e.g., ground subleases, equipment). nodes.title: ACQUISITIONS AND DIVESTITURES
nodes.heading: NOTE 4 — ACQUISITIONS AND DIVESTITURES
nodes.start_phrase: On May 2, 2022, the Company commenced a public offer to the shareholders of LeoVegas to tender 100% of the shares at a price of SEK 61 in cash per share.

nodes.title: LeoVegas acquisition.
nodes.heading: 4.1 LeoVegas acquisition.
nodes.start_phrase: On May 2, 2022, the Company commenced a public offer to the shareholders of LeoVegas to tender 100% of the shares at a price of SEK 61 in cash per share.
nodes.summary:

  - Public tender offer launched May 2, 2022 at SEK 61 per share; 65% acquired on Sept 7, 2022 and an additional 2% on Sept 22, 2022 for $370 million cash; 31% previously acquired in open-market purchases with a fair value of ~$172 million at consolidation; remaining shares (~$11 million at tender price) to be settled via squeeze-out.

  - Total fair value of acquired equity interests: ~$556 million (including cash settlement of equity awards).
  - Acquisition method applied; assets, liabilities, and noncontrolling interests recognized at fair value using Level 1, 2, and 3 inputs; intangible assets valued under the income approach.
  - Identified intangibles: trademarks (indefinite-lived), customer lists and technology (finite-lived, amortized over five years).

  - Purchase price allocation included cash, receivables, technology, trademarks, customer lists, goodwill, other assets, and assumed liabilities (including debt) and noncontrolling interests.
  - Post-acquisition results (Sept 7–Dec 31, 2022): $133 million net revenue; operating loss of $13 million; net loss of $15 million.
- The Cosmopolitan acquisition:
  - Acquired 100% of the equity interests in the operations on May 17, 2022 for $1.625 billion cash plus working capital adjustments (~$1.7 billion total).
  - Strategic rationale: expand customer base and enhance guest offerings in Las Vegas.
  - Acquisition method applied; assets and liabilities recognized at fair value using Level 1, 2, and 3 inputs.
  - Identified intangibles: trademarks (indefinite-lived) and customer lists (amortized over seven years); goodwill is referenced (text indicates tax deductibility but is truncated).

nodes.title: The Cosmopolitan acquisition.
nodes.heading: 4.2 The Cosmopolitan acquisition.
nodes.start_phrase: On May 17, 2022, the Company acquired 100% of the equity interests in the entities that own the operations of The Cosmopolitan for cash consideration of $1.625 billion plus working capital adjustments for a total purchase price of approximately $1.7 billion.
nodes.summary:
- Overview: The note details three significant transactions—acquisitions of LeoVegas (2022), The Cosmopolitan (2022), and the remaining 50% of CityCenter (2021)—including purchase considerations, fair value allocations, valuation methodologies, goodwill and intangible asset treatment, segment assignments, tax implications, and post-acquisition operating results. It also covers a related sale-leaseback of Aria and Vdara.

- LeoVegas acquisition:
  - Public tender offer launched May 2, 2022 at SEK 61 per share; 65% acquired Sept 7, 2022 and an additional 2% Sept 22, 2022 for $370 million cash. The Company had previously acquired 31% in open-market purchases (fair value ~$172 million). Remaining shares (~$11 million at tender price) to be settled via squeeze-out; no gain/loss on consolidation due to prior fair value accounting.
  - Strategic rationale: build a scaled global online gaming business.
  - Total fair value of acquired equity interests: $556 million (including cash settlement of equity awards).
  - Fair value allocation used Level 1, 2, and 3 inputs; intangible assets valued via income approach.
  - Intangibles: trademarks (indefinite-lived), customer lists and technology (finite, 5-year lives).
  - Goodwill: $288 million, not tax deductible; assigned to Corporate and other.
  - Key purchase price allocation items (in thousands): cash $93,407; technology $109,027; trademarks $144,374; customer lists $126,526; goodwill $288,367; liabilities including accounts payable and other current liabilities $(118,302)$ and debt $(104,439)$; noncontrolling interests $(2,861)$. Total $555,695.
  - Post-acquisition results (Sept 7–Dec 31, 2022): net revenue $133 million; operating loss $13 million; net loss $15 million.

- The Cosmopolitan acquisition:
  - Acquired 100% of operating entities on May 17, 2022 for $1.625 billion plus working capital adjustments; total purchase price approximately $1.690 billion.
  - Strategic rationale: expand customer base and enhance Las Vegas offerings.
  - Fair value allocation used Level 1, 2, and 3 inputs; intangibles valued via income approach.
  - Intangibles: trademarks (indefinite-lived) and customer lists (amortized over 7 years).
  - Goodwill: $1.289 billion, tax deductible; assigned to Las Vegas Strip Resorts segment; reflects profitability and expected synergies.
  - Significant purchase price allocation items (in thousands): cash $80,670; property and equipment $120,912; trademarks $130,000; customer lists $95,000; goodwill $1,289,468; operating lease ROU assets $3,404,894; operating lease liabilities $(3,401,815)$; accounts payable and other current liabilities $(145,136)$. Total $1,690,486.
  - Post-acquisition results (May 17–Dec 31, 2022): net revenue $783 million; operating income $117 million; net income $117 million.

- CityCenter acquisition and related divestiture:
  - On Sept 27, 2021, acquired Infinity World’s remaining 50% of CityCenter for $2.125 billion; prior 50% was equity method. Consolidated at 100% with fair value of equity interests at $4.25 billion; recognized a $1.6 billion gain on consolidation.
  - On Sept 28, 2021, sold Aria and Vdara real estate for $3.89 billion and entered into a leaseback; assets classified as held for sale at acquisition and measured at fair value less costs to sell.
  - Fair value allocation used Level 1, 2, and 3 inputs; indefinite-lived trademarks valued under relief-from-royalty method.
  - Goodwill assigned to Las Vegas Strip Resorts; primarily reflects profitability in excess of identifiable assets; approximately 50% tax deductible.

- Valuation and accounting themes across transactions:
  - Use of acquisition method; recognition of 100% of assets, liabilities, and (where applicable) noncontrolling interests at fair value.
  - Valuation inputs spanned Levels 1–3; income approach used for intangible assets.
  - Intangible asset mix included indefinite-lived trademarks and finite-lived customer lists/technology with specified amortization periods.
  - Goodwill assigned by segment with varying tax deductibility.
  - Post-acquisition operating results disclosed for the periods from acquisition dates through year-end 2022.

nodes.title: CityCenter acquisition.
nodes.heading: 4.3 CityCenter acquisition.
nodes.start_phrase: On September 27, 2021, the Company acquired Infinity World’s 50% ownership interest in CityCenter for cash consideration of $2.125 billion.
nodes.summary:
- The Cosmopolitan acquisition: Detailed purchase price allocation totaling $1.69 billion, including goodwill of $1.289 billion (assigned to the Las Vegas Strip Resorts segment), trademarks ($130 million), customer lists ($95 million), property and equipment, and significant operating lease right‑of‑use assets and liabilities. Post-acquisition results (May 17–Dec 31, 2022): $783 million net revenue; $117 million operating and net income.

- CityCenter acquisition: MGM purchased Infinity World’s 50% interest for $2.125 billion, obtaining full control and recognizing a $1.6 billion gain on consolidation based on a $4.25 billion fair value. Immediately sold Aria and Vdara real estate for $3.89 billion and leased them back; related assets were classified as held for sale and measured at fair value less costs to sell. Purchase price allocation included goodwill of $1.397 billion (assigned to Las Vegas Strip Resorts; about 50% tax deductible), trademarks ($180 million), real estate assets held for sale ($3.888 billion), and assumed debt ($1.729 billion). Partial-period 2021 results: $367 million net revenue; $69 million operating income; $68 million net income.

- Unaudited pro forma information (assuming CityCenter consolidation as of Jan 1, 2020 and The Cosmopolitan as of Jan 1, 2021; excluding the CityCenter consolidation gain and subsequent transactions): 2022 net revenues $13.55 billion; net income attributable to MGM $1.487 billion. 2021 net revenues $11.115 billion; net income attributable to MGM $186 million.

- The Mirage transaction: Sold operations to Hard Rock for $1.075 billion; amended VICI master lease to remove The Mirage and reduce annual cash rent by $90 million; recognized a $1.1 billion gain within property transactions. Sale not treated as discontinued operations.

- VICI transaction: VICI acquired MGM Growth Properties (MGP) in a stock-for-stock deal with a 1.366 exchange ratio. VICI OP redeemed most of MGM’s OP units for $4.4 billion cash; MGM retained ~1% VICI OP interest (~$375 million fair value). MGP Class B share held by MGM was canceled; MGM deconsolidated MGP and entered into an amended and restated master lease with VICI. The Mandalay Bay/MGM Grand Las Vegas lease with VICI BREIT Venture was unchanged.

nodes.title: MGM Grand Paradise gaming subconcession.
nodes.heading: 7.2 MGM Grand Paradise gaming subconcession.
nodes.start_phrase: As described in Note 1, the enactment of the new Macau gaming law in June 2022 provided for material changes to the legal form of gaming concessions in Macau, including discontinuing and prohibiting gaming subconcessions subsequent to their expiration, and also included material changes to the rights and obligations provided for under the new gaming concessions.
nodes.summary:
- Impact of Macau’s June 2022 gaming law: Subconcessions discontinued/prohibited post-expiration and rights/obligations under new concessions materially changed. The Company determined the former MGM Grand Paradise gaming subconcession and the new gaming concession are separate units of account.

- Impairment assessment: A triggering event under ASC 360 occurred in June 2022 for the MGM China asset group. Recoverability testing showed undiscounted cash flows significantly exceeded carrying value; no impairment was recognized.

- Useful life change and amortization: The gaming subconcession’s useful life was revised from aligning with the MGM Cotai land concession term (to January 2038) to the subconcession’s actual end date (December 31, 2022). Amortized on a straight-line basis over the shortened period; fully amortized by December 31, 2022.

- Amortization expense and schedule: Intangible asset amortization was $2.7 billion (2022), $197 million (2021), and $194 million (2020). Estimated future amortization totals $411.8 million, with scheduled amounts from 2023 through “Thereafter.”

- Other accrued liabilities (Note 8): Presentation of contract and contract-related liabilities (outstanding chip liability, loyalty program obligations, casino front money, advance deposits and ticket sales, unpaid wagers and other) and other accrued items (payroll and related, taxes other than income taxes, MGP dividend, current operating and finance lease liabilities, other). Total other accrued liabilities increased to $2.236 billion at December 31, 2022 (from $1.983 billion at December 31, 2021).

- Impairment assessment (ASC 360): A triggering event occurred for the MGM China asset group in June 2022; estimated undiscounted cash flows exceeded carrying value, so no impairment was recorded.
- Useful life reassessment and amortization: The gaming subconcession intangible’s useful life was shortened to end on December 31, 2022 (aligned with cessation of subconcession rights), shifting from the prior life tied to the MGM Cotai land concession (January 2038). Amortization was recognized on a straight-line basis over the reduced life, and the subconcession was fully amortized by year-end 2022.
- Amortization expense and schedule: Amortization expense was $2.7 billion (2022), $197 million (2021), and $194 million (2020). Estimated future amortization totals $411.8 million: 2023 $77.2m; 2024 $75.2m; 2025 $73.4m; 2026 $71.6m; 2027 $54.6m; thereafter $59.7m.
- Other accrued liabilities (Note 8): As of December 31, 2022 and 2021, key components include outstanding chip liability, loyalty program obligations, casino front money, advance deposits and ticket sales, unpaid wagers, payroll and related, taxes other than income taxes, current operating and finance lease liabilities, and other items; MGP dividend present in 2021 only. Current portion: $1.286 billion (2022) vs. $1.000 billion (2021).
- Interest expense, net: Total interest incurred of $595.7m (2022), $800.2m (2021), $679.3m (2020); minimal interest capitalized each year, resulting in net interest expense of $595.0m (2022), $799.6m (2021), $676.4m (2020).

- Details the income tax provision (benefit) by jurisdiction and component (current, deferred, valuation allowance) for 2020–2022, resulting in a tax expense of approximately $697 million in 2022, $253 million in 2021, and a tax benefit of $192 million in 2020.
- Reconciles statutory to effective tax rates: 2022 effective rate of 77.1% driven largely by foreign income/loss taxed at non-U.S. rates and state taxes; 2021 rate of 17.3% includes impact of CityCenter consolidation gain; 2020 rate of 12.7%.
- Provides components of deferred tax assets and liabilities and a net deferred tax liability of $3.0 billion at December 31, 2022 (up from $2.4 billion in 2021), highlighting large lease-related deferreds, investments, and tax credit DTAs, with significant valuation allowances.
- Rolls forward the deferred tax valuation allowance, ending at $2.887 billion in 2022; notes a $2.6 billion allowance against $2.8 billion of foreign tax credit (FTC) carryovers tied to Macau’s 35% Special Gaming Tax, with reliance on future U.S. operating income and foreign source income for utilization; provides FTC expiry schedule (2023–2027) and emphasizes judgment/sensitivity of assumptions.
- Describes Macau tax matters: exemption from the 12% complementary tax on gaming profits through December 31, 2022 (with disclosed EPS/NI impacts if not exempt); assumption that complementary tax applies beyond 2022 for deferred tax measurement; non-gaming activities remain subject to complementary tax.
- Notes foreign NOLs including a $1.6 billion Macau complementary tax NOL (expiring 2023–2025); discusses a flat ~$2 million annual payment in lieu of shareholder tax on distributions; records an $89 million increase in Macau valuation allowance due to accelerated amortization of the gaming subconcession.
- Discloses state NOLs of $373 million (DTA of $23 million) with an $8 million valuation allowance; expirations generally 2025–2041 or indefinite.
- Reconciles unrecognized tax benefits, decreasing to $6.9 million at December 31, 2022; $7 million would affect the effective tax rate; interest and penalties immaterial.
- Summarizes tax audit status: IRS examination of 2015–2019 (expected to close in 2023 with no material adjustments); NYC audits (2017–2019); Michigan appeal (2014–2018); reversal of $13 million of unrecognized tax benefits related to a customer loyalty program accounting method issue.
- Introduces Note 11 – Leases: outlines triple-net operating leases of resort real estate and land, including responsibility for property costs and minimum capex; describes financial covenants and potential security requirements; Company was in compliance as of December 31, 2022.
- Provides key lease terms:
  - Bellagio lease (with Bellagio BREIT Venture): 30-year initial term with two 10-year renewals; 2% fixed escalator for first 10 years, then greater of 2% or CPI (capped); annual cash rent increased to $260 million for the lease year beginning December 1, 2022.

nodes.heading: 17.4 Adjusted Property EBITDAR.
nodes.start_phrase: Adjusted Property EBITDAR is a measure defined as earnings before interest and other non-operating income (expense), taxes, depreciation and amortization, preopening and start-up expenses, property transactions, net, gain on REIT transactions, net, restructuring costs (which represents costs related to severance, accelerated stock compensation expense, and consulting fees directly related to the operating model component of the MGM 2020 Plan), rent expense related to triple-net operating leases and ground leases, income from unconsolidated affiliates related to investments in real estate ventures, and also excludes gain on consolidation of CityCenter, net, gain related to CityCenter’s sale of Harmon land recorded within income from unconsolidated affiliates, corporate expense (which includes CEO transition expense and October 1 litigation settlement) and stock compensation expense, which are not allocated to each operating segment, and rent expense related to the master lease with MGP that eliminated in consolidation.
nodes.summary:
- Business segmentation and properties:
  - Las Vegas Strip Resorts segment includes Aria (with Vdara; added Sept 2021), Bellagio, The Cosmopolitan (added May 2022), MGM Grand Las Vegas (with The Signature), Mandalay Bay (with Delano and Four Seasons), The Mirage (through Dec 2022 disposition), Luxor, New York-New York (with The Park), Excalibur, and Park MGM (with NoMad Las Vegas).
  - Regional Operations segment includes MGM Grand Detroit (MI), Beau Rivage (MS), Gold Strike Tunica (MS), Borgata (NJ), MGM National Harbor (MD), MGM Springfield (MA), Empire City (NY), and MGM Northfield Park (OH).
  - MGM China segment includes MGM Macau and MGM Cotai.
  - Corporate and other includes LeoVegas (acquired Sept 2022), investments in unconsolidated affiliates, and other corporate operations/management services; not a separate reportable segment.

- Primary segment profit measure:
  - Adjusted Property EBITDAR is the reportable segment GAAP measure used by management. It excludes interest and other non-operating items, taxes, depreciation and amortization, preopening/start-up costs, property transactions, net; gains on REIT transactions and on consolidation of CityCenter; certain restructuring, CEO transition and litigation costs; corporate expense and stock compensation (unallocated); income from unconsolidated real estate ventures; and rent expense related to triple-net operating and ground leases (including master lease with MGP eliminated in consolidation).

- Segment results (years ended Dec 31, 2022, 2021, 2020):
  - Net revenues:
    - Las Vegas Strip Resorts: $8.40B (2022), $4.74B (2021), $2.25B (2020), reflecting strong recovery and acquisitions.
    - Regional Operations: $3.82B (2022), $3.39B (2021), $1.97B (2020).
    - MGM China: $0.67B (2022), $1.21B (2021), $0.66B (2020), showing 2022 weakness.
    - Consolidated including Corporate/other: $13.13B (2022), $9.68B (2021), $5.16B (2020).
  - Adjusted Property EBITDAR:
    - Las Vegas Strip Resorts: $3.14B (2022), $1.74B (2021), $0.23B (2020).
    - Regional Operations: $1.29B (2022), $1.22B (2021), $0.34B (2020).
    - MGM China: -$203M (2022), $25M (2021), -$194M (2020).
    - Total reportable segment Adjusted Property EBITDAR: $4.23B (2022), $2.98B (2021), $0.38B (2020).

- Other operating and non-operating items (2022 highlights vs prior years):
  - Significant 2022 items include depreciation and amortization of $3.48B, triple-net and ground lease rent expense of $1.95B, gain on REIT transactions of $2.28B, and property transactions, net, of $1.04B.
  - Prior-year notable items include gain on consolidation of CityCenter in 2021 ($1.56B) and a 2021 gain related to sale of Harmon land at an unconsolidated affiliate ($49.8M).
  - Operating income (loss): $1.44B (2022), $2.28B (2021), $(642)M (2020).
  - Non-operating income (expense) net: $(536)M (2022), $(817)M (2021), $(869)M (2020).
  - Income (loss) before taxes: $904M (2022), $1.46B (2021), $(1.51)B (2020).
  - Net income (loss) attributable to MGM Resorts International: $1.47B (2022), $1.25B (2021), $(1.03)B (2020). Significant 2022 benefit from large loss attributable to noncontrolling interests.

- Capital expenditures:
  - Total: $765M (2022), $491M (2021), $271M (2020).
  - 2022 by segment: Las Vegas Strip $411M, Regional $191M, MGM China $31M, Corporate/other $132M.

- Assets disclosure:
  - Total assets are not allocated to segments internally and thus not presented by segment.
  - Long-lived assets by geography (Dec 31): United States $31.33B vs China/other foreign $5.00B in 2022 (with comparative balances for 2021 and 2020).

- Related party transactions (Note 18):
  - CityCenter: Prior to MGM’s Sept 2021 acquisition, MGM managed Aria and Vdara for fees (2% of revenue, 5% of EBITDA); fees earned were $29M (2021) and $16M (2020); reimbursable costs were $187M (2021) and $212M (2020). Agreement terminated upon acquisition.
  - MGM China and Pansy Ho relationships:
    - Shun Tak (associated with Ms. Pansy Ho) provided services (ferry tickets, travel, hotel room rentals, laundry, property cleaning) and office leases; expenses: $3M (2022), $7M (2021, 2020).
    - Entities in which Ms. Ho holds interests provided marketing/PR consulting (including concession tender support): $5M (2022), $4M (2021), $1M (2020).
    - Deferred cash payment obligation ($50M) to GPM (controlled by Ms. Ho) from the 2016 MGM China share purchase was settled in Sept 2021; dividends on the shares and final payment were made to Expert Angels Limited (controlled by an immediate family member of Ms. Ho).
    - MGM Branding and Development Holdings, Ltd. (consolidated entity in which Ms. Ho holds a noncontrolling interest) has brand license and development services agreements with MGM China (eliminated in consolidation); distributions to an entity owned by Ms. Ho: $5M (2022), $8M (2021), $5M (2020).
    - Services Agreement (effective Jan 1, 2023) for Ms. Ho as Managing Director of MGM Grand Paradise: $8M annual compensation plus potential incentives up to $95M tied to defined EBITDA targets.

nodes.title: MGP
nodes.heading: 18.3 MGP
nodes.start_phrase: Prior to the closing of the VICI Transaction, the Company leased the real estate assets of The Mirage, Luxor, New York-New York, Park MGM, Excalibur, The Park, Gold Strike Tunica, MGM Grand Detroit, Beau Rivage, Borgata, Empire City, MGM National Harbor, MGM Northfield Park, and MGM Springfield pursuant to a master lease with MGP.
nodes.summary:
- Overview of the Company’s master lease with MGM Growth Properties (MGP) covering numerous properties prior to the VICI Transaction.
- February 2020 removal of Mandalay Bay from the MGP master lease tied to the MGM Grand Las Vegas/Mandalay Bay transaction; annual cash rent reduced by $133 million to $813 million.
- Scheduled 2% fixed annual rent escalations:
  - Lease year 5 (April 1, 2020): rent increased to $828 million.
  - Lease year 6 (April 1, 2021): rent increased to $843 million.
- October 29, 2021: MGP acquired MGM Springfield real estate for $400 million (common control transaction); adjustments recorded to noncontrolling interests and capital in excess of par; master lease amended to add MGM Springfield and increase annual rent by $30 million to $873 million.
- Regulatory contingency for MGM Springfield transfer: trust agreement in place with VICI pending final regulatory approvals; property could be placed in trust if VICI suitability is questioned.
- Lease year 7 (April 1, 2022): annual rent increased to $877 million, reflecting a 2% base rent escalator (+$16 million) partially offset by a percentage rent reset based on prior five-year average net revenues (−$12 million).
- April 2022 completion of the VICI Transaction: deconsolidation of MGP (including its VICI BREIT Venture investment) and entry into an amended and restated master lease with VICI.
- Consolidation notes: all intercompany transactions with MGP eliminated; public ownership of MGP Class A shares presented as noncontrolling interests.
- Bellagio BREIT Venture: the Company holds a 5% interest; the venture owns Bellagio real estate and leases it to a Company subsidiary.

nodes.title: Bellagio BREIT Venture
nodes.heading: 18.4 Bellagio BREIT Venture
nodes.start_phrase: The Company has a 5% ownership interest in Bellagio BREIT Venture, which owns the real estate assets of Bellagio and leases such assets to a subsidiary of the Company pursuant to a lease agreement.
nodes.summary:
- Overview of the Company’s master lease with MGM Growth Properties (MGP) covering numerous casino resort real estate assets (e.g., The Mirage, Luxor, New York-New York, Park MGM, Excalibur, The Park, Gold Strike Tunica, MGM Grand Detroit, Beau Rivage, Borgata, Empire City, MGM National Harbor, MGM Northfield Park, and, later, MGM Springfield) prior to the VICI Transaction.
- February 2020: Mandalay Bay removed from the MGP master lease in connection with the MGM Grand Las Vegas/Mandalay Bay transaction; annual cash rent reduced by $133 million to $813 million.
- Fixed 2% annual rent escalators:
  - Fifth lease year (starting April 1, 2020): rent increased to $828 million.
  - Sixth lease year (starting April 1, 2021): rent increased to $843 million.
- October 29, 2021: MGP acquired the real estate of MGM Springfield from the Company for $400 million (common control accounting). Noncontrolling interests and capital in excess of par adjusted accordingly. The master lease was amended to add MGM Springfield, increasing annual cash rent by $30 million to $873 million.
- Regulatory contingency: Until final approvals, a trust agreement governs the MGM Springfield property (held in trust or returned to the Company) if there is reasonable cause to question VICI’s suitability as landlord post-VICI Transaction.
- Seventh lease year (starting April 1, 2022): annual cash rent increased to $877 million, reflecting a 2% escalator (+$16 million) partially offset by a percentage rent reset based on the prior five-year average net revenues (−$12 million).
- April 2022: Completion of the VICI Transaction; MGP (including its investment in the VICI BREIT Venture) was deconsolidated. The Company entered into an amended and restated master lease with VICI.
- Consolidation/accounting: All intercompany transactions under the MGP master lease were eliminated while MGP was consolidated; public ownership of MGP Class A shares was recognized as noncontrolling interests.
- Bellagio BREIT Venture: The Company holds a 5% interest in the venture that owns Bellagio’s real estate and leases it to a Company subsidiary.

- Item 9A: Controls and Procedures
  - Disclosure controls and procedures were concluded by the CEO and CFO to be effective as of December 31, 2022, providing reasonable assurance of timely, accurate SEC reporting and internal communication, based on evaluations under Exchange Act Rules 13a-15 and 15d-15.
  - No changes in internal control over financial reporting during the quarter ended December 31, 2022 that materially affected or are reasonably likely to materially affect ICFR.
  - Management’s Annual Report on ICFR:
    - Management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate ICFR for MGM Resorts International and subsidiaries.
    - Objective is to provide reasonable assurance that financial statements and related disclosures are reliable, free of material misstatement or omission, and fairly present financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows; and that information is communicated timely for required disclosures.
    - Key ICFR elements: skilled and trained accounting personnel; written accounting policies; documented systems and procedures; segregation of duties; internal audit function; independent Audit Committee oversight.
    - Evaluation performed using the COSO 2013 Internal Control—Integrated Framework with participation of the principal executive and financial officers.
    - The Cosmopolitan, acquired in Q2 2022, was excluded from the ICFR evaluation as of December 31, 2022.

accumulated and communicated to management to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosures.

nodes.summary:
- Extract from a concession contract governing the operation of games of fortune or chance in casinos in the Macau Special Administrative Region (Macau SAR).
- Clause 1 (Scope): Authorizes operation of casino games in Macau SAR; expressly excludes mutual betting, certain public operations unless allowed under Law No. 16/2001 Section 3(7), interactive games, and gaming/betting on ships or aircraft except as permitted by Law No. 16/2001 Section 5(4)(1) and (5).
- Clause 2 (Objectives/Obligations): Requires operations to safeguard national and Macau SAR security; promote economic diversification and sustainable development; ensure fairness and honesty; remain free from criminal influence; align with policies combating illegal cross-border capital flows and preventing money laundering and terrorism; adhere to legal limits on the size and operation of gaming; ensure suitability of supervisory and operational personnel; and protect Macau SAR’s tax interests.
- Clause 3 (Applicable Law and Jurisdiction): Contract is governed exclusively by Macau SAR law; concessionaire waives litigation outside Macau; Macau courts have exclusive jurisdiction.

nodes.title: Applicable law and jurisdiction
nodes.heading:
Clause 3
Applicable law and jurisdiction
nodes.start_phrase: One. This concession contract is subject exclusively to the law of Macau SAR.
nodes.summary:

- Establishes governing law and jurisdiction: the contract is governed exclusively by Macau SAR law; the concessionaire waives litigation in other jurisdictions; Macau courts have exclusive jurisdiction over disputes.
- Mandates observance of Macau SAR legislation and waives the concessionaire’s ability to invoke foreign law to avoid obligations.

CHAPTER II
Locations for the games of fortune or chance in casinos
nodes.start_phrase: One. The operation of games of fortune or chance in casinos, by the Concessionaire, outside the casinos, as referred in clause 10, requires prior authorization of the Chief Executive.
nodes.summary:
- Scope and approvals: Any intention by the Concessionaire to operate games of fortune or chance—whether in Macau casinos or in other countries/regions—requires prior authorization from the Chief Executive after consultation with the Specialized Committee for Games of Fortune and Chance.
- Government cooperation: The Concessionaire must submit or obtain and provide all documents, information, or data requested by the Macau SAR Government for authorization purposes, except items legally deemed confidential.
- Legal framework: The concession regime is governed by Law No. 7/2022 (amending Law No. 16/2001), Law No. 16/2001, Administrative Regulation No. 26/2001 (public tendering, concession contracts, and suitability/financial capacity requirements), other applicable provisions, and the current concession contract.
- Compliance obligation: The Concessionaire must operate strictly in line with applicable laws and the concession contract.
- Term: The concession runs for 10 years, from 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2032, with certain contractual clauses surviving beyond the term.
- Locations and authorization: Operating outside casinos requires prior authorization from the Chief Executive. Applications must follow Section 5-A of Law No. 16/2001 and specify logistic service areas. Casinos must generally be located on real estate owned by the Concessionaire, subject to statutory exceptions (Section 5(4) and Section 37 of Law No. 16/2001).
- Authorized casinos: “MGM Casino Macau” and “MGM Casino Cotai.”
- Game types: Authorization covers the games listed in Section 6(2) of Law No. 7/2022 and any others approved by the Secretary for Economy and Finance under Section 3(4) of Law No. 16/2001.
- Reporting and operational requirements: Each December, the Concessionaire must submit to the Gaming Inspection and Coordination Bureau (DICJ) the planned number and locations of tables and slot machines for the following year. Changes to the number of tables or machines require prior communication to DICJ. The Concessionaire must maintain and operate a minimum variety of games as instructed by DICJ.

Clause 10
Authorized sites for the operation of games of fortune and chance

nodes.summary:
- Clause 9 (Locations for operation): Operating games outside casinos requires prior authorization from the Chief Executive. Applications must be filed under Section 5-A of Law No. 16/2001 specifying logistic service areas. Casinos must be located on real estate owned by the Concessionaire, except as allowed by Sections 5(4) and 37 of Law No. 16/2001.
- Clause 10 (Authorized sites): The Concessionaire may operate “MGM Casino Macau” and “MGM Casino Cotai.”
- Clause 11 (Types of games and operational obligations): The Concessionaire may operate games listed in Section 6(2) of Law No. 7/2022 and any others authorized by the Secretary for Economy and Finance under Section 3(4) of Law No. 16/2001. Each December, it must submit to the Gaming Inspection and Coordination Bureau (DICJ) a list of the number and locations of gaming tables and slot machines planned for the following year. Any changes to these numbers require prior communication to DICJ, and the Concessionaire must maintain a minimum variety of games as instructed by DICJ.

nodes.title: Types of games to be operated
nodes.heading:
Clause 1 1
Types of games to be operated
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionair e is authorized to operate the types of games of fortune or chance referred in Section 6 (2) of Law No. 7/2022, as well as all types of games of fortune or chance authorized by the Secretary for Economy and Finance, under Section 3 (4) of Law No. 16/2001.
nodes.summary:
- Clause 9 sets location rules: operating games of fortune or chance outside the authorized casinos requires prior authorization from the Chief Executive; applications must be submitted under Section 5-A of Law No. 16/2001 detailing specific logistic service areas; casinos must be on real estate owned by the Concessionaire, except as allowed by Section 5(4) and Section 37 of Law No. 16/2001.
- Clause 10 lists authorized casino sites: “MGM Casino Macau” and “MGM Casino Cotai.”
- Clause 11 defines game types and capacity management: the Concessionaire may operate games under Section 6(2) of Law No. 7/2022 and any others authorized by the Secretary for Economy and Finance under Section 3(4) of Law No. 16/2001; annually by December, it must submit to the Gaming Inspection and Coordination Bureau (DICJ) the planned number and locations of tables and slot machines for the following year; changes to numbers require prior communication to DICJ; a minimum variety of games must be maintained per DICJ instructions.
- Clause 12 mandates continuous operation: casinos must be open 24/7 year-round; operations may be suspended or hours adjusted only in exceptional cases at the request or with authorization of the Chief Executive, who also determines resumption; requests require 10 days’ notice to DICJ and public posting at casino entrances; in urgent situations (e.g., serious accidents, catastrophes), DICJ consent is required for suspension/resumption; a 24/7 emergency communication mechanism must be maintained with DICJ and other concessionaires.
- Clause 13 requires high-standard electronic surveillance and control: equipment must meet high international standards and be approved by DICJ, with submissions of written requests and technical specs (and specimens if asked); installation may be required in adjacent or access areas; new or upgraded equipment must be installed when requested to maintain standards; any suspected crimes, contraventions, administrative offences, or serious illegal acts must be promptly reported to the relevant authorities.

nodes.title: Continuous operation of the casinos
nodes.heading:
Clause 12
Continuous operation of the casinos
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionaire undertakes to maintain the casinos open every day of the year , for twenty-four hours, without interruption.
nodes.summary:
- Clause 12 (Continuous operation): Requires the Concessionaire to keep casinos open 24/7 year-round. Operations may be suspended or hours adjusted only in exceptional cases at the request or with the authorization of the Chief Executive, who decides when operations resume. For planned exceptions, the Concessionaire must notify DICJ at least 10 days in advance and post notices at casino entrances. In urgent situations (serious accident, catastrophe, natural calamity) prior authorization may be waived, but DICJ consent is required for both suspension and resumption. The Concessionaire must maintain a 24/7 emergency communication mechanism with DICJ and other concessionaires.
- Clause 13 (Electronic surveillance and control): Requires installation of DICJ-approved, high international standard electronic surveillance and control equipment in casinos, with written requests and technical specifications submitted to DICJ; DICJ may require equipment samples. Such equipment must also be installed in adjacent or access areas when requested. The Concessionaire must upgrade or install new equipment as requested to maintain standards. It must promptly report to relevant authorities any known or suspected crimes, contraventions, administrative offences, or other serious illegal acts.

nodes.title: Electronic surveillance and control equipment
nodes.heading:
Clause 13
Electr onic surveillance and contr ol equipment
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionaire undertakes to install in the casinos electronic surveillance and control equipment of high international standard as approved by DICJ.
nodes.summary:
- Clause 12 (Continuous operation): Casinos must operate 24/7 year-round. Exceptions to suspend or adjust hours require Chief Executive authorization, with DICJ notified 10 days in advance and public notice at casino entrances. In urgent cases (accident/calamity), prior authorization may be waived but DICJ consent is still required for suspension and resumption. The Concessionaire must maintain a 24/7 emergency communication channel with DICJ and other concessionaires.

- Clause 13 (Electronic surveillance and control): The Concessionaire must install and, upon request, upgrade DICJ-approved, high-standard surveillance and control equipment in casinos and, when requested, in adjacent/access areas. DICJ may request technical specs and samples. The Concessionaire must promptly report crimes, contraventions, or serious illegal acts to authorities.

- Chapter III – Concessionaire company:
  - Clause 14 (Object, head office, structure): Corporate purpose must include casino gaming; adding related activities requires prior authorization from the Secretary for Economy and Finance. The company must be headquartered in Macau SAR and be a limited company.
  - Clause 15 (Share capital and shares): Minimum share capital MOP 5,000,000,000, with net worth maintained at or above that level throughout the concession. The Chief Executive may mandate capital increases. All shares must be nominal. Capital increases via public subscription, issuance of preferred shares, creation/issuance of new share types/series, and share transfers all require Government authorization. Clause 15.7 begins a pledge concerning shareholders’ share capital but is truncated.

nodes.title: Concessionaire company
nodes.heading:
CHAPTER III
Concessionaire company
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionaire’ s corporate purpose shall include the operation of games of fortune or chance in casinos.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes the framework for the Concessionaire company (Chapter III).
- Clause 14 (Object, head office, corporate structure):
  - Corporate purpose must include operating games of fortune or chance in casinos.
  - Any addition of correlated activities to the corporate purpose requires prior authorization from the Secretary for the Economy and Finance.
  - The Concessionaire must keep its head office in the Macau SAR and be incorporated as a limited company.
- Clause 15 (Share capital and shares):
  - Minimum share capital set at MOP 5,000,000,000, with net worth maintained at or above that level during the concession.
  - Chief Executive may require an increase in share capital if circumstances warrant.
  - All share capital must be in nominal shares.
  - Any capital increase via public subscription requires Government authorization.
  - Issuance of preferred shares requires Government authorization.
  - Creation/issuance of types or series of shares, and any transfer of such shares, require Government authorization.
  - An additional obligation regarding the share capital of company shareholders is introduced but the text is truncated.

nodes.title: Object, head office and corporate structure
nodes.heading:
Clause 14
Object, head office and corporate structur e
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionaire’ s corporate purpose shall include the operation of games of fortune or chance in casinos.
nodes.summary:
- Defines the concessionaire’s corporate purpose as operating games of fortune or chance in casinos; adding related activities requires prior authorization from the Secretary for the Economy and Finance.
- Requires the concessionaire to maintain its head office in the Macau SAR and be incorporated as a limited company.
- Sets a minimum share capital and net worth of MOP 5,000,000,000 during the concession term, with the Chief Executive empowered to require increases if circumstances warrant.
- Mandates that all shares be nominal; any capital increase via public subscription needs Government authorization.
- Issuance of preferred shares, creation/issuance of new classes or series of shares, and transfers of shares all require Government authorization.
- Begins a clause indicating the concessionaire’s pledge concerning the share capital of its corporate shareholders (text incomplete).

nodes.title: Share capital and shares
nodes.heading:
Clause 15
Shar e capital and shar es
nodes.start_phrase: One. The share capital of the Concessionaire shall not be less than MOP 5,000,000,000 (five billion patacas), with its net worth to be kept at not less than that amount during the term of the concession.
nodes.summary:
- Scope and structure of the concessionaire:
  - Corporate purpose must include operating games of chance in casinos.
  - Adding related activities during the concession requires prior authorization from the Secretary for Economy and Finance.
  - Must maintain head office in the Macau SAR and be incorporated as a limited company.

- Share capital and shares:
  - Minimum share capital: MOP 5,000,000,000; net worth must not fall below this during the concession.
  - Chief Executive may require a capital increase if circumstances warrant.
  - All share capital must be in nominal (registered) shares.
  - Public capital increases, issuance of preferred shares, creation/issuance of new share types or series, and any transfer of such shares require Government authorization.
  - The concessionaire must endeavor to ensure that the entire ownership chain of its corporate shareholders (down to ultimate holders) is represented exclusively by nominal shares, except for listed companies regarding exchange-tradable shares.

- Transfer and encumbrance of shares:
  - Any inter vivos transfer or encumbrance of shares, or acts granting voting or other corporate rights to third parties, requires authorization from the Secretary for Economy and Finance.
  - The concessionaire must refuse to register or recognize shareholders who acquire/hold shares in breach of the contract or law and must not act in ways that imply recognition of such transfers.
