  - Mortis causa share transfers must be reported to DICJ within 15 days of becoming aware, with supporting documents; the concessionaire must ensure registration in its share register.
  - After authorized transactions, the holder must promptly notify the concessionaire, which must report to DICJ within 30 days of registration, providing copies and detailed terms.
  - The concessionaire must ensure that transfers of holdings at any level of its shareholder chain corresponding directly or indirectly to 5% or more of its share capital are subject to authorization by the Secretary for Economy and Finance, except for listed companies regarding exchange-tradable shares.

nodes.title: Transfer and encumbrance of shares
nodes.heading:
Clause 16
Transfer and encumbrance of shar es
nodes.start_phrase: One. The transfer inter vivos or encumbrance, by any means, of the ownership or other rights over shares representing the Concessionaire's share capital, as well as the performance of any acts involving the attribution of voting rights or other corporate rights to a person other than its holder , shall require authorization from the Secretary for Economy and Finance.
nodes.summary:
- All shares throughout the ownership chain down to final shareholders must be registered (nominal), except for shares of listed companies to the extent they are tradable on a stock exchange.
- Clause 16 sets strict controls on share transfers and encumbrances:
  - Any inter vivos transfer or encumbrance of Concessionaire shares, or any act granting voting or other corporate rights to a non-holder, requires prior authorization from the Secretary for Economy and Finance.
  - The Concessionaire must refuse to register or recognize any shareholder or transaction made in breach of the contract or law and must not imply recognition of such acts.
  - Mortis causa transfers of Concessionaire shares must be reported to DICJ within 15 days of becoming known, with supporting documents, and recorded in the share register.
  - After authorized transactions, the holder must promptly notify the Concessionaire, which must report to DICJ within 30 days of registration, enclosing formal documents and detailed terms/conditions.
  - Inter vivos transfers of shareholdings at any tier up to final holders that correspond, directly or indirectly, to 5% or more of the Concessionaire’s share capital require authorization from the Secretary for Economy and Finance, except for listed entities with tradable shares.
  - Mortis causa transfers of such 5%+ indirect holdings must be communicated to DICJ as soon as known.
  - Any encumbrance or attribution of voting/other corporate rights affecting such 5%+ indirect holdings must also be notified to DICJ promptly, with the same exception for listed tradable shares.
  - The 30‑day reporting and documentation requirements apply mutatis mutandis to the indirect transfers covered above.
- Clause 17 defines “decisions on major financial initiatives” and notification duties:
  - Internal movement of funds exceeding 50% of share capital.
  - Decisions on salaries, remunerations, or employee benefits exceeding 10% of share capital.
  - Any other financial decisions exceeding 10% of share capital.
  - The Concessionaire must notify the Chief Executive at least five working days before such decisions, unless there is acceptable just cause.

nodes.title: Notification and authorization
nodes.heading:
Clause 17
Notification and authorization
nodes.start_phrase: One. The following are considered to be decisions on major financial initiatives, referred to in Section 22 (1) (12) of Law No. 16/2001:
nodes.summary:
- Mandatory notifications to DICJ of mortis causa transfers, encumbrances, or attribution of voting/other corporate rights involving any shareholdings that, directly or indirectly, correspond to 5% or more of the Concessionaire’s share capital, cascading through all tiers of ownership to ultimate holders; exceptions apply to tradable shares of listed companies.
- Extension of earlier transfer restrictions to additional forms of ownership/right transfers via cross-referenced clauses.
- Definition of “major financial initiatives” (per Law No. 16/2001, Sec. 22(1)(12)): internal fund movements exceeding 50% of share capital; compensation/benefit decisions exceeding 10%; other financial decisions exceeding 10%.
- Advance notice obligation: Concessionaire must notify the Chief Executive at least five working days before taking major financial decisions, unless justified.
- Prior authorization by the Secretary for Economy and Finance required for: (i) transfers of real or credit rights exceeding MOP 100,000,000; (ii) borrowing/loan agreements of MOP 100,000,000 or more.
- Issuance of debt securities by the Concessionaire requires authorization from the Chief Executive.
- Stock exchange restrictions: the Concessionaire and any company it controls may not be listed; if any direct or indirect 5%+ shareholder is listed, the Concessionaire must notify DICJ within 15 days with relevant information; it must also endeavor to ensure prior government notification before such companies proceed with listings.
- Annual December filing to the Government detailing the Concessionaire’s shareholding and capital structure, and those of all 5%+ upstream holders through to ultimate shareholders (with exceptions for listed companies’ tradable shares), or a declaration of no change.
- Obligation to obtain and submit authenticated declarations from each shareholder and upstream qualifying holders confirming their shareholdings.

nodes.title: Issuance of debt securities
nodes.heading:
Clause 18
Issuance of debt securities
nodes.start_phrase: The issuance of debt securities by the Concessionaire requires the Chief Executives’ authorization.
nodes.summary:
- High-value transactions require prior approval: transfers of the concessionaire’s real or credit rights exceeding MOP 100,000,000 and any loans of MOP 100,000,000 or more need authorization from the Secretary for Economy and Finance.
- Debt issuance control: any issuance of debt securities by the concessionaire requires authorization from the Chief Executive.
- Stock exchange restrictions and notifications: the concessionaire and any company it controls may not be listed on a stock exchange; if any shareholder holding 5% or more of the concessionaire is listed, the concessionaire must notify DICJ within 15 days and provide related information/documents; the concessionaire will endeavor to ensure such companies do not proceed with a listing without prior government notification.
- Ownership transparency: annually in December, the concessionaire must submit a detailed report of its shareholding and capital structure, tracing entities with 5% or more holdings up to ultimate shareholders (with exceptions for publicly traded shares), or confirm no change; it must also obtain authenticated declarations from shareholders and relevant upstream holders confirming their shareholdings.

nodes.title: Listing on the stock exchange
nodes.heading:
Clause 19
Listing on the stock exchange
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionaire, or a company in which it is the controlling shareholder , may not be listed on a stock exchange.
nodes.summary:
- Transfers of the Concessionaire’s real or credit rights exceeding MOP 100,000,000, and any loan agreements of MOP 100,000,000 or more, require prior authorization from the Secretary for Economy and Finance.
- Issuance of debt securities by the Concessionaire requires authorization from the Chief Executive.
- Stock exchange restrictions: the Concessionaire and any company it controls may not be listed. If any shareholder holding 5% or more (directly or indirectly) is listed, the Concessionaire must notify DICJ within 15 days and provide relevant listing information, and must seek to ensure such companies do not list without prior government notification.
- Shareholding transparency: each December, the Concessionaire must submit to the Government a detailed report of its shareholding structure, and the capital structure of all entities holding 5% or more (recursively up to ultimate shareholders), with exceptions for publicly listed shares, or submit a no-change declaration.
- The Concessionaire must also endeavor to obtain and deliver duly authenticated declarations from each shareholder and relevant upstream holders confirming their stated shareholdings.

nodes.title: Shareholder and capital structure
nodes.heading:
Clause 20
Shar eholder and capital structur e
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionaire undertakes to submit annually a document to the Government, during each December , detailing its shareholding structu re, and as well the share capital structure of the companies holding 5% or more of the Concessionaire’ s share capital, and also the structure of the share capital of the companies holding 5% or more of these companies’ share capital, and so on until the individuals or companies that are last shareholders, except with regard to companies that are listed on stock exchanges in what concerns the shares dealt therein, or to present a declaration attesting that these have not under gone any change.
nodes.summary:
- Government approvals for major financing: transfers of the Concessionaire’s real or credit rights and any loan agreements at or above MOP 100,000,000 require authorization from the Secretary for Economy and Finance; any issuance of debt securities requires authorization from the Chief Executive.
- Stock exchange restrictions: the Concessionaire and any company it controls may not be listed. If any direct or indirect shareholder with 5% or more is listed, the Concessionaire must notify DICJ within 15 days with relevant information and documents, and must endeavor to ensure such companies do not list without prior government notification.
- Transparency of ownership: each December the Concessionaire must submit an up-to-date, detailed shareholding chain showing all holders of 5% or more at each level up to ultimate shareholders (with exceptions for listed companies’ traded shares), or confirm no changes. It must also endeavor to provide authenticated declarations from each shareholder attesting their registered holdings, with copies of the share certificates.
- Corporate governance conflicts: individuals may not hold positions in more than one corporate body among concessionaires, junkets, or management companies (except participation in general meetings). The Concessionaire must promptly notify DICJ of appointments to its corporate bodies; the government will inform if appointees hold conflicting roles. Actions taken in breach are voidable, and DICJ will require removal of offending members within a set period.
- Managing director requirements: the board must delegate management to a managing director who is a permanent resident of Macau SAR and holds at least 15% of the Concessionaire’s share capital.

nodes.title: Prohibition on accumulating functions in the corporate bodies
nodes.heading:
Clause 21
Prohibition on accumulating functions in the corporate bodies
nodes.start_phrase: One. It is prohibited for any person to accumulate functions in the following corporate bodies or to accumulate functions in more than one corporate body of any of the companies mentioned below , with the exception of general meetings:
nodes.summary:
- Addresses registration of shares, requiring proof via copies of the securities representing the respective shares.
- Clause 21: Prohibits individuals from holding roles in more than one corporate body among concessionaires, junkets (gaming promoters), and management companies, except participation in general meetings.
- Requires concessionaires to promptly notify DICJ of appointments to their corporate bodies.
- Government will inform concessionaires if an appointee also serves on another concessionaire, gaming promoter, or management company in Macau SAR.
- Acts or resolutions made in breach of the prohibition are voidable.
- DICJ may order concessionaires to remove offending corporate body members within a set timeframe.
- Clause 22: The board must delegate management to a managing director.
- The managing director must be a permanent resident of Macau SAR and hold at least 15% of the concessionaire’s share capital.

nodes.title: Managing Director
nodes.heading:
Clause 22
Managing Dir ector
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionaire's board of directors undertakes to delegate the management of the Concessionaire to a managing director .
nodes.summary:
- Share registration: references a requirement to register share transactions, accompanied by copies of the securities representing the shares.
- Clause 21 (Prohibition on accumulating functions): 
  - Individuals cannot hold roles simultaneously in corporate bodies of concessionaires, junkets, or management companies (except participation in general meetings).
  - Concessionaires must promptly notify DICJ of appointments to boards or other corporate bodies.
  - Government will inform if an appointee also serves in another concessionaire, gaming promoter, or management company.
  - Acts/resolutions involving improperly appointed members are voidable.
  - DICJ can order removal of violating members within a specified period.
- Clause 22 (Managing Director):
  - Board must delegate company management to a Managing Director.
  - The Managing Director must be a Macau SAR permanent resident and hold at least 15% of the concessionaire’s share capital.
  - Appointment, scope of powers, term, and any temporary or definitive replacement require Chief Executive authorization; draft board resolutions with full details must be sent to DICJ.
  - If not approved, a new draft must be submitted within 15 days; if the person is rejected, a completed Annex II to Administrative Regulation No. 26/2001 for the new Managing Director must be provided.
  - Concessionaire may not issue standing mandates/powers of attorney that effectively transfer board powers, except for routine administrative acts, unless authorized by the Government.
- Clause 23 (Articles of association and shareholder agreements):
  - Any amendments to articles or shareholder agreements require DICJ approval under penalty of nullity.
  - Proposed amendments must be submitted to DICJ at least 30 days before the shareholders’ meeting.
  - Certified copies of approved changes must be delivered to DICJ within 30 days of the vote.
  - Concessionaire must inform DICJ of any shareholder agreements it knows of and must inquire shareholders shortly before or during general meetings about the existence of such agreements (especially those on voting/corporate rights), reporting the results to DICJ.
  - DICJ will notify within 60 days whether it approves amendments and shareholder agreements.
- Clause 24 heading follows but content is not included in this excerpt.

nodes.title: Sections of association and shareholder agreements
nodes.heading:
Clause 23
Sections of association and shar eholder agreements
nodes.start_phrase: One. Any change to the Concessionaire’ s articles of association and agreements between shareholders must be approved by DICJ, under penalty of nullity .
nodes.summary:
- Management delegation and Managing Director (MD) appointment:
  - Any delegation of management, MD appointment, scope of powers, term, and any temporary/definitive replacement require Chief Executive authorization, under penalty of nullity.
  - Concessionaire must submit to DICJ a board resolution draft detailing the MD’s identity, powers, term, and replacement provisions; any replacement resolutions must also be submitted.
  - If the Government disapproves any terms or the proposed person, the Concessionaire must submit a new draft within 15 days of notification and, if a new person is indicated, provide Annex II to Administrative Regulation No. 26/2001 completed by the new MD.
  - The Concessionaire may not issue mandates/powers of attorney that, on a stable basis, grant board-level powers to conduct company business, except for expedient acts (e.g., at public offices/services) unless authorized by the Government.

- Clause 23 – Articles of association and shareholder agreements:
  - Any change to articles of association and any shareholder agreements must be approved by DICJ, under penalty of nullity.
  - Proposals to amend articles must be sent to DICJ at least 30 days before the shareholders’ meeting where they will be decided.
  - A certified copy of any approved amendment must be delivered to DICJ within 30 days of the vote.
  - The Concessionaire must inform DICJ of any shareholder agreements it knows of and must inquire of shareholders within 15 days prior to any annual meeting (or during a meeting without prior notice) about the existence of agreements, especially those on voting or other corporate rights, and report the results to DICJ.
  - DICJ will notify the Concessionaire within 60 days whether it approves amendments to statutes and shareholder agreements.

nodes.title: Duty of information
nodes.heading:
Clause 24
Duty of information
nodes.start_phrase: One. Without prejudice to any other duties of information established under the concession’ s regime mentioned in Clause 6, the Concessionaire undertakes to:
nodes.summary:
- Establishes a broad duty of information by the Concessionaire to DICJ, requiring prompt notification of:
  - Any circumstances affecting normal operations (e.g., liquidity/solvency issues, legal proceedings involving the company, its directors, 5%+ shareholders, or key employees; and any known crimes, misdemeanors, or administrative infractions in casinos or gaming areas).
  - Any events that could impair, impede, or make excessively onerous timely and full compliance with concession obligations, or that could justify termination.
  - Remunerations (salaries, earnings, wages, fees, profit-sharing mechanisms) paid to directors, investors, and key employees; existing or proposed perks, including profit distribution; and existing or proposed management and service contracts, along with certified copies of related contracts or instruments.
  - Imminent or foreseeable serious changes in the economic/financial situation of the Concessionaire, its controlling shareholders, closely associated entities (including financiers/guarantors of investments/obligations), and 5%+ shareholders who committed or guaranteed such financing.
  - When average annual turnover with any third party reaches or exceeds MOP 500,000,000.
- Requires annual (January) submission to DICJ of all bank accounts and balances.
- Requires prompt submission of any additional information requested by DICJ, and provision of details/information to DICJ and DSF as needed.
- Allows DICJ to determine that notifications/submissions concerning remunerations, perks, and related contracts (items 3 and 4) be made on an annual basis.

Management Company (Clause 25):
- Contracting a management company requires authorization by the Chief Executive and approval of the draft management contract.
- The management company may only receive remuneration for management; no sharing of casino revenues or payment of commissions is allowed.
- The management company is subject to Law 16/2001 and other applicable legislation.

nodes.title: Management Company
nodes.heading:
CHAPTER IV
Management Company
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionaire undertakes to submit the contracting of a management company to the Chief Executive’ s authorization and to submit the draft management contract for approval.
nodes.summary:
- Disclosure and reporting duties to the Gaming Inspection and Coordination Bureau (DICJ) and the Financial Services Bureau (DSF), including:
  - Identification of closely associated entities that have committed to or guaranteed financing of the concessionaire’s contractual investments/obligations.
  - Identification of shareholders holding 5% or more who have provided such commitments/guarantees.
  - Notification to DICJ when average annual turnover with any third party reaches or exceeds MOP 500,000,000.
  - Annual January submission to DICJ of all bank accounts and balances.
  - Prompt submission of any additional information requested by DICJ or DSF.
- DICJ may require that certain obligations (referenced as subparagraphs 3 and 4 of the prior paragraph) be fulfilled on an annual basis.
- Management company regime (Chapter IV, Clause 25):
  - Hiring a management company requires prior authorization from the Chief Executive and approval of the draft management contract.
  - The concessionaire may only pay management remuneration; sharing casino revenues or paying commissions to the management company is prohibited.
  - Law 16/2001 and other applicable legislation apply to the management company.

nodes.title: Applicable regime
nodes.heading:
Clause 25
Applicable r egime
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionaire undertakes to submit the contracting of a management company to the Chief Executive’ s authorization and to submit the draft management contract for approval.
nodes.summary:
- Reporting and disclosure duties to DICJ (Macau Gaming Inspection and Coordination Bureau):
  - Identify and report entities closely associated with the Concessionaire that commit to or guarantee financing of its investment and contractual obligations.
  - Identify and report shareholders holding 5%+ who commit to or guarantee such financing.
  - Notify DICJ when average annual turnover with any third party reaches or exceeds MOP 500,000,000.
  - Annually (in January) submit to DICJ a list of all bank accounts and balances.
  - Promptly provide any additional information requested by DICJ.
  - Promptly provide information required by DICJ and the Financial Services Bureau (DSF) for their functions.
  - DICJ may require certain obligations (referenced subparagraphs 3 and 4) to be performed annually.

- Management company regime (Clause 25):
  - Contracting a management company requires prior authorization by the Chief Executive and approval of the draft management contract.
  - Payments to the management company are limited to management remuneration; no revenue sharing or commissions allowed.
  - Law 16/2001 and other applicable laws apply to the management company.

- Concessionaire’s good standing (Clause 26):
  - The Concessionaire must remain trustworthy throughout the concession term and is subject to continuous government monitoring.
  - The Concessionaire bears the costs of good-standing verification within DICJ-set deadlines; DICJ issues documentation evidencing such costs.

- Suitability of shareholders, directors, and key employees (Clause 27):
  - Shareholders with 5%+, directors, and key employees must remain trustworthy and are subject to ongoing government monitoring.
  - The Concessionaire must ensure their suitability, acknowledging their impact on the Concessionaire’s own suitability.
  - The Concessionaire must require these persons to promptly inform DICJ of any facts relevant to their or the Concessionaire’s trustworthiness.
  - Every six months, the Concessionaire must ask them about any such facts and promptly inform DICJ if it becomes aware of relevant information.

nodes.title: Appropriate qualifications
nodes.heading:
CHAPTER V
Appropriate qualifications
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionaire undertakes to remain trustworthy during the term of the concession, according to law .
nodes.summary:
- Establishes “Appropriate qualifications” standards (Chapter V) for a concession.
- Clause 26: The Concessionaire must remain trustworthy throughout the concession term, is subject to continuous government monitoring and supervision, and must pay the DICJ-set costs for verifying its good standing, with DICJ documentation serving as proof.
- Clause 27: Shareholders holding 5% or more, directors, and key employees must also remain trustworthy and are under continuous government monitoring. The Concessionaire must ensure their suitability, recognizing that their trustworthiness impacts the Concessionaire’s own. It must require these parties to promptly inform DICJ of any facts relevant to trustworthiness, conduct six-monthly inquiries of them about such facts, and promptly inform DICJ of any relevant facts it becomes aware of.

nodes.title: Good standing of the Concessionaire
nodes.heading:
Clause 26
Good standing of the Concessionair e
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionaire undertakes to remain trustworthy during the term of the concession, according to law .
nodes.summary: Chapter V sets out “appropriate qualifications” requirements. Clause 26 mandates that the Concessionaire maintain legal trustworthiness (“good standing”) throughout the concession, remain under continuous government monitoring and supervision, and bear DICJ-specified costs for verification, with DICJ issuing a cost document as proof. Clause 27 extends suitability obligations to shareholders holding 5% or more, directors, and key employees, who must remain trustworthy and are likewise subject to ongoing government oversight. The Concessionaire must ensure their suitability, recognizing its impact on the Concessionaire’s own standing, require these parties to promptly inform DICJ of any facts relevant to trustworthiness, conduct semiannual inquiries to detect such facts, and promptly notify DICJ upon becoming aware of any relevant information.

nodes.title: Suitability of the shareholders, directors and key employees of the Concessionaire and management companies
nodes.heading:
Clause 27
Suitability of the shar eholders, dir ectors and key employees of the Concessionair e and management companies
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionaire's shareholders holding 5% or more of its share capital and its directors and key employees must remain trustworthy during the Concessionaire’ s term, according to law .
nodes.summary:
- Chapter V sets out “Appropriate qualifications” requirements focused on maintaining trustworthiness (“good standing”) of the Concessionaire and related parties.
- Clause 26: The Concessionaire must remain trustworthy throughout the concession, is subject to continuous government monitoring and supervision, and must bear DICJ-specified costs for verifying its good standing, with DICJ issuing documentation of such costs.
- Clause 27: Shareholders holding 5% or more, directors, key employees, and contracted management companies must also remain trustworthy and are under continuous government oversight. The Concessionaire must:
  - Ensure these parties’ ongoing suitability, recognizing its impact on the Concessionaire’s own suitability.
  - Require them to promptly inform DICJ of any facts relevant to their or the Concessionaire’s trustworthiness.
  - Conduct semiannual inquiries to detect such facts and promptly report any known relevant facts to DICJ.
  - Apply the same verification processes (including associated costs) to these parties.
- Clause 28: Special duty of cooperation—beyond the general duty in Clause 67, the Concessionaire must provide any documents, information, or materials the Government deems necessary to verify suitability.
- Clause 29: Special duty of notification—the Concessionaire must notify DICJ within 15 days of learning that any director or 5%+ shareholder:
  - Is participating in, operating, or ceasing operations of games of fortune or casino games in other jurisdictions.
  - Is under investigation by a foreign regulator in a way that could sanction, suspend, influence authorized operations, or affect obtaining gaming licenses or concessions.
- Chapter VI introduces “Financial Capacity and Financing” (content not included in the excerpt).

nodes.title: Special duty of cooperation
nodes.heading:
Clause 28
Special duty of cooperation
nodes.start_phrase: Without prejudice to the general duty of cooperation set out in Clause 67, the Concessionaire undertakes to provide the Government with any document, information or materials the Government considers necessary to verify its suitability .
nodes.summary:
- Establishes reporting obligations to the DICJ regarding the good-standing and suitability of shareholders holding 5% or more, directors, and key employees, to be communicated as soon as possible after becoming aware.
- Imposes an ongoing duty to ensure that contracted management companies, significant shareholders, directors, and key employees remain of good-standing throughout the concession, recognizing the impact on the concessionaire’s own suitability.
- Extends the verification processes (per a referenced paragraph three) to assess the good-standing of significant shareholders, management companies, and their directors and key employees.
- Clause 28 (Special duty of cooperation): Requires the concessionaire to provide any documents, information, or materials the Government deems necessary to verify suitability.
- Clause 29 (Special duty of notification): Requires notification to the DICJ within 15 days of becoming aware of:
  - Participation in, operation of, or cessation of gaming activities or licensing processes in other countries or regions by directors or shareholders holding 5% or more.
  - Investigations by foreign regulators that could punish, suspend, influence authorized gaming operations, or affect licensing or concessions.
- Introduces Chapter VI on Financial Capacity and Financing (no substantive provisions included in this excerpt).

nodes.title: Special duty of notification
nodes.heading:
Clause 29
Special duty of notification
nodes.start_phrase: The Conce ssionaire undertakes to notify DICJ within 15 days of becoming aware of the following situations concerning any of its directors or any of its shareholders who, directly or indirectly , hold 5% or more of its share capital:
nodes.summary:
- Continuous suitability and good-standing: The concessionaire must promptly inform DICJ of facts affecting the good-standing of shareholders owning 5% or more, directors, and key employees; ensure these parties and any contracted management companies remain of good-standing; and submit to verification processes for these persons/entities.
- Special duty of cooperation: Provide any documents, information, or materials the Government deems necessary to verify suitability.
- Special duty of notification: Within 15 days, notify DICJ of directors or ≥5% shareholders’ participation in foreign gaming licensing/operations or cessation thereof, and any investigations by foreign regulators that could affect gaming operations or licensing.
- Financial capacity: Maintain sufficient financial resources to operate the concession and meet all contractual and investment obligations (including annexed Investment Plans); accept continuous Government monitoring of the concessionaire and ≥5% shareholders; bear DICJ’s costs for financial standing verifications.
- Financing controls: Notify the Government of third-party loans or similar contracts over MOP 60,000,000, and obtain Secretary for Economy and Finance approval if over MOP 100,000,000; do not lend to directors, shareholders, or key employees without authorization; avoid transactions granting third parties management or intervention rights (e.g., step-in rights).
- Risk allocation: The concessionaire assumes full responsibility for all financing and financial-capacity risks; the Macau SAR bears no obligations or risks regarding the concessionaire’s financing.

nodes.title: Financial Capacity and Financing
nodes.heading:
CHAPTER VI
Financial Capacity and Financing
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionaire shall maintain the financial capacity to operate the concession, as well as to timely and fully comply with the obliga tions relating to any aspect of its activity , investments and obligatio ns that it is contractually bound to provide or has undertaken under this concession contract, in particular the Investment Plans annexed to this concession contract.
nodes.summary:
- Clause 30 (Financial capacity): The Concessionaire must maintain sufficient financial capacity to operate the concession and meet all contractual and investment obligations, including annexed Investment Plans. The Government will continuously monitor the Concessionaire and any shareholder with 5%+ equity. The Concessionaire must pay the costs of financial standing verifications as determined and documented by DICJ.

- Clause 31 (Loans and similar contracts): The Concessionaire must notify the Government of any third‑party loan/similar contract over MOP 60,000,000, and obtain authorization from the Secretary for Economy and Finance if over MOP 100,000,000. It may not lend to or enter similar contracts with its directors, shareholders, or key employees without the Secretary’s authorization. It is prohibited from transactions that give third parties management or intervention powers (e.g., step‑in rights).

- Clause 32 (Risk allocation): The Concessionaire bears full responsibility for all financing-related risks of the concession (subject to Clause 42). The Macau SAR assumes no obligations or risks regarding the Concessionaire’s financing.

nodes.title: Financial capacity of the Concessionaire
nodes.heading:
Clause 30
Financial capacity of the Concessionair e
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionaire shall maintain the financial capacity to operate the concession, as well as to timely and fully comply with the obliga tions relating to any aspect of its activity , investments and obligatio ns that it is contractually bound to provide or has undertaken under this concession contract, in particular the Investment Plans annexed to this concession contract.
nodes.summary:
- The concessionaire must maintain sufficient financial capacity to operate the concession and fulfill all contractual obligations, including investment plans.
- Continuous government monitoring applies to the concessionaire and any shareholder holding 5% or more of its capital; the concessionaire bears the verification costs as set and documented by DICJ.
- The concessionaire must notify the Government of any third-party loan or similar contract exceeding MOP 60,000,000, and obtain authorization from the Secretary for Economy and Finance if it exceeds MOP 100,000,000.
- Loans or similar contracts to directors, shareholders, or key employees require authorization from the Secretary for Economy and Finance.
- The concessionaire is prohibited from entering transactions that grant third parties management or intervention powers (e.g., step-in rights).
- The concessionaire assumes full responsibility and risk for financing; the Macau SAR bears no obligation or risk regarding the concessionaire’s financing (subject to Clause 42).

nodes.title: Loans and similar contracts
nodes.heading:
Clause 31
Loans and similar contracts
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionaire undertakes to notify the Government of any loan or similar contract with a third-party worth more than MOP 60,000,000 (sixty million patacas); if the value exceeds MOP 100,000,000 (one hundred million patacas), it must be authorized by the Secretary for Economy and Finance.
nodes.summary:
- Clause 30 (Financial capacity): The concessionaire must maintain sufficient financial capacity to operate the concession and meet all contractual obligations, especially the annexed Investment Plans. The Government will continuously monitor the concessionaire and any shareholder with 5%+ ownership. The concessionaire must pay the costs of financial standing verifications within the DICJ’s set timeframe; a DICJ-issued cost statement serves as proof.

- Clause 31 (Loans and similar contracts): The concessionaire must notify the Government of any third-party loan or similar contract exceeding MOP 60,000,000, and obtain authorization from the Secretary for Economy and Finance if it exceeds MOP 100,000,000. It may not grant loans or similar contracts to directors, shareholders, or key employees without the Secretary’s authorization. It is prohibited from entering into arrangements that give third parties management or intervention powers (including step-in rights).

- Clause 32 (Undertaking risks): The concessionaire assumes full and exclusive responsibility for all risks related to its financial capacity and financing under the concession (without prejudice to Clause 42). The Macau SAR bears no obligation, responsibility, or risk regarding the concessionaire’s financing.

nodes.title: Undertaking risks
nodes.heading:
Clause 32
Undertaking risks
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionair e expressly undertakes all obligations and full and exclusive responsibility for all risks inherent in the concession with respect to its financial capacity and its financing, without prejudice of Clause 42.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes the Concessionaire’s duty to maintain sufficient financial capacity to operate the concession and fulfill all contractual obligations, especially the agreed Investment Plans, with continuous government monitoring that also covers shareholders holding 5% or more.
- Requires the Concessionaire to bear the costs of government/DICJ financial capacity verifications, with DICJ-issued cost statements serving as proof.
- Imposes notification and authorization controls on financing: any third‑party loan or similar contract over MOP 60,000,000 must be notified to the Government; those exceeding MOP 100,000,000 require authorization by the Secretary for Economy and Finance.
- Prohibits loans or similar arrangements to directors, shareholders, or key employees without prior authorization, and forbids transactions granting third parties management or step‑in rights over the Concessionaire.
- Allocates all financing-related risks and obligations exclusively to the Concessionaire; Macau SAR assumes no responsibility for the Concessionaire’s financing (subject to a referenced exception in Clause 42).
- Obligates the Concessionaire to secure all necessary financing to meet its operational and investment commitments and bars it from invoking defenses against Macau SAR arising from its financing arrangements with third parties, including lenders and shareholders.
- Requires maintenance of legally mandated reserve funds.
- Establishes a special duty of cooperation: immediate provision of any documents/data the Government deems necessary to assess financial capacity; prompt notification of financing obligations of MOP 16,000,000 or more; submission of certified copies of related documents; and procurement of commitments from all controlling shareholders (including the ultimate controlling shareholder) to provide requested information and documents.

nodes.title: Securing of financing
nodes.heading:
Clause 33
Securing of financing
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionaire undertakes to secure the financing required to timely and fully comply with its obligations relating to any of its activity , inves tments and obligations it is contractually bound to make or has assumed under the terms of this concession contract, in particular the Investment Plans attached to this concession contract.
nodes.summary:
- Concessionaire must secure all financing needed to timely and fully meet its activities, investments, and contractual obligations, especially the attached Investment Plans.
- The Concessionaire cannot assert defenses against the Macau SAR based on its agreements with third parties (including lenders and its shareholders) related to obtaining such financing.
- Obligation to maintain legally required reserve funds.
- Special cooperation with the Government to demonstrate ongoing financial capacity, including:
  - Immediate provision of any documents, information, or data the Government deems necessary.
  - Prompt notification of any financing-related obligations (loans, mortgages, debt declarations, guarantees, etc.) of MOP 16,000,000 or more.
  - Submission of certified copies of documents for such financing obligations.
  - Obtaining statements from all controlling shareholders (including the ultimate controlling shareholder) binding them to these cooperation duties and to provide requested materials.

nodes.title: Reserve funds
nodes.heading:
Clause 34
Reserve funds
nodes.start_phrase: The Concessionaire undertakes to maintain the reserve funds required by law .
nodes.summary:
- Clause 33 (Securing of financing): The Concessionaire must obtain all financing necessary to meet its contractual obligations and investment plans on time and in full. It cannot invoke any exceptions or defenses against the Macau SAR based on its contracts with third parties (including lenders or its shareholders) used to obtain such financing.
- Clause 34 (Reserve funds): The Concessionaire must maintain all reserve funds required by law.
- Clause 35 (Special duty of cooperation): 
  - Must promptly provide the Government with any documents, information, or data needed to verify its ongoing financial capacity.
  - Must notify the Government as soon as possible of any loans, mortgages, guarantees, debt declarations, or similar obligations of MOP 16,000,000 (sixteen million patacas) or more related to any aspect of its activity.
  - Must promptly submit certified copies of documents for such financing arrangements.
  - Must obtain and submit statements from each controlling shareholder, including the ultimate controlling shareholder, agreeing to be bound by this cooperation duty and to provide any requested documents, information, authorizations, or evidence.

nodes.title: Special duty of cooperation
nodes.heading:
Clause 35
Special duty of cooperation
nodes.start_phrase: One. Without prejudice to the general duty of cooperation provided for in Clause 70, the Concessionaire undertakes to immediately make available to the Government any document, information or data which the Government considers necessary to verify that it continues to have adequate financial capacity .
nodes.summary:
- Clause 33 (Securing of financing): The Concessionaire must obtain all financing necessary to timely and fully meet its contractual obligations, including the attached Investment Plans. It cannot invoke defenses against the Macau SAR arising from its financing arrangements or relationships with third parties (e.g., lenders, shareholders).
- Clause 34 (Reserve funds): The Concessionaire must maintain all reserve funds required by law.
- Clause 35 (Special duty of cooperation): 
  - Must promptly provide any documents, information, or data the Government deems necessary to verify ongoing financial capacity.
  - Must notify the Government as soon as possible of any financing-related obligations (loans, mortgages, guarantees, debt declarations, etc.) of MOP 16,000,000 or more.
  - Must promptly submit certified copies of documents relating to such financing obligations.
  - Must obtain statements from each controlling shareholder, including the ultimate controlling shareholder, agreeing to be bound by this cooperation duty and to provide any requested documents, information, authorizations, or evidence.
- The excerpt ends at the heading for Chapter VII.

nodes.title: Investment Plans
nodes.heading:
CHAPTER VII
Investment Plans
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionaire undertakes to implement the Investment Plans annex ed to this concession contract, as well as the investment projects included in the awar d proposal submitted by the Concessionaire as a bidder in the public tender for the award of concession for the operation of games of fortune or chance in casinos, under the terms stated in the aforementioned Plans and award proposal.
nodes.summary: Insufficient information: the partial document text is empty, so the main points cannot be determined.

nodes.title: Investment Plans
nodes.heading:
Clause 36
Investment Plans
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionaire undertakes to implement the Investment Plans annex ed to this concession contract, as well as the investment projects included in the awar d proposal submitted by the Concessionaire as a bidder in the public tender for the award of concession for the operation of games of fortune or chance in casinos, under the terms stated in the aforementioned Plans and award proposal.
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Sets obligations and procedures for implementing the Investment Plans annexed to the casino operation concession, including projects pledged in the award proposal.
- Concessionaire’s duties:
  - Implement all listed projects using qualified labor.
  - Prioritize hiring Macau SAR–based companies and residents.
  - Comply with Macau SAR technical norms, regulations, official specifications, and manufacturer/patent instructions in design.
  - Submit construction projects to the Land and Urban Construction Bureau (DSSCU) with required documents and a works plan.
  - Execute works strictly per approved designs, applicable laws, international standards, and best trade practices.
  - Use certified, internationally recognized high-quality materials, systems, and equipment.
  - Maintain high international quality standards across all projects and commercial establishments.
  - Ensure modern, efficient, high-quality management.
  - Promptly notify the Government of any situations that may significantly affect construction or operations, including structural or other anomalies, via a detailed, reasoned report (with external expert input if needed) and proposed remedial measures.
- Liability: Concessionaire is liable to Macau SAR and third parties for losses from serious design, execution, maintenance, or operational deficiencies related to the Investment Plans.
- Government’s role: Commits to facilitating lawful execution of the listed projects.
- Project changes (Clause 37):
  - Government may request documents or impose changes to ensure compliance with technical standards and quality levels.
  - Government cannot impose changes that increase the overall investment amount specified in Clause 41.
- Execution and supervision (Clause 38):
  - By 30 September each year, the Concessionaire must submit for Government approval a plan of the specific projects to be executed in the following year, including project details, investment amounts, and execution deadlines.

nodes.title: Changes to the projects listed in the Investment Plans
nodes.heading:
Clause 37
Changes to the pr ojects listed in the Investment Plans
nodes.start_phrase: One. In the execution of the Investment Plans annexed to this concession contract, the Government may require any documents or impose changes regarding the execution of the listed projects to ensure complia nce with the standards, technical regulations in force and the level of the quality standards.
nodes.summary:
- Establish and maintain high international quality standards for commercial establishments and overall management within the concessionaire’s properties.
- Promptly notify the Government of any significant issues affecting construction or operations, including structural or other anomalies, via a detailed, reasoned report that may include input from recognized external experts and proposed/implemented corrective measures.
- Concessionaire liability to the Macau SAR and third parties for losses arising from serious deficiencies, errors, or omissions in project design, dimensioning, construction, maintenance, and operation related to the Investment Plans.
- Government commitment to facilitate the concessionaire’s lawful execution of the projects in the annexed Investment Plans.
- Clause 37: Government may request documents or impose changes to ensure compliance with current standards, technical regulations, and quality levels, but cannot require changes that increase the overall investment amount referenced in Clause 41.
- Clause 38: By 30 September each year, the concessionaire must submit for Government approval a proposal of the specific projects to be executed the following year, detailing each project, the investment amount, and the execution deadline.

nodes.title: Execution and supervision of the Investment Plans
nodes.heading:
Clause 38
Execution and supervision of the Investment Plans
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionaire undertakes to subm it to the Government, by 30 September of each year, a proposal for the implementation of the specific projects referred to in the Investment Plans annexed to this concession contract which it intends to execute in the following year, which shall include, at least, the details of the specific investment project it intends to execute in the following year, the amount of the investment, and the deadline for its execution – for the purposes of approval by the Government.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes the Concessionaire’s obligations to:
  - Maintain international quality standards in commercial establishments within its properties.
  - Ensure modern, efficient, high-quality management aligned with international standards.
  - Promptly notify the Government of any situation that significantly affects construction or operations, providing detailed, reasoned reports (including inputs from recognized external experts when appropriate) and outlining corrective measures.

- Sets Concessionaire liability to the Macau SAR and third parties for losses arising from serious deficiencies, errors, or omissions in project design, construction, maintenance, and operation related to the Investment Plans.

- Commits the Government to facilitate, in accordance with law, the Concessionaire’s execution of projects listed in the Investment Plans.

- Clause 37: Allows the Government to require documents or impose changes to projects in the Investment Plans to ensure compliance with technical standards, regulations, and quality levels, without increasing the overall investment amount stipulated in Clause 41.

- Clause 38: Defines execution and oversight of Investment Plans:
  - By 30 September each year, the Concessionaire must submit next year’s specific project proposals (content, investment amount, execution deadline) for Government approval.
  - Government decides within 60 days and may adjust content, amounts, and timelines by agreement to meet socio-economic needs.
  - In cases of force majeure or special circumstances not attributable to the Concessionaire, it may request amendments or partial/total suspension with detailed, documented justification.
  - By 31 March each year, the Concessionaire must report on the previous year’s implementation (status, invested amounts, deadlines, results) and provide any additional information requested.
  - If projects are not authorized due to legal/urban planning issues or public interest, earmarked funds must be redirected to related projects indicated and accepted by the Government.
  - Requires ongoing cooperation and provision of documents/information for monitoring.

- Clause 39: Assigns Government (via DSSCU) responsibility to monitor and supervise construction work for compliance with work plans and quality of materials, systems, and equipment under applicable legislation and the Investment Plans.

nodes.title: Supervision of construction work
nodes.heading:
Clause 39
Supervision of construction work
nodes.start_phrase: One. Through DSSCU, the Government shall monitor and supervise the execution of the construction work, namely its compliance with the plan of works and the quality of the materials, systems and equipme nt according to the applicable legislation as per the Investment Plans attached to this concession contract.
nodes.summary:
- Government approval of specific project proposals within 60 days, with possible adjustments to project scope, investment amount, and execution period by mutual agreement to match socio-economic needs.
- Force majeure/special circumstances not attributable to the Concessionaire: ability to request amendments to approved projects or partial/total suspension, supported by detailed reports and documentation.
- Annual reporting by 31 March on Investment Plans and approved specific projects: implementation status, invested amounts, deadlines, results, plus any additional information requested by the Government.
- If Investment Plans or specific projects are not authorized due to legal, planning, or public interest reasons, earmarked funds must be reallocated to activity-related projects indicated and accepted by the Government.
- Ongoing cooperation and submission of documents/information for Government monitoring of Investment Plan execution.
- Government (via DSSCU) supervision of construction works: compliance with approved plans, materials, systems, and equipment; bi-monthly detailed progress reports per Administrative Regulation No. 38/2022; extraordinary reports when progress is compromised; provision of all project documents and clarifications on request.
- Government may order additional quality tests; costs of tests and any defect repairs borne by the Concessionaire.
- Technical orders/notices may be directed to the project manager, who must diligently oversee works and be present on site when required.
- Authority to suspend/halt works for noncompliance; Government supervision does not create Macau SAR liability—Concessionaire remains solely responsible except where Government decisions cause issues.
- Contracting/subcontracting third parties does not relieve the Concessionaire of its legal or contractual obligations.
- Application of remaining funds after completion: if total expenditure is below the committed amount, the remainder must be spent on related projects accepted by the Government or on Government-designated projects of relevant public interest.
- Insurance obligations: maintain adequate insurance with Macau-authorized insurers (or abroad with Government authorization if necessary), including at least workplace accident/occupational illness, motor vehicle liability, civil liability for owned/leased ships and aircraft, and civil liability for installation of advertising materials.

nodes.title: Contracting and subcontracting
nodes.heading:
Clause 40
Contracting and subcontracting
nodes.start_phrase: The execution of the Investment Plans that involves hiring and subcontracting third parties does not exempt the Concessionaire from the legal or contractual obligations to which it is bound.

nodes.title: Application of the remaining funds of the Investment Plans
nodes.heading:
Clause 41
Application of the r emaining funds of the Investment Plans
nodes.start_phrase: If, upon completion of the execution of the Investment Plans annexed to this concession contract, the total value of the expenditure incurred by the Concessionaire, directly or, subject to Government authorization , indirectly , is less than the overall amount and value committed to at the time of activation of the constant investment increase mechanism in the award proposal submitted by the Concessionaire as a bidder in the publi c tender for the award of concessions for the operation of games of fortune or chance in casinos, the Concessionaire undertakes to spend the remaining amount on projects related to its activity , to be designated by the Concessionaire and accepted by the Government, or on projects of relevant public interest for the Macau SAR, to be designated by the Government.
nodes.summary:
- Assigns the Concessionaire sole responsibility for any defects in the design, execution, or operation of the works, except when caused by Government decisions.
- Clarifies that hiring or subcontracting third parties for Investment Plan execution does not relieve the Concessionaire of its legal or contractual obligations.
- Requires that any unspent funds from the Investment Plans (relative to the committed amount tied to the investment increase mechanism in the award proposal for casino gaming concessions) be redirected either to Concessionaire-proposed, Government-approved projects related to its activity or to Government-designated projects of public interest for the Macau SAR.
- Establishes insurance obligations: the Concessionaire must maintain comprehensive coverage for risks inherent to the concession, placing policies with Macau-authorized insurers or, if unfeasible/too onerous, with foreign insurers subject to Government authorization.
- Specifies mandatory insurance types: workplace accident and occupational disease; motor vehicle liability; civil liability for company-owned or leased ships/aircraft; and civil liability for installation of advertising materials.

nodes.title: Insurance
nodes.heading:
Clause 42
Insurance
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionaire is obligated to contract and maintain up-to-date insurance contracts necessary to guarantee effective and complete coverage for the risks inheren t in the development of the activities included in the concession.
nodes.summary:
- Concessionaire bears sole responsibility for design, execution, and operation defects, except those caused by Government decisions.
- Hiring or subcontracting third parties does not relieve the Concessionaire of its legal and contractual obligations.
- If actual spending on approved Investment Plans is below the committed amount, the remaining funds must be used for Concessionaire-related projects approved by the Government or for Government-designated public-interest projects in the Macau SAR.
- Mandatory insurance program:
  - Maintain adequate, up-to-date coverage with Macau-authorized insurers (or foreign insurers with Government authorization if local coverage is unfeasible/too onerous).
  - Required policies: workplace accident/occupational disease; motor vehicle liability; civil liability for ships/aircraft; civil liability for advertising installations; general civil liability for casino and other concession activities; multi-risk property damage; construction all-risks including civil liability.
  - Multi-risk property coverage must include fire/explosion; water damage; natural disasters (floods, typhoons, earthquakes, etc.); aircraft impact/falling objects; vehicle collision; theft/robbery; strikes/riots/public disorder.
  - Minimum limits: per law for the first four; Government-set for general civil liability based on business volume and prior-year accident index; net asset value for property (gross minus accumulated depreciation); construction project value for construction insurance.
  - Ensure contractors cover labor accidents/occupational diseases.
  - Provide policy copies to the Government upon issuance/renewal; do not start construction before submission.
  - No cancellation/suspension/modification/replacement without Government authorization (insurer changes require prompt notice).
  - Government may pay overdue premiums on the Concessionaire’s behalf using its compliance bond.
- Property obligations:
  - Conserve or replace Macau SAR assets used under the concession as instructed by the regulator (DICJ).
  - Conserve Government-managed land, soil, and natural resources allocated to the concession (via lease or concession).
  - Casinos must be located on property owned by the Concessionaire, subject to exceptions provided in Macau laws (Law No. 7/2022 and Law 16/2001).

nodes.title: Property
nodes.heading:
CHAPTER VIII
Property
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionaire undertakes to ensure the conservation or replacement, as instructed by DICJ, of the Macau SAR assets which have been or will be used in connection with the operation of the concession through the temporary transfer of its usufruct, fruition, and use.
nodes.summary:
- Insurance obligations: The concessionaire must ensure contractors carry insurance for labor accidents and occupational diseases; prove existence and validity of insurance to the Government by sending policy copies upon signing or renewal; not commence construction before providing those copies; not cancel, suspend, modify, or replace policies without Government authorization (except when changing insurer, with prompt notice); and the Government may pay premiums on the concessionaire’s behalf using the compliance bond if the concessionaire fails to pay.
- Macau SAR property: The concessionaire must conserve or replace Macau SAR assets used under the concession as directed by DICJ, and ensure conservation of government-managed land, soil, and natural resources allocated to the concession under the Basic Law.
- Casino property ownership: Casinos must be located on property owned by the concessionaire, subject to exceptions provided in Law No. 7/2022 and Law 16/2001 (Section 5(4) and Section 37).

nodes.title: Macau SAR Property
nodes.heading:
Clause 43
Macau SAR Pr operty
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionaire undertakes to ensure the conservation or replacement, as instructed by DICJ, of the Macau SAR assets which have been or will be used in connection with the operation of the concession through the temporary transfer of its usufruct, fruition, and use.
nodes.summary:
- Insurance obligations:
  - Sets the insurable value of construction work (referencing subparagraph 7).
  - Concessionaire must require its contracting entities to insure against labor accidents and occupational diseases.
  - Must prove to the Government that insurance policies exist and are valid by sending copies upon initial signing and renewal.
  - May not commence any construction until the Government has received the policy copies.
  - May not cancel, suspend, modify, or replace insurance without Government authorization, except when changing insurers, in which case the Government must be informed promptly.
  - If the Concessionaire fails to pay premiums, the Government may pay them directly using the Concessionaire’s compliance bond.

- Property obligations (Chapter VIII):
  - Concessionaire must conserve or replace Macau SAR assets used in the concession (via temporary usufruct/fruition/use) as instructed by DICJ.
  - Must ensure conservation of land, soil, and natural resources under Government responsibility (per Section 7 of the Macau SAR Basic Law) allocated to the concession, whether by lease or concession.
  - Casinos must be located on property owned by the Concessionaire, subject to exceptions in Section 5 of Law 7/2022 and Sections 5(4) and 37 of Law 16/2001.

nodes.title: Other property
nodes.heading:
Clause 44
Other property
nodes.start_phrase: One. Casinos shall be required to be located on property owned by the Concessionaire, except as prescribed in Section 5 of Law No. 7/2022 and Section 5 (4) and Section 37 of Law 16/2001.
nodes.summary:
- Insurance obligations:
  - Concessionaire must ensure contractors/partners have coverage for labor accidents and occupational diseases.
  - Must provide the Government copies of all insurance policies upon issuance and renewal, and may not begin construction before doing so.
  - May not cancel, suspend, modify, or replace insurance without Government authorization; insurer changes are allowed with prompt Government notification.
  - Government may pay overdue premiums on the Concessionaire’s behalf using the compliance bond if the Concessionaire defaults.
  - References insurance tied to construction work values.

- Property and asset management:
  - Concessionaire must conserve or replace Macau SAR assets used under temporary usufruct, as directed by DICJ.
  - Must conserve Government-managed land, soil, and natural resources allocated to the concession (per Basic Law Section 7).
  - Casinos must be on property owned by the Concessionaire, except where specific laws allow otherwise.
  - Casinos, gaming equipment, and utensils cannot be encumbered without Government approval; at concession end they must be free of encumbrances.
  - New casinos must be in strata-titled buildings/complexes, operated as clearly delimited autonomous units.
  - Must submit property registry certificates, building by-laws, and floor plans; register ownership changes to autonomous units and send certificates via DSF.
  - Must submit condominium (horizontal property) regulations for Government approval.

- Reversion on termination:
  - On termination or extinction, casinos and allocated gaming equipment/utensils (even if off-premises) revert automatically and free of charge to Macau SAR, except items under temporary transfer per Clause 49.
  - Assets must be delivered in good repair, allowing for normal wear and tear.
  - A public deed record serves as the transfer title, even if underlying land concession is provisional.
  - If the Concessionaire fails to hand over, the Government may take immediate administrative possession.

nodes.title: Reversion of the casinos and gaming equipment and utensils
nodes.heading:
Clause 45
Reversion of the casinos and gaming equipment and utensils
nodes.start_phrase: One. Upon termination or extinction of the concession, the casinos, as well as the gaming equipment and utensils allocated, even if located outside their premises, will revert gratuitously and automatically to the Macau SAR, with the exception of the casinos, equipment and utensils allocated to games whose use and fruition have been temporarily transferred to the Concessionaire under the terms of Clause 49.
nodes.summary:
- Restrictions on encumbrances: The Concessionaire may not encumber casinos, gaming equipment, or utensils without Government authorization; at concession expiry all such assets must be free of liens or encumbrances.
- Location and property structuring for new casinos: New casinos must be situated in buildings or building complexes under strata (horizontal) property, operated as clearly identified autonomous units with delimited areas.
- Property documentation and approvals: The Concessionaire must submit Property Registry certificates, building by-laws, and floor plans; register any changes to autonomous unit ownership and send updated land registry certificates via DSF; and submit condominium regulations for Government approval.
- Reversion of assets: On termination or extinction of the concession, casinos and allocated gaming equipment/utensils (including those outside casino premises) revert automatically and free of charge to the Macau SAR, except assets temporarily transferred under Clause 49.
- Condition on handover: Assets must be delivered in perfect repair and operating condition, allowing for normal wear and tear; normal renewal of gaming equipment/utensils is unaffected.
- Transfer formalities: A public deed record serves as the title for registration upon reversion, even if the land concession is provisional.
- Enforcement on failure to deliver: Government may immediately take administrative possession if the Concessionaire fails to hand over; related expenses may be covered by the performance bond.
- Inspection: DICJ will inspect properties covered by Clauses 43 and 44 prior to reversion, with a report and the Concessionaire’s representatives allowed to attend.
- Protection during dissolution/liquidation: Properties may not be divided until Government certifies via compulsory inventory that revertible assets are in proper condition or that sums due to Macau SAR are secured by acceptable guarantees.
- Inventory obligations: The Concessionaire must keep a triplicate, up-to-date inventory of SAR-owned and revertible properties/rights; submit annual updates to DICJ and DSF by May 31; complete the inventory 90 days before concession end; and, upon early termination, finalize it on a Government-set date.
- Improvements: Any improvements made to properties under Clause 43 or to revertible properties confer no right to compensation and need not be removed.
- Land use regime: The regime for land concessions used by the Concessionaire, including for operations, is governed by the separate land concession contract.

nodes.title: Inventory of the assets allocated to the concession
nodes.heading:
Clause 46
Inventory of the assets allocated to the concession
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionaire undertakes to prepare in triplicate and maintain updated the inventory of all properties and rights belonging to the Macau SAR and allocated to the concession, as well as all properties revertible to the Macau SAR, submitting for that effect, by 31 May of each year , an annual update of the maps showing all alterations to DICJ and DSF .
nodes.summary:
- Expenses related to compliance with the Concessionaire’s legal or contractual obligations are covered by a bond.
- DICJ will inspect properties referenced in Clauses 43 and 44 to verify their conservation and maintenance, with an inspection report and the Concessionaire’s representatives allowed to attend.
- In the event of dissolution or liquidation, properties may not be divided until the Government, via a compulsory inventory, certifies revertible assets are in perfect condition or any sums owed to the Macau SAR are secured by an acceptable guarantee.
- Normal renewal of allocated gaming equipment and utensils is not affected.
- Inventory obligations: the Concessionaire must keep a triplicate, continuously updated inventory of Macau SAR-owned and revertible assets allocated to the concession; submit annual updates by 31 May to DICJ and DSF; complete the inventory at least 90 days before concession expiry; and, upon early termination, complete it on a Government-set date.
- Improvements made to assets under Clause 43 and to revertible assets grant no compensation or indemnity and need not be removed.
- Land use by the Concessionaire is governed by the terms of the separate land concession contract.

nodes.title: Improvements
nodes.heading:
Clause 47
Impr ovements
nodes.start_phrase: The improvements that, for any reason, are made to the properties referred to in Clause 43, as well as to properties that are revertible to the Grantor , do not entitle the Concessionaire to any compensation or indemnity and do not need to be removed.
nodes.summary:
- DICJ will inspect properties allocated to the concession (Clauses 43 and 44), with Concessionaire representatives allowed to attend; an inspection report will be issued. Related expenses are covered by the Concessionaire’s compliance bond.
- In case of dissolution or liquidation, assets cannot be divided until the Government certifies via a compulsory inventory that revertible assets are in perfect condition and operation, or until any amounts owed to the Macau SAR are secured by an acceptable guarantee.
- Normal renovation of allocated gaming equipment and utensils is not restricted by the above.
- The Concessionaire must keep, in triplicate, an up-to-date inventory of SAR-owned and revertible assets allocated to the concession; submit annual updates by May 31 to DICJ and DSF; complete the inventory 90 days before concession expiry; and, upon early termination, complete it on a Government-set date.
- Improvements to SAR/revertible properties give no right to compensation and need not be removed.
- Land use for concession operations is governed by a separate land concession contract.

nodes.title: Concession of land to be used by the Concessionaire
nodes.heading:
Clause 48
Concession of land to be used by the Concessionair e
nodes.start_phrase: One. The regime governing the concession of land to be used by the Concessionaire, namely for the concession operation, is stipulated in the respective land concession contract.
nodes.summary:
- DICJ will inspect the properties covered by Clauses 43 and 44, with Concessionaire representatives allowed to attend, and issue an inspection report; related expenses are secured by the Concessionaire’s performance bond.
- In the event of dissolution or liquidation, assets cannot be divided until the Government, via a compulsory inventory, certifies revertible assets are in perfect condition or that any sums owed to the Macau SAR are secured/paid; routine renewal of allocated gaming equipment and utensils is unaffected.
- The Concessionaire must keep, in triplicate, an up-to-date inventory of state-owned and revertible assets allocated to the concession, submitting annual updates by 31 May to DICJ and DSF; the inventory must be finalized 90 days before the concession ends, or on a date set by the Government if it terminates earlier.
- Improvements made to government or revertible properties confer no right to compensation and need not be removed.
- Land use by the Concessionaire is governed by a separate land concession contract, which is subject to applicable provisions of the main concession contract.
- Under Law No. 16/2001 (Sections 37–39), the Government temporarily transfers, via deed of surrender, the casinos “MGM Casino Macau” and “MGM Casino Cotai,” and the usufruct/use of related gaming equipment and utensils, for concession operations; these assets revert to the Macau SAR.
- The temporary transfer ends if the concession is rescinded or extinguished; the Concessionaire must return casinos and listed equipment free of liens, per a DICJ-approved inventory.
- The Government may require demolition of conservation works/improvements or restoration of casinos to their original condition within a set period; all costs are borne by the Concessionaire, and if it fails to act, the Government will do so at the Concessionaire’s expense, with no indemnity for demolished works.
- The Concessionaire may change the purpose of functional zones in the casinos with prior Government authorization.
- The Concessionaire must pay the agreed amount for the usufruct/use per Section 39 of Law No. 16/2001, with a proportional refund if the concession ends before the end of the calendar year.

nodes.title: Assets necessary for the operation of the concession
nodes.heading:
Clause 49
Assets necessary for the operation of the concession
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Parties shall comply with the provisions of Sections 37 to 39 of Law No. 16/2001, whereby the Government, through the deed of surrender , temporarily transfer s to the Concessionaire the following casinos that will revert to the Macau SAR on 31 December 2022, as well as the usufruct, fruition and use of gaming equipment and utensils, listed in the inventory accompanying the deed of surrender , for the purpose of operating games of fortune or chance in a casino, whose concession is granted to the Concessionaire under this contract:
nodes.summary:
- Land concession contract between the Government and the Concessionaire is governed, where applicable, by this concession contract.
- Government temporarily transfers to the Concessionaire, via deed of surrender, the casinos “MGM Casino Macau” and “MGM Casino Cotai,” along with the usufruct, fruition, and use of listed gaming equipment/utensils, all reverting to the Macau SAR on 31 December 2022.
- The temporary usufruct ends upon rescission or extinction of the gaming concession; the Concessionaire must return casinos and equipment free of liens/encumbrances per the DICJ-approved inventory.
- Government may require demolition of conservation works/improvements or restoration to original condition at the Concessionaire’s expense; if not complied with, the Government will execute demolition, with all costs borne by the Concessionaire and no compensation due.
- The Concessionaire may alter casino functional zones with prior Government authorization.
- The Concessionaire must pay for the usufruct pursuant to Section 39 of Law No. 16/2001 and may recover a proportional amount if the concession ends before year-end.
- The Concessionaire assumes all civil/other liabilities arising from the temporary use; the Macau SAR assumes none.
- The Concessionaire may perform maintenance, repairs, and improvements without Government authorization and at its own cost, with no right to compensation.
- Unusable/unfit gaming equipment/utensils must be decommissioned or destroyed with DICJ authorization, with no compensation.
- Premium obligations: an annual premium is due to the Macau SAR, comprising a fixed part of MOP 30,000,000 per year (per Chief Executive Order No. 215/2001) and a variable part based on the number of gaming tables and machines; specified rates include MOP 300,000 per reserved table (e.g., special rooms/areas) and MOP 150,000 per non-reserved table.

nodes.title: Premium
nodes.heading:
CHAPTER IX
Premium
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Conce ssionaire undertakes to pay an annual premium to the Macau SAR while the concession is in force, as consideration for the operation of the games of fortune or chance in a casino.
nodes.summary:
- Allocation and liability for casino equipment and utensils: the Concessionaire assumes all civil and other liabilities arising from their temporary use; the Macau SAR bears no liability.
- Maintenance and improvements: the Concessionaire may perform maintenance, repairs, and improvements to casinos and allocated equipment without prior government authorization, at its own cost and with no right to government compensation.
- Disposal of unusable equipment: when equipment becomes useless or unfit, the Concessionaire must remove from use or destroy it with DICJ authorization, with no right to compensation.
- Premium obligations (Chapter IX, Clause 50): the Concessionaire must pay an annual premium to the Macau SAR for operating casino games, consisting of fixed and variable components.
- Fixed premium: MOP 30,000,000 per year (per Chief Executive Order No. 215/2001).
- Variable premium: calculated based on the number of gaming tables and machines; rates specified for tables include MOP 300,000 per year for each reserved table (special rooms/areas) and MOP 150,000 per year for each non-reserved table.

nodes.title: Premium
nodes.heading:
Clause 50
Premium
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Conce ssionaire undertakes to pay an annual premium to the Macau SAR while the concession is in force, as consideration for the operation of the games of fortune or chance in a casino.
nodes.summary:
- Allocation and liability for gaming equipment: The concessionaire assumes all civil and other liability arising from the temporary use of casino equipment and utensils; the Macau SAR bears no liability.
- Equipment management: The concessionaire may perform maintenance, repairs, and improvements to casinos and gaming equipment without prior government authorization, at its own cost and with no right to government compensation.
- Disposal of unusable equipment: When gaming equipment/utensils are useless or unfit, the concessionaire must decommission or destroy them with DICJ authorization, with no right to compensation.
- Premium obligations (Chapter IX, Clause 50):
  - An annual premium is due to the Macau SAR for operating casino games, composed of fixed and variable parts.
  - Fixed part: MOP 30,000,000 per year (per Chief Executive Order No. 215/2001).
  - Variable part based on assets operated:
    - MOP 300,000/year per reserved gaming table (e.g., special rooms/areas).
    - MOP 150,000/year per non-reserved gaming table.
    - MOP 1,000/year per electrical or mechanical gambling machine, including slot machines.
  - Minimum variable premium applies regardless of actual operations: at least the amount corresponding to 500 tables and 1,000 machines.
  - Payment terms:
    - Fixed part due by January 10 each year (government may allow monthly installments).
    - Variable part paid monthly by the 10th of the following month, calculated by the number of days each table and machine operated in the prior month.
    - Payments are settled via DSF payment slip.
  - Special premium: If the situation in Section 20(4) of Law No. 16/2001 occurs, the concessionaire must pay a special premium per that law, with analogous payment timing and DSF procedures.
- Contributions (Chapter X, Clause 51): The concessionaire must pay the contribution under Section 22(1)(2) of Law No. 16/2001 monthly by the 10th of the following month via DSF payment slip.

nodes.title: Contributions under Section 22 (1) subparagraphs 2) and 3) of Law No. 16/2001
nodes.heading:
CHAPTER X
Contributions under Section 22 (1) subparagraphs 2) and 3) of Law No. 16/2001
