nodes.start_phrase: One. By law, the Conce ssionaire shall pay the Macau SAR the contribution foresee n in Section 22 (1) subparagraph 2) of Law No. 16/2001.
nodes.summary:
- Sets payment obligations for a gaming concessionaire, including an annual premium with fixed and variable parts.
- Requires MOP 1,000 per year for each electrical or mechanical gambling machine, including slot machines.
- Establishes a minimum variable premium calculated as if at least 500 gaming tables and 1,000 gaming machines were operated, regardless of actual numbers.
- Fixed part of the annual premium is due by 10 January each year; the Government may allow monthly installments.
- Variable part is payable monthly by the 10th of the following month, based on the number of days each table and machine was operated in the prior month.
- Payments are settled via DSF using the respective payment slips.
- Imposes a special premium when triggered under Section 20(4) of Law No. 16/2001, applying referenced procedural provisions with necessary adaptations.
- Confirms the legal obligation to pay the contribution under Section 22(1)(2) of Law No. 16/2001 to the Macau SAR, due monthly by the 10th via DSF.

nodes.title: Contributions under Section 22 (1) subparagraph 2) of Law No. 16/2001
nodes.heading:
Clause 51
Contributions under Section 22 (1) subparagraph 2) of Law No. 16/2001
nodes.start_phrase: One. By law, the Conce ssionaire shall pay the Macau SAR the contribution foresee n in Section 22 (1) subparagraph 2) of Law No. 16/2001.
nodes.summary:
- Sets a fee of MOP 1,000 per year for each electrical or mechanical gambling machine, including slot machines.
- Establishes a minimum variable annual premium equivalent to operating 500 gaming tables and 1,000 gaming machines, regardless of actual numbers operated.
- Requires payment of the fixed part of the annual premium by January 10 each year, with the Government able to allow monthly installments.
- Requires monthly payment of the variable part by the 10th day of the following month, based on tables and machines operated in the prior month.
- Specifies that the variable component is calculated by counting the number of days each table and machine was operated during the month.
- States that annual premium payments are made via payment slip at DSF.
- Mandates payment of a special premium in cases under Section 20(4) of Law No. 16/2001, following Section 20(4)–(8), with adapted application of the payment provisions.
- Introduces Chapter X on contributions under Section 22(1)(2) and (3) of Law No. 16/2001.
- Clause 51: Confirms the legal obligation to pay the contribution under Section 22(1)(2) monthly by the 10th of the following month via DSF payment slip.

nodes.title: Contributions under Section 22 (1) subparagraph 3) of Law No. 16/2001
nodes.heading:
Clause 52
Contributions under Section 22 (1) subparagraph 3) of Law No. 16/2001
nodes.start_phrase: One. By law, the Concessionaire shall pay the Macau SAR the contribution foreseen in Section 22 (1) subparagraph 3) of Law No. 16/2001.
nodes.summary:
- Annual premium obligations:
  - MOP 1,000 per year for each electrical or mechanical gambling machine, including slot machines.
  - Variable premium has a floor equal to operating 500 gaming tables and 1,000 gaming machines, regardless of actual numbers.
  - Fixed part due by January 10 each year; government may allow monthly installments.
  - Variable part due monthly by the 10th for the prior month, calculated by the number of days each table/machine operated.
  - Premium payments are settled via DSF (Macau Financial Services Bureau).

- Special premium under Law No. 16/2001, Section 20(4):
  - Concessionaire must pay the special premium per paragraphs 4–8 of that Section, with payment timing and DSF settlement aligned to the annual premium provisions.

- Contributions under Law No. 16/2001, Section 22(1):
  - Subparagraph 2: Payable monthly by the 10th via DSF; accounted for as a separate Macau SAR budget entry.
  - Subparagraph 3: Same monthly payment and budget entry requirements; Government may designate beneficiary projects/entities.
    - Government and Concessionaire may agree to allocate funds to projects/entities up to half of the calculated contribution; direct payments by the Concessionaire reduce the DSF amount correspondingly.

- Special tax on gambling:
  - Payable monthly by the 10th of the following month.
  - May be paid in patacas or another currency accepted by the Government; if in patacas, payment is made directly at DSF.

nodes.title: Tax obligations and the submission of documents
nodes.heading:
CHAPTER XI
Tax obligations and the submission of documents
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionaire undertakes to pay the Macau SAR the legally stipulated special tax on gambling, which shall be paid monthly to the government by the tenth day of the following month to which it relates .
nodes.summary:
- Establishes fiscal obligations of the gambling Concessionaire to the Macau SAR, focusing on mandated contributions and special gambling tax.
- Clause 52: Requires the Concessionaire to pay the contribution under Section 22(1)(3) of Law No. 16/2001 monthly by the 10th day of the following month via DSF, with the contribution recorded as a separate budget entry.
- Allows the Government to designate projects or entities to receive part of the contribution; the Government and Concessionaire may agree to allocate up to 50% of the contribution to such projects/entities.
- Permits the Concessionaire to pay agreed project/entity allocations directly, with a corresponding reduction in the amount remitted to DSF.
- Clause 53: Obligates monthly payment of the legally stipulated special tax on gambling by the 10th day of the following month.
- The special tax can be paid in patacas or another Government-accepted currency; if in patacas, payment is made directly at DSF.

nodes.title: Special tax on gambling
nodes.heading:
Clause 53
Special tax on gambling
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionaire undertakes to pay the Macau SAR the legally stipulated special tax on gambling, which shall be paid monthly to the government by the tenth day of the following month to which it relates .
nodes.summary:
- Establishes the Concessionaire’s obligation to pay the contribution under Law No. 16/2001, Section 22(1)(3), monthly by the 10th of the following month via DSF, with the amount recorded as a separate Macau SAR budget entry.
- Allows the Government to designate projects/entities to receive part of this contribution and permits Government–Concessionaire agreements to allocate up to 50% of the amount to agreed projects/entities; direct payments to such beneficiaries reduce the DSF remittance accordingly.
- Chapter XI sets out tax obligations and document submission requirements:
  - Special gaming tax: payable monthly by the 10th; can be paid in patacas directly to DSF or in an accepted foreign currency via the Monetary Authority of Macau, which converts and credits DSF.
  - Withholding taxes: definitive withholding and monthly remittance to DSF of tax on junket commissions and the legally required professional tax on employees.
  - Payment of all other applicable taxes, contributions, duties, fees, and emoluments not exempt under Macau SAR law.
  - Annual compliance by March 31: submission to DICJ of a DSF certificate showing no outstanding tax/contribution debts (including fines, surcharges, compensatory/default interest), plus tax status documents for the prior year for the managing director, corporate body members, key employees, and shareholders with 5% or more equity.
  - Annual submission to DICJ by March 31 of a Social Security Fund certificate confirming contributions are up to date.
- Clause 58 (Provision of information) is introduced but its content is not included in the excerpt.

nodes.title: Withholding taxes
nodes.heading:
Clause 54
Withholding taxes
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionaire undertakes to withhold, on a definitive basis, the legally required tax on commissions paid to junkets, remitting the respective amounts monthly to DSF by the tenth day of the following month.
nodes.summary:
- Procedure for paying special gaming tax in non-pataca currencies: payments must be made by delivering the accepted currency to the Monetary Authority of Macau, which converts/makes the equivalent amount available in patacas to the Financial Services Bureau (DSF).
- Withholding obligations:
  - Definitive withholding of legally required tax on commissions paid to junkets, with monthly remittance to DSF by the 10th of the following month.
  - Definitive withholding of the legally stipulated professional tax for employees, with monthly remittance to DSF under applicable rules.
- Obligation to pay all other taxes, contributions, duties, fees, and emoluments due under Macau SAR law, unless exempt.
- Annual compliance documentation to DICJ by 31 March:
  - Certificate from DSF for the previous fiscal year proving no outstanding debts to Macau SAR for taxes, contributions, fines, surcharges, compensatory/default interest, and 3% charges.
  - Tax status documentation for the previous tax year for the managing director, corporate body members, key employees, and shareholders holding 5% or more.
- Annual proof of Social Security compliance: document from the Social Security Fund, by 31 March, confirming contributions are up to date.
- An upcoming clause on the provision of information is indicated but not fully included in the excerpt.

nodes.title: Payment of other taxes, contributions, fees or, emoluments due
nodes.heading:
Clause 55
Payment of other taxes, contributions, fees or , emoluments due
nodes.start_phrase: The Concessionaire undertakes to pay other taxes, contributions, duties, or emoluments due and stipulated in the legislation of the Macau SAR and from which payment is not exempted.
nodes.summary:
- Payment of special gaming tax in non-pataca currencies: if paid in a government-accepted currency, the Concessionaire must deliver it to the Monetary Authority of Macau, which will provide the equivalent in patacas to DSF.
- Withholding obligations:
  - Definitive withholding of legally required tax on commissions paid to junkets; monthly remittance to DSF by the 10th of the following month.
  - Definitive withholding of legally stipulated professional tax for employees; monthly remittance to DSF under applicable rules.
- Obligation to pay all other applicable taxes, contributions, duties, and emoluments under Macau SAR law where no exemption applies.
- Annual compliance documentation due to DICJ by March 31:
  - DSF certificate for the prior fiscal year proving no debts to the Macau SAR for taxes, contributions, fines, surcharges, and related interest.
  - Document stating the prior tax year status of the managing director, corporate body members, key employees, and shareholders holding 5% or more of share capital.
  - Social Security Fund document proving social security contributions are in order.
- Clause 58 (Provision of information) is introduced but its content is not included in the excerpt.

nodes.title: Document proving the inexistence of debts owing to the Macau SAR
nodes.heading:
Clause 56
Document pr oving the inexistence of debts owing to the Macau SAR
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionair e is obligated to deliver to DICJ, by 31 of March each year, a certificate issued by DSF regarding the previous fiscal year proving that the Concessionaire is not in debt to the Macau SAR for contributions and taxes, fines or surchar ges, including compensatory and default interest and 3% of debts.
nodes.summary:
- Procedures for paying the special gaming tax when made in a government‑accepted currency: payment is delivered to the Monetary Authority of Macau, which makes the equivalent amount available in patacas to DSF.
- Withholding obligations: the Concessionaire must withhold and definitively remit (by the 10th of the following month) taxes on commissions paid to junkets and the legally stipulated professional tax on employees, sending payments to DSF under applicable rules.
- Commitment to pay all other applicable taxes, contributions, duties, fees, or emoluments under Macau SAR law, unless exempt.
- Annual compliance reporting to DICJ by 31 March:
  - Certificate from DSF for the prior fiscal year proving no debts to the Macau SAR for taxes, contributions, fines, surcharges, and related interest.
  - Document stating the prior tax year status of the managing director, corporate body members, key employees, and shareholders holding 5% or more of share capital.
- Annual proof to DICJ by 31 March from the Social Security Fund that the Concessionaire’s social security contributions are in order.
- Clause 58 heading indicates forthcoming requirements on the provision of information (content not included in this excerpt).

nodes.title: Document proving the inexistence of debts to the Social Security of the Macau SAR
nodes.heading:
Clause 57
Document pr oving the inexistence of debts to the Social Security of the Macau SAR
nodes.start_phrase: The Concessionaire is obliged to deliver to DICJ, by 31 of March each year, a document issued by the Social Security Fund proving the Concessionaire has in order its contributions to the Social Security of the Macau SAR .
nodes.summary:
- Specifies that when the special gaming tax is paid in a government-accepted foreign currency, payment is made to the Monetary Authority of Macau, which credits the equivalent in patacas to DSF.
- Establishes withholding obligations: the Concessionaire must definitively withhold taxes on junket commissions and remit them monthly to DSF by the 10th of the following month; and must withhold legally required professional tax from employees and remit monthly to DSF per legal rules.
- Requires payment of all other taxes, contributions, duties, and emoluments due under Macau SAR law unless exempt.
- Mandates annual compliance submissions to DICJ by March 31: a DSF certificate showing no debts to the Macau SAR for taxes, contributions, fines, surcharges, and related interest; and a document reporting the prior-year tax status of the managing director, corporate body members, key employees, and shareholders holding 5% or more.
- Requires annual proof, by March 31, from the Social Security Fund that the Concessionaire’s social security contributions are in order, to be delivered to DICJ.
- Indicates an upcoming clause on the provision of information (Clause 58), content not included in the excerpt.

nodes.title: Provision of informationst st st
nodes.heading:
Clause 58
Provision of informationst
st
st
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionaire undertakes to send quarterly to the Government, by the last day of the month following the relevant quarter , its balance sheet for the previous quarter , with the exception of that relativ e to the last quarter of each year, which must be submitted by the last day of February of the following year .
nodes.summary:
- Specifies that if the special gaming tax is paid in a government-accepted foreign currency, it must be delivered to the Monetary Authority of Macau, which will make the equivalent in patacas available to the Financial Services Bureau (DSF).
- Clause 54 (Withholding taxes): Requires the Concessionaire to withhold and remit, on a definitive basis, (i) taxes on commissions paid to junkets by the 10th of the following month, and (ii) professional tax for its employees, remitted monthly under applicable law.
- Clause 55 (Other fiscal obligations): Mandates payment of all other taxes, contributions, duties, fees, and emoluments due under Macau SAR law unless exempt.
- Clause 56 (No-debt certification to Macau SAR): By March 31 each year, the Concessionaire must submit to DICJ a DSF certificate for the prior fiscal year proving no outstanding taxes, contributions, fines, surcharges, or interest; and provide tax status documents for its managing director, board members, key employees, and shareholders holding 5% or more.
- Clause 57 (Social Security compliance): By March 31 each year, submit to DICJ a Social Security Fund certificate confirming contributions are in order.
- Clause 58 (Provision of information): Submit quarterly balance sheets by the last day of the month after each quarter (Q4 by the last day of February). At least 30 days before the AGM, provide prior-year accounting and statistical statements, full names of management/supervisory board members, proxies, and head of accounting, and the directors’ report and accounts with supervisory and external accountants’ opinions.
- Clause 59 (Accounting and internal audit): Maintain sound accounting with appropriate internal controls; follow Government/DICJ/DSF guidelines; apply Macau Financial Reporting Standards; the Chief Executive may require specific ledgers, documents, accounting criteria, and special presentation norms.
- Clause 60 (External audit): Annual audit by an independent, internationally recognized auditor approved by DICJ and DSF, with provision of all necessary documents, including those referenced in Law No. 16/2001, Section 34.
- Clause 61 (Extraordinary audits): Introduces the topic of extraordinary audits (details not included in the excerpt).

nodes.title: Accounting and internal Audit
nodes.heading:
Clause 59
Accounting and internal Audit
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionaire undertakes to have its own well-managed accounting system with appropriate internal control procedures and to comply with the guidelines issued by the Government in this regard, namely through DICJ or DFS.
nodes.summary:
- Regular financial reporting: The Concessionaire must submit quarterly balance sheets to the Government by the last day of the month following each quarter, with the last quarter’s report due by the last day of February of the following year.
- Pre-AGM submissions: At least 30 days before the annual general meeting, the Concessionaire must provide (1) accounting and statistical statements for the previous financial year; (2) full names (in all variants) of members of management and supervisory boards, appointed proxies, and the head of accounting; (3) the board of directors’ report and accounts, with opinions from the supervisory board and external qualified accountants.
- Accounting and internal control: The Concessionaire must maintain a well-managed accounting system with appropriate internal controls and follow Government guidelines (via DICJ or DSF). It must use Macau SAR Financial Reporting Standards, and the Chief Executive may require specific ledgers, documents, accounting criteria, and special norms.
- External audit: Annual audits must be conducted by an independent, internationally recognized auditor approved by DICJ and DSF, with all necessary documents provided, including those referred to in Section 34 of Law No. 16/2001.
- Extraordinary audits: Clause referenced, indicating the possibility of extraordinary audits, though details are not included in the excerpt.

nodes.title: External audit of annual accounts
nodes.heading:
Clause 60
External audit of annual accounts
nodes.start_phrase: The Concessionaire undertakes to have its accounts annually audited by an external independent entity of recognized high international standards previously accepted by DICJ and DSF, providing in advance all the documents necessary , namely those referred to in Section 34 of the Law No. 16/2001.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes the Concessionaire’s periodic reporting duties to the Government: quarterly balance sheets due by the last day of the month following each quarter, with the fourth quarter due by the last day of February of the following year.
- Requires pre-AGM submissions at least 30 days before the annual accounts approval meeting: prior fiscal year accounting and statistical statements; full names (in all variants) of members of the management and supervisory boards, appointed proxies, and the head of accounting; and the board of directors’ report and accounts with the supervisory board’s opinions and those of external qualified accountants.
- Mandates a well-managed accounting system with appropriate internal controls and compliance with Government guidelines via DICJ or DSF.
- Requires the use of Macau SAR Financial Reporting Standards; allows the Chief Executive, upon DICJ/DSF proposal, to impose additional ledgers/documents, set accounting criteria, and require special norms for compilation and presentation.
- Obligates annual external audits by an independent, internationally recognized auditor pre-approved by DICJ and DSF, with advance provision of necessary documents, including those referenced in Law No. 16/2001, Section 34.
- Introduces Clause 61 on extraordinary audits (details not provided in the excerpt).

nodes.title: Extraordinary audits
nodes.heading:
Clause 61
Extraordinary audits
nodes.start_phrase: The Concessionaire agrees, at any time, with or without prior notice, to be audited by an independent external entity of recognized international standards, or by another entity , whenever DICJ or DSF deem it necessary or convenient.
nodes.summary:
- Periodic financial reporting: quarterly balance sheets to the Government by the end of the month following each quarter (Q4 by end of February); at least 30 days before the AGM, submit prior-year accounting/statistical statements, full names of management and supervisory board members, proxies and head of accounting, and the directors’ report and accounts with supervisory board and external accountants’ opinions.
- Accounting and internal audit: maintain a well-managed accounting system with appropriate internal controls; follow Government guidance via DICJ/DSF; adopt Macau SAR Financial Reporting Standards; the Chief Executive may mandate specific ledgers, documents, accounting criteria, and special norms.
- External audits: annual audit by an independent, internationally recognized auditor approved by DICJ and DSF, with advance provision of required documents, including those under Law No. 16/2001, Section 34.
- Extraordinary audits: accept audits at any time, with or without notice, by independent external or other entities as deemed necessary by DICJ/DSF.
- Compulsory publications: by 30 April annually, publish prior-year financials and governance information in the Official Gazette and two major newspapers (one Chinese, one Portuguese), including balance sheet, profit and loss and annex, activity report summary, statutory audit board opinion, summary of external auditor’s opinion, list of shareholders with 5%+ holdings (with percentages), and names of governing bodies; send copies to the Government at least 10 days before publication and any other required elements.
- Cooperation duty: cooperate with the Government (DICJ/DSF) by providing requested information, enabling account analysis/inspection and extraordinary audits, and fulfilling duties under the concessions regime.
- Guarantees: introduction to a chapter requiring a surety to secure compliance with the Concessionaire’s legal and contractual obligations (details not included in the excerpt).

nodes.title: Compulsory publications
nodes.heading:
Clause 62
Compulsory publications
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionaire undertakes to publish, by 30 April every year, the following elements pertaining to the previous year ending 31 December in the Official Gazette of the Macau Special Administrative Region and in two of the most widely read newspapers in the Macau SAR, one in Chinese and one in Portuguese:
nodes.summary:
- Audit oversight: The Concessionaire must submit to audits at any time, with or without notice, by independent external auditors of recognized international standards or other entities whenever the DICJ or DSF deem necessary.
- Annual compulsory publications: By 30 April each year (for the prior year ending 31 December), the Concessionaire must publish in the Macau SAR Official Gazette and two leading newspapers (one Chinese, one Portuguese) the balance sheet, profit and loss account and annex; a summary activity report; the statutory audit board’s opinion; a summary of the external auditor’s opinion; a list of shareholders holding 5% or more (with percentages) at any time during the year; and the names of governing body members.
- Pre-publication submission: All elements to be published, and any other items required under the concessions regime (Clause 6), must be sent to the Government at least 10 days before publication.
- Special cooperation duty: The Concessionaire must cooperate with the Government, particularly DICJ and DSF, by providing requested information, allowing analysis/inspection of accounts, facilitating extraordinary audits, and fulfilling duties under the concessions regime referenced in Clause 6.
- Guarantees: Introduction of Chapter XII indicating a surety requirement (Clause 64) as a guarantee for compliance with the Concessionaire’s legal or contractual obligations (details not included in the excerpt).

nodes.title: Special duty of cooperation
nodes.heading:
Clause 63
Special duty of cooperation
nodes.start_phrase: Without prejudice to the general duty of cooperation set out in Clause 70, the Concessionaire undertakes to cooperate with the Government, namely with DICJ and DSF, in providing the elements and information that may be requested and the analysis or inspection of its accounts, in the performance of extraordinary audits, and generally , in respect to the duties specified in the concessions regime referred to in Clause 6 .
nodes.summary:
- Audit rights: The Concessionaire may be audited at any time, with or without notice, by an independent external entity of recognized international standards or another entity whenever DICJ or DSF deem it necessary.
- Annual compulsory publications (Clause 62): By 30 April each year, the Concessionaire must publish (for the prior calendar year) in the Macau SAR Official Gazette and two widely read Macau newspapers (one Chinese, one Portuguese):
  - Balance sheet, profit and loss account, and annex
  - Summary of the activity report
  - Opinion of the statutory audit board
  - Summary of the external auditor’s opinion
  - List of shareholders holding 5% or more at any time during the year, with percentages
  - Names of governing body members
- Pre-publication submission: Copies of the above, and any other items required under the concessions regime (Clause 6), must be sent to the Government at least 10 days before publication.
- Special duty of cooperation (Clause 63): The Concessionaire must cooperate with the Government, DICJ, and DSF by providing requested information, allowing analysis/inspection of accounts, facilitating extraordinary audits, and complying with duties under the concessions regime (Clause 6).
- Guarantees (Chapter XII, Clause 64 heading): Introduces a surety as a guarantee of the Concessionaire’s compliance with legal or contractual obligations (details not included in the excerpt).

nodes.title: Guarantees
nodes.heading:
CHAPTER XII
Guarantees
nodes.start_phrase: One. The collateral that guarantees complian ce with the Concessionaire's legal or contractual obligations may be provided in any of the legally prescribed forms, provided it is accepted by the Government.
nodes.summary:
The excerpt outlines regulatory oversight and transparency obligations for the Concessionaire in Macau:

- Audit rights: The Concessionaire agrees to audits at any time, with or without prior notice, by an independent external entity of recognized international standards or another entity, whenever DICJ or DSF deem it necessary or convenient.
- Clause 62 – Compulsory publications: By 30 April each year, the Concessionaire must publish prior-year (ending 31 December) information in the Macau SAR Official Gazette and two widely read local newspapers (one Chinese, one Portuguese), including: balance sheet, profit and loss account and annex; summary activity report; statutory audit board opinion; summary of external auditor’s opinion; list of shareholders holding 5% or more at any time during the year with respective percentages; and names of governing body members. Copies of these materials and any other items required under the concessions regime (Clause 6) must be sent to the Government at least 10 days before publication.
- Clause 63 – Special duty of cooperation: The Concessionaire must cooperate with the Government, particularly DICJ and DSF, by providing requested information, enabling analysis/inspection of accounts, supporting extraordinary audits, and generally fulfilling duties under the concessions regime referenced in Clause 6.
- Chapter XII – Guarantees, Clause 64: Introduces a surety to guarantee compliance with the Concessionaire’s legal and contractual obligations (details not included in the excerpt).

nodes.title: Surety as a guarantee of compliance with the Concessionaire's legal or contractual obligations
nodes.heading:
Clause 64
Surety as a guarantee of compliance with the Concessionair e's legal or contractual obligations
nodes.start_phrase: One. The collateral that guarantees complian ce with the Concessionaire's legal or contractual obligations may be provided in any of the legally prescribed forms, provided it is accepted by the Government.
nodes.summary:
- Audit rights: The Concessionaire agrees to audits at any time, with or without notice, by independent external entities or others designated when DICJ or DSF deem necessary.
- Clause 62 – Compulsory publications: By April 30 each year, publish prior-year information (to Dec 31) in the Official Gazette and two major Macau newspapers (one Chinese, one Portuguese), including:
  - Balance sheet, profit and loss account, and annex
  - Summary of activity report
  - Opinion of the statutory audit board
  - Summary of the external auditor’s opinion
  - List of shareholders holding 5% or more at any time during the year, with percentages
  - Names of governing body members
  Additionally, send the Government copies of these and any other required elements at least 10 days before publication.
- Clause 63 – Special duty of cooperation: The Concessionaire must cooperate with the Government (DICJ and DSF) by providing requested information, allowing account analyses/inspections, facilitating extraordinary audits, and fulfilling duties under the concessions regime.
- Chapter XII – Guarantees:
  - Clause 64 – General surety: Maintain an autonomous first-demand bank guarantee in favor of the Government, issued by a Macau-authorized credit institution, securing:
    - Compliance with legal/contractual obligations
    - Payment of the premium due to the Macau SAR (Clause 50)
    - Payment of fines/penalties
    - Compensation for damages and lost profits from non-compliance
    - Compliance with labor obligations
    Value: MOP 1,000,000,000 from 1 Jan 2023 until 180 days after concession/contract termination. Must be kept in force; Government may draw without prior court decision; Concessionaire must restore the amount within 15 days after use; cancellation only with Government authorization; Government may approve term changes or substitution; all costs borne by the Concessionaire; covers statutory guarantees cited (Law No. 16/2001 and Administrative Regulation No. 26/2001).
  - Clause 65 – Specific tax guarantee: When required, provide an autonomous first-demand bank guarantee to secure payment of the special gaming tax if there is justified concern about non-payment; terms require Government authorization to change; Government may draw without court decision upon non-payment; Concessionaire must restore the amount within 15 days.

nodes.title: Specific bank guarantee to secure the payment of the special tax on gambling
nodes.heading:
Clause 65
Specific bank guarantee to secur e the payment of the special tax on gambling
nodes.start_phrase: One. Pursuant to Section 27 (5) of Law No. 16/2001, the Concessionaire undertakes to present, when so required by the Government, an autonomous bank guarantee, on first demand, issued in favor of the Government and intended to guarantee payment, if there is justifiable fear that the Concessionaire will not pay the probable monthly amounts of the special tax on gaming within the period and under the terms, conditions, and in the amount to be set by the Government.
nodes.summary:
- Outlines the Government’s rights and the Concessionaire’s duties regarding autonomous bank guarantees used to secure legal and contractual obligations: Government may draw without prior court decision; cancellation requires Government authorization; the Concessionaire must restore the guarantee within 15 days after use; the Government may authorize changes or substitutions of the guarantee; all issuance/maintenance/cancellation costs are borne by the Concessionaire; the guarantee also satisfies statutory guarantees under specified Macau laws and regulations.
- Establishes a specific autonomous bank guarantee to secure payment of the special gaming tax: may be demanded by the Government when there is justified fear of nonpayment of probable monthly tax; terms cannot be altered without Government authorization; Government may call the guarantee without prior court decision upon default; the Concessionaire must replenish within 15 days of notice; cancellation only with Government authorization and no earlier than 180 days after concession end or termination; all related costs borne by the Concessionaire.
- Provides for guarantees by the controlling shareholder(s) (or, if none, shareholders with ≥5%): may be required when there is justified fear the Concessionaire cannot meet obligations; acceptable forms include cash deposit, bank guarantee, bond insurance, or other Civil Code forms; terms, timing, and amount set by order of the Chief Executive; Government may use the guarantee without prior court decision upon breach; the Concessionaire must endeavor that shareholders restore the guarantee within 15 days; terms require Government authorization to change.
- Introduces Chapter XIII on Government oversight, supervision, and control of the Concessionaire’s compliance (heading only in this excerpt).

nodes.title: Guarantee provided by a controlling shareholder or shareholders of the Concessionaire
nodes.heading:
Clause 66
Guarantee pr ovided by a contr olling shar eholder or shar eholders of the Concessionair e
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Government may require that the Concessionaire's controlling shareholder provide a guarantee to secure compliance with the commitments and obligations assum ed by the Concessionaire; if the Concessionaire does not have a controlling shareholder , the Secretary for Economy and Finance may require that the aforementioned guarantee to be provided by shareholders holding 5% or more of the Concessionaire's share capital.
nodes.summary:
- Autonomous bank guarantee: May be canceled only with Government authorization and only 180 days after the concession ends or is terminated; all issuance, maintenance, and cancellation costs are borne by the Concessionaire.
- Clause 66 (Guarantee by controlling shareholder(s)): 
  - Government may require a guarantee from the Concessionaire’s controlling shareholder; if none, from shareholders holding 5% or more.
  - Trigger: justified concern that the Concessionaire cannot meet legal or contractual obligations.
  - Forms: cash deposit, bank guarantee, bond insurance, or other forms under Civil Code Section 619; terms, period, and value set by order of the Chief Executive.
  - Government may draw on the guarantee without prior court decision upon the Concessionaire’s noncompliance.
  - If used, the Concessionaire must ensure its controlling shareholder(s) restore the full amount within 15 days of notification.
  - Guarantee terms cannot be changed without Government authorization.
- Chapter XIII, Clause 67: Introduces Government oversight, supervision, and control of the Concessionaire’s compliance (details not provided in this excerpt).

nodes.title: Supervision of compliance with the Concessionaire's obligations
nodes.heading:
CHAPTER XIII
Supervision of compliance with the Concessionaire's obligations
nodes.start_phrase: One. The power to supervise, oversee and monitor compliance with the Concessionaire's obligations is exercised by the Government, namely through DICJ and DSF .
nodes.summary:
- Cancellation and costs of autonomous bank guarantee: may be cancelled only with Government authorization, 180 days after concession end or termination; all issuance, maintenance, and cancellation costs are borne by the Concessionaire.
- Clause 66 establishes a guarantee by controlling shareholder(s): 
  - Government may require the Concessionaire’s controlling shareholder to provide a guarantee securing the Concessionaire’s obligations; if there is no controlling shareholder, the Secretary for Economy and Finance may require shareholders with 5%+ holdings to provide it.
  - This guarantee can be required when there is a justified concern that the Concessionaire may not meet legal or contractual obligations.
  - Acceptable forms include cash deposit, bank guarantee, bond insurance, or other forms under Civil Code Section 619; timing, terms, and amount are set by order of the Chief Executive.
  - Government may draw on the guarantee without a prior court decision if the Concessionaire fails to comply.
  - If used, the Concessionaire must ensure the controlling shareholder(s) restore the full amount within 15 days of notification.
  - Terms and conditions of the guarantee cannot be changed without Government authorization.
- Introduction to Chapter XIII: outlines Government oversight, supervision, and control of the Concessionaire’s compliance (details to follow).

nodes.title: Oversight, supervision and control by the Government
nodes.heading:
Clause 67
Oversight, supervision and contr ol by the Government
nodes.start_phrase: One. The power to supervise, oversee and monitor compliance with the Concessionaire's obligations is exercised by the Government, namely through DICJ and DSF .
nodes.summary: This excerpt outlines financial guarantees and regulatory oversight in a casino concession context. It sets that an autonomous bank guarantee can be canceled only with Government authorization 180 days after the concession ends or is terminated, with all related costs borne by the Concessionaire. The Government may require guarantees from the Concessionaire’s controlling shareholder—or, if none, from shareholders holding at least 5%—when there is justified concern about non-compliance; such guarantees may be in cash, bank guarantee, bond insurance, or other forms under Civil Code Section 619, with terms set by the Chief Executive. The Government may draw on these guarantees without prior court judgment if obligations are breached, and the Concessionaire must ensure replenishment within 15 days; changes to guarantee terms need Government approval. The Government, through DICJ and DSF, has broad powers to supervise and inspect, including unannounced access to premises and records, and the Concessionaire must follow Government/DICJ directives, including possible suspension of casino operations. DICJ provides permanent oversight, conducts triennial compliance reviews with mandated remediation if deficiencies are found, and monitors gross gaming revenue daily. The chapter also records mutual cooperation duties, including the Government’s general duty to cooperate and the Concessionaire’s general obligation to cooperate.

nodes.title: Daily monitoring of gross gaming revenue
nodes.heading:
Clause 68
Daily monitoring of gr oss gaming r evenue
nodes.start_phrase: The Conce ssionaire is subject to daily supervision by the Government, through DICJ, of its gross gaming revenues, in accordance with the law .
nodes.summary:
- Establishes the Government’s supervisory, oversight, and monitoring powers over the Concessionaire, exercised primarily through DICJ and DSF.
- Requires the Concessionaire, upon request and without prior notice, to grant free access to premises and to provide full inspection access to accounting, transactions, books, minutes, accounts, statistics, management records, and any information deemed necessary by the Government or its authorized appointees.
- Obligates the Concessionaire to comply with Government determinations and DICJ instructions, including potential suspension of casino operations.
- Confirms that the concession’s operation is under the permanent supervision and oversight of DICJ pursuant to applicable law.
- Mandates a triennial DICJ review of the Concessionaire’s compliance with the concession contract; if deficiencies or lack of proactivity are found, the Concessionaire must remedy them within a deadline set by the Secretary for Economy and Finance under Law No. 16/2001, Section 22(1)(11).
- Imposes daily Government (DICJ) monitoring of the Concessionaire’s gross gaming revenue.
- Sets out general duties of cooperation: the Government’s duty to cooperate to enable the Concessionaire to fulfill legal and contractual obligations, and a forthcoming clause indicating the Concessionaire’s general obligation to cooperate (details not included in the excerpt).

nodes.title: General duties of cooperation
nodes.heading:
CHAPTER XIV
General duties of cooperation
nodes.start_phrase: The Government undertakes to cooperate with the Concessionaire so as to enable it to fulfill its legal and contractual obligations.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes the Government’s authority—primarily through DICJ and DSF—to supervise, oversee, and monitor the concessionaire’s compliance with its obligations.
- Requires the concessionaire, upon request and without prior notice, to grant free access to premises and to all accounting, books, minutes, records, statistics, and management information, and to provide any information deemed necessary by the Government or its appointed agents.
- Obligates the concessionaire to comply with Government determinations issued under oversight powers, including DICJ instructions and potential suspension of casino operations.
- Confirms the concession’s operation is under permanent supervision and oversight by DICJ in accordance with applicable law.
- Mandates a three-year compliance review by DICJ; if deficiencies or lack of proactivity are found, the concessionaire must remedy them within a period set by the Secretary for Economy and Finance, pursuant to Section 22(1)(11) of Law No. 16/2001.
- Clause 68: Imposes daily Government (DICJ) monitoring of the concessionaire’s gross gaming revenue.
- Chapter XIV introduces general cooperation duties: the Government’s duty to cooperate with the concessionaire (Clause 69) and a general cooperation obligation of the concessionaire (Clause 70, details truncated).

nodes.title: Government's General Duty to Cooperate
nodes.heading:
Clause 69
Government's General Duty to Cooperate
nodes.start_phrase: The Government undertakes to cooperate with the Concessionaire so as to enable it to fulfill its legal and contractual obligations.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes the Government’s authority—through DICJ and DSF—to supervise, oversee, and monitor the Concessionaire’s compliance.
- Requires the Concessionaire, upon request and without prior notice, to grant free access to premises and to accounting/management records, transactions, books, minutes, accounts, statistics, and other documents, and to provide any information deemed necessary.
- Obligates the Concessionaire to comply with Government/DICJ determinations, including instructions that may involve suspending casino operations.
- Confirms that the concession’s operation is under DICJ’s permanent supervision and oversight.
- Mandates a DICJ review every three years of overall compliance with the concession; deficiencies must be remedied within a deadline set by the Secretary for Economy and Finance pursuant to Law No. 16/2001, Section 22(1)(11).
- Imposes daily Government (DICJ) supervision of gross gaming revenue.
- Introduces general duties of cooperation: the Government’s duty to cooperate with the Concessionaire (Clause 69) and the Concessionaire’s general cooperation obligation (Clause 70, text partially shown).

nodes.title: General obligation of cooperation by the Concessionaire
nodes.heading:
Clause 70
General obligation of cooperation by the Concessionair e
nodes.start_phrase: For the purposes set forth in this concession contract, the Concessionaire undertakes to cooperate with the Government, submitting any documents and providing any information, data, authorizations or evidence requested thereof.
nodes.summary:
- Government oversight: Compliance is supervised by the Government via DICJ and DSF, with permanent supervision by DICJ under applicable law.
- Unrestricted access: The Concessionaire must, upon request and without prior notice, grant the Government or its authorized designees free access to premises and to inspect all accounting, records, statistics, and management documents, and provide any information deemed necessary.
- Compliance with directives: The Concessionaire must obey Government and DICJ determinations, including instructions that may involve suspending casino operations.
- Triennial review: DICJ will review overall compliance every three years; any deficiencies or lack of proactivity must be remedied within a period set by the Secretary for Economy and Finance, per Law No. 16/2001, Section 22(1)(11).
- Daily GGR monitoring: DICJ conducts daily supervision of the Concessionaire’s gross gaming revenue.
- Cooperation duties: The Government must cooperate to enable the Concessionaire to meet legal and contractual obligations; the Concessionaire must cooperate by submitting all requested documents, information, data, authorizations, and evidence.
- Operational obligations: The Concessionaire must operate all casino premises and related facilities normally for their intended or authorized purposes.
- Organizational and safety standards: The Concessionaire must ensure all contracted entities observe good organization, proper operations, and special safety measures for patrons, casinos, employees, and other personnel.
- Qualified contractors: Only duly licensed and authorized entities with adequate technical and professional capacity may be engaged.
- Strategic commitments: The Concessionaire must implement its submitted plans for overseas customer market expansion and social responsibility, including support for local SMEs and diversification of local industries.

nodes.title: Other duties of the Concessionaire
nodes.heading:
CHAPTER XV
Other duties of the Concessionaire
nodes.start_phrase: The Concessionaire undertakes to operate normally all of the premises of the casinos and other facilities and buildings assigned to the operation of the concession for the scopes for which they are intended or authorized.
nodes.summary:
- Obligation to cooperate with the Government by providing any requested documents, information, data, authorizations, or evidence.
- Duty to operate all casino premises and associated facilities normally and strictly for their intended or authorized purposes.
- Responsibility to ensure contracted entities follow sound organizational and operational practices and implement special safety measures for patrons, casinos, employees, and other personnel.
- Requirement to engage only duly licensed and authorized entities with appropriate technical and professional capacity.
- Commitment to implement plans from the winning tender proposal, including:
  - Expansion of markets for overseas customers.
  - Social responsibility initiatives, specifically supporting local small and medium-sized enterprises and promoting diversification of local industries.

nodes.title: Operation of the casinos and other facilities and premises
nodes.heading:
Clause 71
Operation of the casinos and other facilities and pr emises
nodes.start_phrase: The Concessionaire undertakes to operate normally all of the premises of the casinos and other facilities and buildings assigned to the operation of the concession for the scopes for which they are intended or authorized.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes the Concessionaire’s duty to cooperate with the Government by providing requested documents, information, data, authorizations, and evidence.
- Requires normal operation of all casino premises and other assigned facilities strictly for their intended or authorized purposes.
- Sets general duties:
  - Ensure all contracted entities follow proper organizational and operational standards and implement special safety measures for patrons, employees, and all personnel on-site.
  - Engage only duly licensed, authorized entities with adequate technical and professional capacity.
  - Implement overseas market expansion plans in line with the Concessionaire’s winning tender proposal.
  - Execute social responsibility plans per the tender proposal, including support for local SMEs and diversification of local industries.

nodes.title: General duties of the Concessionaire
nodes.heading:
Clause 72
General duties of the Concessionair e
nodes.start_phrase: One. It is the Concess ionaire's special obligation to promote and demand, from all entities that may be contracted for the development of activities included within the concession, the observance of all rules of good organization and operation and special safety measures in relation to the patrons, its casinos, its employees and other persons who perform functions therein.
nodes.summary:
- Concessionaire must cooperate with the Government by providing any requested documents, information, data, authorizations, or evidence.
- Must operate all casino premises and assigned facilities normally and only for their intended or authorized purposes.
- General duties include:
  - Ensuring good organization, proper operation, and special safety measures for patrons, casinos, employees, and all personnel performing functions.
  - Contracting only duly licensed, authorized, and technically/professionally capable entities for concession-related activities.
  - Implementing overseas market expansion plans as committed in its public tender proposal.
  - Executing social responsibility plans per its award proposal, including:
    - Supporting local SMEs.
    - Promoting diversification of local industries.
    - Guaranteeing rights and interests of local employees (work credits, in-service training, professional advancement, and welfare protections).
    - Hiring disabled or rehabilitated individuals.
    - Supporting public-interest activities.
    - Supporting educational, scientific/technological, environmental, cultural, and sports initiatives.
  - Preparing a vocational training plan for workers within a Government-set timeframe and supplying related documentation/information.
- Must join the non-mandatory central provident fund system under Law No. 7/2017.
- Requires Government authorization to replace, cancel, or alter evidential documents/records related to its activities, and to acquire gaming equipment and materials.
- Government authorizations/approvals or refusals do not relieve the Concessionaire of its contractual obligations nor transfer responsibility to the Government, except where Government action imposes special and extraordinary burdens or losses on the Concessionaire.
- Chapter on Liability of the Concessionaire is introduced (Clause 76), but its content is not included in this excerpt.

nodes.title: Adherence to the non-mandatory central provident fund system
nodes.heading:
Clause 73
Adher ence to the non-mandatory central pr ovident fund system
nodes.start_phrase: The Conce ssionaire undertakes to join the non-compulsory central welfare scheme established by Law No. 7/2017 (Non-compulsory central provident fund).
nodes.summary: The excerpt outlines the Concessionaire’s social and regulatory obligations: ensuring local employees’ rights, training, advancement, and welfare; promoting inclusive hiring of disabled or rehabilitated persons; supporting public-interest initiatives across education, science/technology, environment, culture, and sports; preparing a government-timed vocational training plan and providing related documentation; joining the non-compulsory central provident fund under Law No. 7/2017; obtaining government authorization to replace, cancel, or alter evidentiary documents/records and to acquire gaming equipment/material; and clarifying that government approvals or refusals do not relieve the Concessionaire’s contractual obligations nor transfer liability to the Government, except where government action imposes special, extraordinary burdens or losses. It also signals the start of a chapter on the Concessionaire’s liability (Clause 76).

nodes.title: Other Government Authorizations
nodes.heading:
Clause 74
Other Government Authorizations
nodes.start_phrase: The replac ement, cancellation or alteration of evidential documents and records relating to the activity of the Concessionaire or the acquisition of gaming equipment and material shall require Government authorization.
nodes.summary:
- Social responsibility obligations for the Concessionaire, including:
  - Protecting rights and interests of local employees (work credits, in-service training, career advancement, welfare protections).
  - Hiring disabled or rehabilitated individuals.
  - Supporting activities in the public interest.
  - Supporting educational, scientific/technological, environmental, cultural, and sports initiatives.
- Requirement to prepare a vocational training plan for workers within a government-defined timeframe and to provide related documentation/information.
- Commitment to join the non-mandatory central provident fund system under Law No. 7/2017.
- Government authorization required for replacing, canceling, or altering evidential documents and records related to the concessionaire’s activities, and for acquiring gaming equipment and materials.
- Clarification that government authorizations, approvals, or refusals do not relieve the Concessionaire of contractual obligations nor transfer responsibility to the Government, except where government action imposes special and extraordinary burdens or losses on the Concessionaire.
- Introduction of Chapter XVI on the Liability of the Concessionaire (beginning at Clause 76).

nodes.title: Government authorizations and approvals
nodes.heading:
Clause 75
Government authorizations and appr ovals
nodes.start_phrase: The Government authorizations, approvals and its possible refusals do not exonerate the Concessionaire from the punctual compliance with the obligations undertaken in this concession contract, nor do they imply the assumption by the Government of any responsibilities, except when its action has imposed a burden or caused special and extraordinary losses for the Concessionaire.
nodes.summary:
- Social and employment obligations: protect local employees’ rights (work credits, in‑service training, professional advancement, and welfare protections); promote hiring of disabled or rehabilitated individuals; support public-interest initiatives and activities in education, science and technology, environmental protection, culture, and sports.
- Workforce development: prepare and submit, within a government-set timeframe, a vocational training plan for workers involved in concession activities, along with any required supporting documents or information.
- Welfare scheme participation: commit to join the non-compulsory central provident fund established by Law No. 7/2017.
- Regulatory controls: obtain government authorization for replacing, canceling, or altering evidential documents and records related to the Concessionaire’s activities, and for acquiring gaming equipment and materials.
- Effect of government approvals: authorizations or refusals do not relieve the Concessionaire of its contractual obligations nor transfer liability to the Government, except where government action imposes special and extraordinary burdens or losses on the Concessionaire.
- Transition to Chapter XVI: introduction to the Concessionaire’s liability (Clause 76) follows.

nodes.title: Liability of the Concessionaire
nodes.heading:
CHAPTER XVI
Liability of the Concessionaire
nodes.start_phrase: The Concessionaire is liable to the Maca u SAR for losses resulting from total or partial non-compliance with its legal or contractual obligations due to facts it is responsible for .
nodes.summary:
- Protection of local employees’ rights and interests, including work credits, in‑service training, career advancement, and welfare protections.
- Commitment to hire disabled or rehabilitated individuals.
- Support for activities in the public interest, including educational, scientific/technological, environmental, cultural, and sports initiatives.
- Obligation to develop a vocational training plan for concession-related workers within a government-set timeframe and provide accompanying documentation/information.
- Agreement to join the non-compulsory central provident fund under Law No. 7/2017.
- Requirement to obtain government authorization for replacing, canceling, or altering evidential documents/records and for acquiring gaming equipment and materials.
- Clarification that government authorizations/approvals or refusals do not relieve the concessionaire of contractual obligations nor create government liability, except where government actions impose special and extraordinary burdens or losses.
- Introduction of Chapter XVI on the concessionaire’s liability (Clause 76), with details not included in the excerpt.

nodes.title: Civil liability to the Macau SAR
nodes.heading:
Clause 76
Civil liability to the Macau SAR
nodes.start_phrase: The Concessionaire is liable to the Maca u SAR for losses resulting from total or partial non-compliance with its legal or contractual obligations due to facts it is responsible for .
nodes.summary:
- Establishes the concessionaire’s civil liability to the Macao SAR for losses arising from its total or partial breach of legal or contractual duties when attributable to the concessionaire.
- Clarifies that the Macao SAR bears no non-contractual liability to third parties for acts of the concessionaire or its representatives.
- Confirms the concessionaire’s liability, under principal–agent rules, for damages caused by entities it engages to perform concession-related activities.
- Prohibits any assignment, conveyance, disposal, encumbrance, transfer, or partial assignment—whether explicit or implicit, formal or informal—of the right to operate a casino/gaming area, the related games of fortune or chance rights/obligations, or the concessionaire’s contractual position, without prejudice to Law No. 7/2022, Section 5(3).
- Imposes penalty payments to the Macao SAR for violations, without prejudice to other sanctions:
  - MOP 2,000,000,000 for full assignment/conveyance/alienation of the right to operate a casino or gaming area.
  - MOP 1,000,000,000 for partial assignment/conveyance/alienation of that right.
  - MOP 600,000,000 for encumbrance of that right, in whole or in part.

nodes.title: Exemption of the Macau SAR from the Concessionaire's non-contractual liability to third parties
nodes.heading:
Clause 77
Exemption of the Macau SAR fr om the Concessionair e's non-contractual liability to
third parties
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Macau SAR neither assumes nor shares any responsibility which the Concessionaire may be liable to for acts done by it or on its behalf that involve or may involve civil or other liability .
nodes.summary:
- Establishes the concessionaire’s civil liability to the Macau SAR for losses arising from total or partial non-compliance with legal or contractual obligations attributable to the concessionaire.
- Clarifies that the Macau SAR bears no non-contractual liability to third parties for acts of the concessionaire or those acting on its behalf; the concessionaire is solely responsible, including for damages caused by entities it retains, under principles of principal–agent relations.
- Regulates “subjective changes” in the concession: prohibits assigning, conveying, disposing of, or encumbering, in whole or in part and by any means (express/tacit; formal/informal), the right to operate a casino or gaming zone, any related legal rights and obligations, or the concessionaire’s contractual position, save as allowed by Law No. 7/2022, Section 5(3).
- Sets penalty clauses for violations, payable to the Macau SAR, without prejudice to other sanctions:
  - MOP 2,000,000,000 for assignment/conveyance/alienation of the right to operate a casino or gaming area as a whole.
  - MOP 1,000,000,000 for such actions in part.
  - MOP 600,000,000 for encumbrance of the right to operate a casino or gaming area, in whole or in part.

nodes.title: Subjective changes in the concession
nodes.heading:
CHAPTER XVII
Subjective changes in the concession
nodes.start_phrase: One. Without prejudice to the provisions of Section 5 (3) of Law No. 7/2022, the Concessionaire undertakes not to assign, convey , dispose of, or in any way encumber , in whole or in part, expressly or tacitly , formally or informally , the right to operate a casino or gaming zone, or undertake the transfer or partial assignment of the legal rights and obligations relating to games of fortune or chance in casinos or the contractual position of the Concessionaire to third parties, or undertake any legal transaction aimed at achieving the same result.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes the concessionaire’s civil liability to the Macau SAR for losses arising from total or partial non-compliance with legal or contractual obligations attributable to the concessionaire.
- Clarifies that the Macau SAR bears no non-contractual (tort) liability to third parties for acts of the concessionaire or its representatives; the concessionaire remains solely responsible.
- Extends the concessionaire’s liability to damages caused by entities it retains to perform concession-related activities (principal–agent responsibility).
- Prohibits the assignment, conveyance, disposal, encumbrance, or any form of transfer—whether whole or partial, explicit or implicit, formal or informal—of the right to operate a casino or gaming zone, the related rights and obligations for games of fortune or chance, or the concessionaire’s contractual position, subject to any exception under Section 5(3) of Law No. 7/2022.
- Imposes penalty clauses for violations, payable to the Macau SAR:
  - MOP 2,000,000,000 for whole assignment/conveyance/alienation of the right to operate a casino or gaming area.
  - MOP 1,000,000,000 for partial assignment/conveyance/alienation.
  - MOP 600,000,000 for encumbrance of the right, in whole or in part.
- Notes that these penalties apply without prejudice to other applicable sanctions or penalties.

nodes.title: Assignment of the contractual position, encumbrance, conveyance, and alienation
nodes.heading:
Clause 78
Assignment of the contractual position, encumbrance, conveyance, and alienation
nodes.start_phrase: One. Without prejudice to the provisions of Section 5 (3) of Law No. 7/2022, the Concessionaire undertakes not to assign, convey , dispose of, or in any way encumber , in whole or in part, expressly or tacitly , formally or informally , the right to operate a casino or gaming zone, or undertake the transfer or partial assignment of the legal rights and obligations relating to games of fortune or chance in casinos or the contractual position of the Concessionaire to third parties, or undertake any legal transaction aimed at achieving the same result.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes the concessionaire’s civil liability to the Macau SAR for losses arising from total or partial non-compliance with legal or contractual obligations attributable to it.
- Confirms the Macau SAR bears no non-contractual liability to third parties for acts of the concessionaire or its agents; the concessionaire is fully responsible for its own acts and those performed on its behalf, and is liable for damages caused by entities it retains under principal–agent rules.
- Prohibits assignment, conveyance, disposal, encumbrance, or any transfer (in whole or in part) of casino operation rights, legal rights/obligations related to casino gaming, or the concessionaire’s contractual position, including any equivalent legal arrangements; subject to Law No. 7/2022, Section 5(3).
- Sets penalty clauses for prohibited transfers/encumbrances:
  - Whole assignment/conveyance/alienation of casino or gaming area: MOP 2,000,000,000
  - Partial assignment/conveyance/alienation: MOP 1,000,000,000
  - Encumbrance (whole or part): MOP 600,000,000
  - Transfer/partial assignment of legal rights/obligations or contractual position, or equivalent act: MOP 600,000,000
- Bans sub-concessions (whole or part) or equivalent arrangements; penalties:
  - Whole sub-concession: MOP 1,000,000,000
  - Partial sub-concession: MOP 600,000,000
- Addresses breach of contract: attributable failures to comply with law, the concession contract, or Government determinations trigger applicable legal/contractual sanctions.
- Provides limited exemption for force majeure or non-imputable events, only to the extent they actually prevented timely and full performance; defines force majeure as unforeseeable, irresistible, beyond the concessionaire’s control, including war, terrorism, public order changes, epidemics, atomic radiation, fire, lightning, severe floods, cyclones, tropical storms, earthquakes, and other natural disasters directly affecting concession activities.

nodes.title: Prohibition on granting sub-concessions
nodes.heading:
Clause 79
Prohibition on granting sub-concessions
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionaire may not grant sub-concessions on its concession, in whole or in part, or undertake any legal business aimed at achieving the same result.
nodes.summary:
- Imposes a penalty of MOP 600,000,000 for transferring or assigning, in part, the legal rights/obligations or contractual position in the casino gambling concession to a third party, or conducting any equivalent legal transaction.
- Clause 79 establishes a prohibition on granting sub-concessions, in whole or in part, or engaging in any legal arrangement intended to achieve the same effect.
- Violations of the sub-concession ban trigger penalties payable to the Macau SAR: MOP 1,000,000,000 for a sub-concession of the whole concession and MOP 600,000,000 for a sub-concession of part of the concession, without prejudice to other applicable sanctions.
- Chapter XVIII (Non-compliance): Clause 80 defines breach of contract—if the concessionaire fails to meet legal or contractual duties or government determinations for reasons attributable to it, it is subject to sanctions under law or the contract.
- Provides exemptions from liability in cases of force majeure or other non-imputable facts, but only to the extent that timely and full compliance was prevented.
- Force majeure is defined as unforeseeable, irresistible events beyond the concessionaire’s control whose effects occur regardless of will or personal circumstances, with examples including war, terrorism, public order disturbances, epidemics, atomic radiation, fire, lightning, severe floods, cyclones, tropical storms, earthquakes, and other natural disasters directly affecting concession activities.

nodes.title: Non-compliance with the contract
nodes.heading:
CHAPTER XVIII
Non-compliance with the contract
nodes.start_phrase: One. Without prejudice to Clauses 81 and 82, failure by the Concessionaire, for reasons attributable thereto, to comply with the duties and obligations arising from the legislation or this concession contract or the determinations of the Government shall subject the Concessionaire to the application of the sanctions or penalties prescribed by law or the contract herein.
nodes.summary:
- Penalty of MOP 600,000,000 for transferring or assigning, in whole or in part, the legal rights/obligations or contractual position of the casino gambling concession to a third party, or conducting any transaction with the same effect.
- Explicit prohibition on granting sub-concessions, in whole or in part, or engaging in equivalent legal arrangements.
- Monetary penalties for prohibited sub-concessions: MOP 1,000,000,000 for the entire concession; MOP 600,000,000 for part of the concession, payable to the Macau SAR.
- Establishes breach-of-contract framework: the Concessionaire is liable for non-compliance with laws, the concession contract, or government determinations, subject to prescribed sanctions.
- Provides exemption from liability for force majeure or non-imputable events, but only to the extent they prevent timely and full compliance.
- Defines force majeure as unforeseeable, irresistible events beyond the Concessionaire’s control, listing examples such as war, terrorism, public order disturbances, epidemics, radiation, major fires, floods, cyclones, tropical storms, earthquakes, and other natural disasters directly affecting concession activities.

nodes.title: Breach of contract
nodes.heading:
Clause 80
Breach of contract
nodes.start_phrase: One. Without prejudice to Clauses 81 and 82, failure by the Concessionaire, for reasons attributable thereto, to comply with the duties and obligations arising from the legislation or this concession contract or the determinations of the Government shall subject the Concessionaire to the application of the sanctions or penalties prescribed by law or the contract herein.
nodes.summary:
- Sets a MOP 600,000,000 penalty for partially transferring or assigning casino concession rights or equivalent arrangements to third parties.
- Prohibits any sub-concessions or similar legal arrangements; penalties are MOP 1,000,000,000 for sub-conceding the whole concession and MOP 600,000,000 for part.
- Establishes breach-of-contract rules: the Concessionaire faces legal/contractual sanctions for non-compliance attributable to it; exemptions apply only for narrowly defined force majeure events (e.g., war, terrorism, public disorder, epidemics, radiation, major fires, floods, cyclones, storms, earthquakes, other natural disasters).
- Requires immediate notification to the Government of force majeure, identification of affected obligations, and mitigation/normalization measures; obliges the Concessionaire to rebuild/restore affected assets and operations or transfer insurance proceeds to the Macau SAR if it opts not to rebuild.
- Outlines termination grounds per Law No. 16/2001 by the Chief Executive (after consulting the Specialized Commission), including threats to national security/Macau SAR, mutual agreement, redemption, breach by the Concessionaire, public interest, and lack of good standing.
- Allows rescission/termination of the concession at any time by mutual agreement between the Government and the Concessionaire.

nodes.title: Termination, cessation, and suspension of the concession
nodes.heading:
CHAPTER XIX
Termination, cessation, and suspension of the concession
nodes.start_phrase: According to Section 45 of Law No. 16/2001, the casino gambling concession may be terminated by the Chief Executive, after hearing the Specialized Commission for the Gaming Sector , for the following reasons:
nodes.summary:
- Force majeure obligations: The concessionaire must immediately notify the Government of any force majeure event, specify which contractual obligations are affected, and indicate mitigation and normalization measures as soon as possible.
- Asset restoration and insurance: In events referenced earlier (e.g., damage/loss), the concessionaire must rebuild or restore assets promptly to reestablish proper casino operations; if it has no economic interest in doing so, it must transfer the insurance payout to the Macau SAR.
- Termination framework (Chapter XIX): Outlines termination, cessation, and suspension of the casino gambling concession.
- Clause 81 (Termination): The Chief Executive, after hearing the Specialized Commission for the Gaming Sector, may terminate under Law No. 16/2001, Section 45, for: threats to national security or the Macau SAR; mutual agreement; redemption; breach by the concessionaire; public interest; or lack of good standing per Section 14.
- Clause 82 (Rescission by mutual agreement): The Government and the concessionaire may terminate the concession at any time by mutual agreement.

nodes.title: Termination
nodes.heading:
Clause 81
Termination
nodes.start_phrase: According to Section 45 of Law No. 16/2001, the casino gambling concession may be terminated by the Chief Executive, after hearing the Specialized Commission for the Gaming Sector , for the following reasons:
nodes.summary: The excerpt outlines the concessionaire’s duties in force majeure situations and the legal framework for terminating a Macau casino gambling concession. It requires the concessionaire to promptly notify the Government of any force majeure, identify which contractual obligations are impeded, and propose mitigation/normalization measures. If assets are damaged in events referenced earlier, the concessionaire must rebuild/restore them to reestablish casino operations; if it lacks economic interest in doing so, it must transfer insurance proceeds to the Macau SAR. Chapter XIX introduces termination, cessation, and suspension rules. Clause 81 specifies that the Chief Executive, after consulting the Specialized Commission for the Gaming Sector and under Section 45 of Law No. 16/2001, may terminate the concession for threats to national security or to the Macau SAR, by agreement, by redemption, for breach by the concessionaire, for public interest, or for lack of good standing under Section 14 of that law. Clause 82 affirms that the Government and the concessionaire may rescind the contract at any time by mutual agreement.

nodes.title: Rescission by mutual agreement
nodes.heading:
Clause 82
Rescission by mutual agr eement
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Government and the Concessionaire may at any time terminate this concession contract by mutual agreement.
nodes.summary:
- Force majeure: The concessionaire must immediately notify the Government of any force majeure event, identify affected contractual obligations, and outline mitigation/normalization measures. It must rebuild/restore assets and casino operations as soon as possible; if it has no economic interest in doing so, it must transfer insurance proceeds to the Macau SAR.
- Chapter XIX (Termination, cessation, suspension):
  - Clause 81 (Termination): The Chief Executive, after hearing the Specialized Commission for the Gaming Sector, may terminate the casino concession for: threats to national security/Macau SAR; mutual agreement; redemption; breach by the concessionaire; public interest; or lack of good standing under Section 14 of Law No. 16/2001.
  - Clause 82 (Rescission by mutual agreement): The Government and concessionaire may terminate at any time by agreement. The concessionaire remains fully responsible for winding up its contracts; the Macau SAR assumes no liability unless expressly agreed.
  - Clause 83 (Redemption): From the 8th year, the Government may redeem the concession with at least one year’s registered notice. Macau SAR assumes rights/obligations from valid pre-notice contracts; post-notice contracts are assumed only if pre-authorized. It retains recovery rights for obligations outside normal concession management. The concessionaire is entitled to fair and equitable compensation for benefits foregone in projects under the Investment Plans; for construction projects, the compensation equals prior fiscal year income (before interest, depreciation, amortization) multiplied by years remaining in the concession.
  - Clause 84 (Seizure): If unauthorized termination/interruption (not due to force majeure) is occurring or imminent, or serious organizational/operational deficiencies threaten regular operation, the Government may replace the concessionaire directly or via third parties to ensure continued operation and implement necessary measures for as long as issues persist.

nodes.title: Redemption
nodes.heading:
Clause 83
Redemption
nodes.start_phrase: One. Unless provided otherwise by law, the Government may, from the eighth year of the concession, redeem said concession by giving the Concessionaire at least one year's notice by prepaid registered letter .
nodes.summary:
- The Concessionaire is solely responsible for terminating its own contracts; the Macau SAR assumes no liability unless expressly agreed.
- Clause 83 (Redemption):
  - From the 8th year, the Government may redeem the concession with at least one year’s notice by prepaid registered letter.
  - Upon redemption, the Macau SAR assumes all rights and obligations from valid transactions entered into before the notice.
  - Obligations under contracts signed after the notice are assumed only if the Government authorized them beforehand.
  - The Macau SAR’s assumption of obligations does not waive its right to recover amounts for obligations outside normal concession management.
  - The Concessionaire is entitled to fair and equitable compensation under Section 46(2) of Law No. 16/2001 for benefits lost on projects in the approved Investment Plans. For construction projects, compensation equals the prior fiscal year’s income (before interest, depreciation, and amortization) multiplied by the remaining years of the concession.
- Clause 84 (Seizure):
  - If there is an unauthorized (and non–force majeure) termination or interruption of operations, or serious organizational/operational deficiencies that jeopardize regular operation, the Government may replace the Concessionaire—directly or via third parties—to ensure continued operation and implement necessary measures for as long as issues persist.

nodes.title: Seizure
nodes.heading:
Clause 84
Seizur e
nodes.start_phrase: One. When the total or partial termination or interruption of the operation of the concession by the Concessionaire occurs or is imminent, without authorization and not due to force majeur e, or when there are serious disturbances or deficiencies in the organization and operation of the Concessionaire or in the general condition of the installations and equipment, which may compromise the regularity of the concession operation, the Government may replace the Concessionaire, directly or through third- parties, ensuring the operation of the concession and promoting the execution of the measures required to ensure the scope of this concession contract, for as long as the termination or interruption lasts or the disturbances and deficiencies persist.
nodes.summary:
- Concessionaire bears full responsibility for ending the effects of its own contracts; Macau SAR assumes no liability unless expressly agreed.
- Redemption (Clause 83): Government may redeem the concession from the 8th year with at least one year’s registered notice.
- On redemption, Macau SAR assumes the Concessionaire’s rights and obligations from valid legal transactions entered before the notice date.
- Obligations from contracts signed after the notice are only assumed if pre-authorized by the Government.
- Macau SAR’s assumption of obligations does not waive its right to recover amounts for obligations outside normal concession management.
- Upon redemption, the Concessionaire is entitled to fair and equitable compensation under Law No. 16/2001, Section 46(2), for benefits lost on projects in the approved Investment Plans; for construction projects, compensation equals prior fiscal year income (pre-interest, depreciation, amortization) multiplied by remaining years of the concession.
