- Seizure (Clause 84): If unauthorized termination/interruption is imminent or serious operational deficiencies exist, the Government may replace the Concessionaire to ensure continued operation; related expenses are borne by the Concessionaire, and the Government may use provided collateral and the controlling shareholder’s guarantee.
- Normal operations must be resumed by the Concessionaire when notified; failure or persistent deficiencies may lead to unilateral termination for breach.
- Termination for non-compliance (Clause 85): The Chief Executive may unilaterally terminate the concession for breaches of law or contract, including:
  - Operating unauthorized games or activities beyond corporate scope;
  - Abandonment or unjustified suspension exceeding 7 consecutive days or 14 non-consecutive days per year;
  - Unauthorized transfer of operation rights;
  - Failure to pay due taxes, premiums, contributions, or other remuneration not timely contested;
  - Refusal/inability to resume operations after seizure or persistence of the underlying issues.

nodes.title: Termination for non-compliance with obligations
nodes.heading:
Clause 85
Termination for non-compliance with obligations
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Chief Executive may terminate the concession for the operation of games of fortune or chance in casinos, by unilateral termination, in the event of non-compli ance with obligations arising from legislation or from this concession contract to which the Concessionaire is bound.
nodes.summary:
- Government seizure/attachment: During seizure, the concessionaire bears maintenance and normalization costs; the Government may use collateral and the controlling shareholder’s guarantee. When reasons for seizure end, the concessionaire can be ordered to resume operations; failure or continued deficiencies can lead to unilateral termination for breach.

- Clause 85 (Termination for non-compliance): Authorizes the Chief Executive to unilaterally terminate for breaches of law or contract. Enumerates specific grounds, including unauthorized gaming or excluded activities, abandonment or unjustified suspension, improper transfer of operation rights, nonpayment of dues, refusal/inability to resume after attachment, obstruction of supervision, systematic breach of fundamental obligations, failure to provide or reinforce guarantees, bankruptcy/insolvency, serious fraud harming public interest, serious/repeated gaming rule violations, and failure to meet required investments by the set deadline. Establishes a cure-notice process except for irremediable breaches; allows urgent attachment; termination takes immediate effect upon notice; financiers/guarantors may be notified. Provides for compensation per general law and mandates immediate, cost-free reversion to Macau SAR of the casinos and all gaming equipment/utensils, free of encumbrances.

- Clause 86 (Cessation): The concession ends at term expiry, terminating contractual relations except for clauses that survive. The concessionaire is solely responsible for winding down its own contracts; Macau SAR has no liability.

- Clause 87 (Revisions): The concession contract may be revised after Government–Concessionaire consultations, following legal requirements and the formalities in Section 91 of Administrative Regulation No. 26/2001.

- Chapter XXI / Clause 88: Introduces a pre-litigation consultation phase (details not included in the excerpt).

nodes.title: Cessation
nodes.heading:
Clause 86
Cessation
nodes.start_phrase: One. The concession and contract for the operation of games of fortune or chance in casinos shall cease at the end of the concession period, ceasing the existing contractual relations between the Parties, without prejudice to the clauses of this concession contract that last beyond the term of the concession.
nodes.summary:
- Unilateral termination for breach: If the Government unilaterally terminates the concession for breach, it must compensate the Concessionaire, with compensation calculated under general legal rules.
- Asset reversion on unilateral termination: Such termination triggers immediate, cost-free reversion to the Macau SAR of the affected casinos and all gaming equipment and utensils, even if located outside the casinos, free of any burdens or charges.
- Cessation at end of term: The concession and related contractual relations end when the concession period expires, except for clauses that expressly survive beyond the term.
- Post-cessation responsibilities: Upon cessation, the Concessionaire is solely responsible for winding up and terminating the effects of its contracts; the Macau SAR bears no liability for these.
- Contract revisions and amendments: The concession contract may be revised after Government–Concessionaire consultations, in accordance with the law; any revisions or addenda must follow the formalities in Section 91 of Administrative Regulation No. 26/2001.
- Pre-litigation phase: Introduces a chapter on consultations during the pre-litigation phase (details not included in the excerpt).

nodes.title: Contract revisions and amendments
nodes.heading:
CHAPTER XX
Contract revisions and amendments
nodes.start_phrase: One. This concession contract may be revis ed after consultations between the Gove rnment and the Concessionaire, under the terms of the law .
nodes.summary:
- Addresses unilateral termination for breach: such termination triggers a duty to compensate the Concessionaire, with compensation calculated under general legal principles.
- Specifies that unilateral termination for breach leads to immediate, cost-free reversion to the Macau SAR of the casinos and all gaming equipment/utensils, even if located outside the casinos.
- Clause 86 (Cessation): The concession and casino gaming contract end at the expiration of the concession term; certain clauses may survive. Upon cessation, the Concessionaire must handle termination of all its related contracts, and the Macau SAR bears no liability for those contracts.
- Chapter XX / Clause 87 (Contract revisions and amendments): The contract may be revised after Government–Concessionaire consultations in accordance with the law; any revisions or addenda must follow the formalities in Section 91 of Administrative Regulation No. 26/2001.
- Chapter XXI / Clause 88 (Pre-litigation phase): Introduces consultations in the pre-litigation phase (details not included in the excerpt).

nodes.title: Revisions of the concession contract
nodes.heading:
Clause 87
Revisions of the concession contract
nodes.start_phrase: One. This concession contract may be revis ed after consultations between the Gove rnment and the Concessionaire, under the terms of the law .
nodes.summary:
- Sets out consequences of unilateral termination for breach of a casino concession: the Concessionaire is entitled to compensation calculated under general law, and the casinos plus all gaming equipment and utensils immediately revert to the Macau SAR at no cost, free of any burdens, even if equipment is located outside the casinos.
- Defines cessation at the end of the concession term: contractual relations between the parties end except for clauses that expressly survive; the Concessionaire bears full responsibility for winding up all its own contracts, with the Macau SAR having no liability for them.
- Provides for revision and amendment of the concession contract: changes may occur after Government–Concessionaire consultations in accordance with applicable law and must follow the formalities in Section 91 of Administrative Regulation No. 26/2001.
- Introduces a pre-litigation phase with consultations (details of the consultation process are not included in the excerpt).

nodes.title: Pre-litigation phase
nodes.heading:
CHAPTER XXI
Pre-litigation phase
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Parties undertake to hold consultations whenever questions or diver gences arise between them regarding the validity , application, execution, interpretation, or integration of the rules that govern this concession contract.
nodes.summary:
- Unilateral termination for breach: If the Government unilaterally terminates the concession for breach, the Concessionaire is entitled to compensation calculated under general legal principles. Termination triggers immediate, cost-free reversion to the Macau SAR of the casinos involved and all gaming equipment and utensils, even if located outside the casinos.
- Clause 86 (Cessation): The concession ends at the expiry of its term, ending contractual relations except for clauses that expressly survive. Upon cessation, the Concessionaire must handle termination of all its own contracts, with the Macau SAR bearing no liability for those arrangements.
- Chapter XX / Clause 87 (Contract revisions and amendments): The concession contract may be revised after Government–Concessionaire consultations in accordance with the law. Any revisions or addenda must follow the formalities set out in Section 91 of Administrative Regulation No. 26/2001.
- Chapter XXI / Clause 88 (Pre-litigation phase): Establishes a consultation mechanism in the pre-litigation phase (details to be elaborated in the clause).

nodes.title: Consultations in pre-litigation phase
nodes.heading:
Clause 88
Consultations in pr e-litigation phase
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Parties undertake to hold consultations whenever questions or diver gences arise between them regarding the validity , application, execution, interpretation, or integration of the rules that govern this concession contract.
nodes.summary:
- Unilateral termination for breach: If the Government unilaterally terminates for breach, it must compensate the Concessionaire per law; all relevant casinos and gaming equipment/utensils immediately revert to the Macau SAR at no cost, free of burdens, even if some items are outside casino premises.
- Cessation at end of term (Clause 86): The concession and related contractual relations end when the concession period expires, with certain clauses surviving; the Concessionaire is solely responsible for winding down its own contracts, and the Macau SAR bears no liability for them.
- Contract revisions (Clause 87): The concession may be revised after Government–Concessionaire consultations under applicable law; revisions and addenda must follow the formalities in Section 91 of Administrative Regulation No. 26/2001.
- Pre-litigation consultations (Clause 88): The Parties must consult on disputes over validity, application, execution, interpretation, or integration of the contract; during consultations, the Concessionaire must fully and timely comply with the contract and Government determinations, without interrupting operations; this applies to successive determinations on the same matter if the first was issued before consultations began.
- Final provisions—licenses and permits (Clause 89): The Concessionaire must obtain, pay for, maintain, and comply with all required licenses/permits/authorizations; it must promptly notify the Government of any withdrawal, expiry, suspension, revocation, or loss of effect and the remedial measures taken; no contract clause substitutes for legally required approvals.
- Final provisions—IP rights (Clause 90): The Concessionaire must respect industrial and intellectual property rights under Macau SAR law and is solely liable for any infringements.

nodes.title: Final Provisions
nodes.heading:
CHAPTER XXII
Final Provisions
nodes.start_phrase: One. This concession contract does not exempt the Concessionaire from applying for, paying for, and/or endeavoring to obtain all licenses, permits, or authorizations necessary to carry out any aspect of its activity or for the fulfilment of the obligations foreseen in this concession contract, as well as from observing or fulfilling all the requirements necessary to obtain and maintain their validity .
nodes.summary:
- Establishes a duty for the Parties to hold consultations whenever questions or divergences arise regarding the validity, application, execution, interpretation, or integration of the concession contract’s rules.
- Clarifies that raising issues does not suspend or reduce the Concessionaire’s obligation to fully and timely comply with the contract and Government determinations, nor permit any interruption of activities; operations must continue under the terms in force at the time the issue was submitted.
- Extends the Concessionaire’s obligation to comply to successive Government determinations on the same matter, including those issued after consultations begin, provided the first determination was communicated before consultations started.
- Chapter XXII – Final Provisions, Clause 89 (Licenses/Permits/Authorizations): The Concessionaire must obtain, pay for, and maintain all necessary licenses, permits, and authorizations; comply with all requirements for their validity; immediately inform the Government of any withdrawal, expiry, suspension, revocation, or loss of effect and report remedial measures; and acknowledges that nothing in the contract replaces legally or contractually required authorizations.
- Clause 90 (Industrial and Intellectual Property): The Concessionaire must respect industrial and intellectual property rights under Macau SAR law and bears exclusive liability for any infringement.

nodes.title: Securing licenses, permits, or authorizations
nodes.heading:
Clause 89
Securing licenses, permits, or authorizations
nodes.start_phrase: One. This concession contract does not exempt the Concessionaire from applying for, paying for, and/or endeavoring to obtain all licenses, permits, or authorizations necessary to carry out any aspect of its activity or for the fulfilment of the obligations foreseen in this concession contract, as well as from observing or fulfilling all the requirements necessary to obtain and maintain their validity .
nodes.summary:
- Establishes a consultation mechanism: Parties must consult whenever questions or disputes arise over the validity, application, execution, interpretation, or integration of the concession contract’s rules.
- Maintains operational and compliance obligations during consultations: The Concessionaire must continue all activities without interruption and fully comply with the contract and Government determinations in force at the time the issue is raised.
- Extends compliance to successive Government determinations: Even if new determinations on the same matter are issued after consultations begin, the Concessionaire must comply, provided the first related determination was communicated before consultations started.
- Final provisions on licenses/permits (Clause 89): The Concessionaire must obtain, pay for, and maintain all necessary licenses, permits, and authorizations, meet all related requirements, and promptly inform the Government of any withdrawal, expiry, suspension, revocation, or loss of effect, including measures taken to restore them. No contract clause substitutes for legally required approvals.
- Intellectual property (Clause 90): The Concessionaire must respect industrial and intellectual property rights under Macau SAR law and is solely liable for any infringements.

nodes.title: Industrial and intellectual property rights
nodes.heading:
Clause 90
Industrial and intellectual pr operty rights
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionaire undertakes to respect industrial and intellectual property rights in the exercise of its activity , under the terms of the law in force in the Macau SAR and is exclusively liable for the ef fects resulting from their violation.
nodes.summary:
- Consultations: Parties must consult on any questions over validity, application, execution, interpretation, or integration of the concession rules. Consultations do not suspend the Concessionaire’s obligations or operations; activities must continue under prevailing terms. Compliance extends to successive Government determinations on the same matter if the first was notified before consultations began.

- Licenses/permits/authorizations (Clause 89): The Concessionaire remains fully responsible for obtaining, paying for, and maintaining all required licenses/permits/authorizations and for meeting all related conditions. It must immediately inform the Government of any withdrawal, expiry, suspension, revocation, or loss of effect, and report corrective measures. Nothing in the contract replaces legally required licensing.

- Industrial and intellectual property (Clause 90): The Concessionaire must respect IPR under Macau SAR law and is solely liable for infringements. Grant of licenses/authorizations (including for Investment Plans) presumes IPR compliance by the Concessionaire. The Concessionaire must provide Macau SAR with studies, plans, blueprints, and other materials needed to perform its duties or exercise rights, and prepare documents to confirm/register such rights. If IPR disputes with third parties persist, Macau SAR will defend the rights and the Concessionaire must assist.

- Notifications and approvals (Clause 91): Unless specified otherwise, communications must be in writing and delivered by hand with docket, by fax with receipt, or by prepaid registered mail. Government authorizations are prior and may include conditions. Non-response to Concessionaire requests equals rejection. Party domiciles for notices include the Government (Direcção de Inspecção e Coordenação de Jogos).

nodes.title: Notifications, communications, notices, authorizations, and approvals
nodes.heading:
Clause 91
Notifications, communications, notices, authorizations, and appr ovals
nodes.start_phrase: One. Unless otherwise specified, notices, notifications, communications, authorizations and approvals referred to in this concession agreement shall be in writing and made:
nodes.summary:
- Intellectual and industrial property: Licenses and permits presume the Concessionaire’s compliance with all IP rights. The Concessionaire must provide the Macau SAR with all studies, plans, and materials needed to perform the contract, prepare documents to confirm/register related rights upon request, and assist the Government in defending such rights in disputes with third parties.
- Notifications and approvals: All notices and approvals must be in writing (hand delivery with docket, fax with receipt, or prepaid registered letter). Government authorizations are prior and may include conditions. Non-response to requests is deemed rejection. Specific addresses and fax numbers for both parties are provided, with the ability to update them upon prior notice.
- Competition compliance: The Concessionaire must observe fair competition principles, avoid agreements or concerted practices with other concessionaires or their group companies that restrict competition, and refrain from abusing a dominant market position.
- Junket responsibility: The Concessionaire is liable to the Government for the casino activities of its registered junkets (including administrators, key employees, and collaborators) and must supervise their conduct.
- Promotion and marketing: The Concessionaire must run advertising and marketing campaigns for its Macau undertakings domestically and abroad, coordinating such efforts with the Government to promote Macau internationally.

nodes.title: Prohibition of acts restricting competition
nodes.heading:
Clause 92
Prohibition of acts r estricting competition
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionair e undertakes to carry out its activity in due respect of sound and fair competition, subject to the inherent principles of market economy .
nodes.summary:
- Identification and contact details: Lists the government authority’s address and fax, and the concessionaire MGM Grand Paradise S.A.’s registered address and fax in Macau. Allows either party to change addresses/fax reception points with prior notice to the other.
- Competition compliance (Clause 92): Requires the concessionaire to respect fair competition and market economy principles; prohibits anti-competitive agreements or concerted practices with other Macau concessionaires or their group companies; forbids abuse of a dominant market position.
- Junket responsibility (Clause 93): Makes the concessionaire liable to the government for the casino activities of its registered junkets, including their administrators, key employees, and collaborators, and obliges the concessionaire to supervise their activities.
- Promotion and marketing (Clause 94): Obligates the concessionaire, under Section 42-A of Law No. 16/2001, to conduct advertising and marketing campaigns in Macau and abroad; commits the government and the concessionaire to coordinate publicity and marketing to promote Macau internationally.

nodes.title: Junkets
nodes.heading:
Clause 93
Junkets
nodes.start_phrase: The Concessionaire is liable to the Government for the casino activities of their registered junkets, as well as their administrators, key employees and collaborators and it shall supervise their activity .
nodes.summary:
- Identifies the parties and contact details: Government address (Avenida da Praia Grande, Edifício China Plaza) and the concessionaire MGM Grand Paradise S.A. (Avenida Dr. Sun Yat Sen, Edifício MGM), with fax numbers, and allows either party to change addresses/fax points with prior notice.
- Clause 92 (Competition): The concessionaire must operate under fair competition principles; it is prohibited from entering anti-competitive agreements or concerted practices with other Macau concessionaires or related group companies, and from abusing a dominant market position.
- Clause 93 (Junkets): The concessionaire is responsible to the Government for the casino activities of its registered junkets, including their administrators, key employees, and collaborators, and must supervise their activities.
- Clause 94 (Promotion): In line with Law No. 16/2001, the concessionaire must conduct advertising and marketing for its operations in Macau and abroad; the Government and the concessionaire will coordinate publicity and marketing to promote Macau internationally.

nodes.title: Promotion of the Concessionaire enterprises
nodes.heading:
Clause 94
Promotion of the Concessionair e enterprises
nodes.start_phrase: One. In compl iance with the provisions of Section 42-A of Law No. 16/2001, the Concessionaire pledges to carry out advertising and marketing campaigns for its undertakings in Macau SAR and abroad.
nodes.summary:
- Identifies the concessionaire as MGM Grand Paradise S.A., provides contact addresses and fax numbers, and allows parties to change these upon prior notice.
- Establishes competition rules: the concessionaire must uphold fair competition, avoid anti-competitive agreements or concerted practices with other concessionaires or affiliated companies, and must not abuse a dominant market position (Clause 92).
- Holds the concessionaire liable for the activities of its registered junkets (including administrators, key employees, and collaborators) and requires supervision of their conduct (Clause 93).
- Requires the concessionaire to conduct advertising and marketing campaigns in Macau and abroad, coordinate publicity with the Government to promote Macau internationally, and prohibits use of casino-related images or context to promote interactive gaming without Government permission (Clause 94).
- Incorporates the concessionaire’s public tender proposal (from CE Order No. 136/2022) into the contract where not contradicted (Clause 95).
- Regulates gaming chips: acquisition requires DICJ authorization; circulation requires authorization by the Secretary for Economy and Finance who may set a cap; mandates chip redemption and prudential requirements (solvency ratio, provisions, and highly liquid assets) to ensure immediate payment (Clause 96).
- Imposes confidentiality over documents produced by the Government or the concessionaire, requiring Government authorization for disclosure and ensuring their employees are bound by confidentiality obligations (Clause 97).

- Clause 96 – Casino chips:
  - Acquisition of chips requires authorization from the Gaming Inspection and Coordination Bureau.
  - Circulation of chips requires authorization from the Secretary for Economy and Finance, who may set a maximum total amount in circulation.
  - The concessionaire must guarantee chip redemption (cash or credit).
  - The concessionaire must maintain solvency, provisions, and comply with prudential rules set by the Government, holding cash or highly liquid securities to ensure immediate chip payment.
- Clause 97 – Confidentiality:
  - Documents produced by the Government or the concessionaire are confidential and may only be disclosed to third parties with Government authorization.
  - Both parties must ensure their employees (including Macau SAR Public Administration staff and concessionaire employees) are bound by confidentiality obligations.

Clause 97
Confidentiality
nodes.start_phrase: One. In compliance with the provisions in the concessions regime mentioned in Clause 6, the documents produced by the Government or by the Concessionaire are confidential and may only be made available to third parties with the Government’ s authorization.
nodes.summary:
- Restriction on marketing: The concessionaire may not use images or contextual references to its casinos on websites or other media promoting interactive games without prior Government permission.
- Incorporation of tender proposal (Clause 95): The bidder’s proposal from the public tender under Chief Executive Order No. 136/2022 forms part of the concession contract wherever it is not expressly or implicitly contradicted.
- Casino chips governance (Clause 96): Acquisition of chips requires authorization from the Gaming Inspection and Coordination Bureau; chip circulation requires authorization from the Secretary for Economy and Finance, who may cap total chips; the concessionaire must redeem chips in circulation (cash or credit) and maintain prudential solvency and liquidity (cash or highly liquid securities) as set by the Government.
- Confidentiality regime (Clause 97): Government and concessionaire documents are confidential and may only be disclosed with Government authorization; employees and relevant third parties must be bound by confidentiality; the contract’s contents are confidential; exceptions apply for judicial and regulatory requests and for necessary disclosures to financiers, investors, lawyers, accountants, auditors, and advisors under equivalent confidentiality; the concessionaire must inform the Government of certain disclosures; without prejudice to Section 48-N of Law No. 16/2001.
- Complaints handling (Clause 98): The concessionaire must provide a dedicated complaints book for casino patrons, display notices of its availability, forward complaints and a report to the Government within 48 hours, and may keep the book in electronic form.

Complaints book
nodes.start_phrase: One. The Concessionaire undertakes to set up and keep available to casino patrons a specific complaints book for complaints regarding the operation of games of fortune or chance in casinos.
nodes.summary:
- Confidentiality obligations:
  - Government and Concessionaire must impose secrecy on anyone with access to confidential documents (e.g., consultants, service providers).
  - Concessionaire must keep the entire concession contract and related documents confidential; disclosure to third parties requires Government authorization.
  - Exceptions for disclosures requested by competent judicial authorities, gaming regulators (including in other jurisdictions), and securities regulators, with mandatory notice to the Government.
  - Permitted disclosure to external financial entities, investors, lawyers, accountants, auditors, and advisors, provided they are bound by equivalent confidentiality.
  - After authorization, Concessionaire must ensure all recipients are bound by secrecy.
  - Without prejudice to Section 48-N of Law No. 16/2001.

- Complaints book:
  - Concessionaire must maintain a dedicated complaints book for casino gaming operations.
  - Visible notice of the book’s existence must be posted in casinos and other gambling areas.
  - Complaints and the Concessionaire’s report must be forwarded to the Government within 48 hours.
  - The complaints book may be in electronic form.

nodes.title: EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT
nodes.heading:
Exhibit 10.4(19)
EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT
nodes.start_phrase: This Empl oyment Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of October 4, 2022, by and between MGM Resorts Satellite, LLC (“Employer”), and Gary Fritz (“Employee”).
nodes.summary:
- Parties and role: Employment Agreement between MGM Resorts Satellite, LLC and Gary Fritz as President – Interactive, reporting to the CEO; “Company” defined as MGM Resorts International and its affiliates.
- Term: October 1, 2022 through September 30, 2026, retroactive if executed later; post-term employment defaults to at-will with specified sections surviving.
- Compensation and benefits:
  - Base salary: $1,250,000 annually; benefits comparable to Company’s second-highest executive rank; reimbursement of reasonable business/travel expenses; eligibility for deferred compensation plan.
  - Annual bonus (from FY2023): Target equals 100% of base; initially 50% Adjusted EBITDAR and 50% strategic/leadership goals; program and metrics may be modified. No 2022 annual bonus, but potential pro rata Target Bonus at Committee discretion.
  - Bonus timing/clawback: Paid Jan 1–Mar 15 following the fiscal year; any amount above 150% of target paid as fully vested Deferred RSUs, delivered in four annual installments; subject to Company clawback policies, including Dodd-Frank.
  - Travel: Extensive travel; may use company aircraft if authorized; otherwise first-class or best available commercial.
  - Special bonuses: Two distinct opportunities of $2,000,000 each (50% cash/50% RSUs) tied to (1) BetMGM TTM Adjusted EBITDA and (2) launching a defined digital offering at an MGM property (details in Exhibit A).
  - Equity awards (2022–2025): Annual grants targeted at $3,750,000 Accounting Value (60% performance/service RSUs; 40% service RSUs), terms at Committee discretion. Treatment upon death/disability/qualifying terminations no less favorable than Forms in Exhibits B–D. Change of Control benefits no less favorable than the Aug 16, 2022 COC Policy.
- Duties/conflicts/boards: Full-time, exclusive service; outside services require approval. Board service permitted if non-competitive, limited to one additional public company board (plus any on Exhibit E) with conflict-of-interest approval not unreasonably withheld.
- Policies and compliance: Bound by Company policies (e.g., anti-harassment, code of conduct, conflict of interest) and responsible gaming standards.
- Licensing: Must obtain and maintain required gaming/regulatory licenses; failure or suitability issues can trigger termination.
- Restrictive covenants:
  - Non-compete: 12 months post-employment against roles substantially similar to last-year role with any defined “Competitor” (gaming/convention/hotel linked to gaming within 150 miles of Company sites; worldwide for mobile gaming/betting). Carve-outs if position is eliminated, Employee resigns for Good Cause, or certain at-will terminations without Employer’s Good Cause after the Specified Term.
  - Non-solicit: 12 months restriction on soliciting Business Contacts or certain employees.
  - Confidentiality/trade secrets: Broad protection of Trade Secrets and Confidential Information; DTSA whistleblower notice; third-party information protection.
  - Information handling: Company-approved devices specified (MacBook Pro, iPad, Google Pixel); return/deletion of Company information at separation; inspection protocols; acknowledgment of copyrights in compilations and restrictions on copying/derivative works.
  - Enforcement: Acknowledged reasonableness; injunctive relief available; assignment of restrictive covenants permitted with assumption of obligations.
- Termination and severance:
  - Employer Good Cause: Defined to include certain criminal, licensing, misconduct, policy breaches, refusal to follow directives, materially adverse conduct, and unsatisfied licensing; cure periods for specified items. On Good Cause, only accrued amounts and expense reimbursements owed.
  - Death: 12 months’ salary lump sum to beneficiary plus any Earned Bonus Amount.
  - Disability: 12 months’ salary lump sum, COBRA Payment (1.5x 12 months of premiums), and any Earned Bonus; Disability defined by inability to perform essential functions for 6 months (consecutive or cumulative in 12 months).
  - Employer No Cause during term: Severance equals one times base salary plus Target Bonus paid over 12 months, COBRA Payment (1.5x 12 months) in 12 installments, and any earned but unpaid bonus; if due to a “Material Digital Acquisition,” severance increases to 2x base + 2x Target over 24 months plus COBRA Payment, with coordination against COC Policy to deliver greater aggregate cash per Agreement timing.
  - Employer No Cause after term (during Restricted Period): Lump sum equal to then-current annual base salary plus any Earned Bonus Amount.
  - Employee Good Cause: Defined (e.g., material duty change, pay/target bonus decrease, adverse reporting change, relocation from greater Seattle, unpaid compensation, Employer breach, required relocation outside North America post-Material Digital Acquisition, or significant power limitation); subject to notice/cure. Triggers Severance or MDA Severance and COBRA Payment as above, plus any accrued/earned bonus.
  - Employee No Cause resignation: 30 days’ notice; Employer may accelerate but must pay through notice period; no severance beyond accrued items.
  - Release/cooperation: Severance/COBRA conditioned on execution and non-revocation of a general release; post-separation cooperation required, with reasonable compensation if more than de minimis.
  - Optional salary continuation: Employer may elect salary continuation after a Washington “layoff” to support enforceability of restrictive covenants.
- Dispute resolution and legal terms:
  - Arbitration: Binding arbitration for employment-related disputes except sex discrimination/harassment claims; per Exhibit F; venue King County, Washington.
  - Severability, no waiver, amendment mechanics (written, Committee-approved), governing law (Washington), venue/jurisdiction (King County).
  - Assignment/successors: Employer may assign; Agreement binds successors; prior agreements superseded.
  - Stockholder protections: No claims against MGMRI stockholders in their stockholder capacity.
  - Section 409A: Intended to comply or be exempt; definitions, installment and reimbursement rules; specified employee six-month delay where applicable.
  - Intellectual property: Broad assignment to Employer of IP created with Company resources, on premises, during hours, or relating to employment; works made for hire; cooperation/POA for filings; no extra compensation.
  - Indemnification: Employer will seek Board approval to designate Employee as an MGM Officer for indemnification under MGM’s bylaws.
  - Interpretation: Negotiated agreement; restrictive covenants intended to comply with Washington RCW 49.62.
  - Execution: Signed by Gary Fritz (Oct 5, 2022) and MGM Resorts Satellite, LLC (Oct 10, 2022).

- Exhibit 99.1: Overview of the company’s regulatory and licensing environment:
  - The gaming industry is highly regulated; each casino is subject to extensive jurisdictional laws focused on the responsibility, financial stability, and character of owners/managers/financial stakeholders. Violations in one jurisdiction can trigger actions in others.
  - The business is also subject to numerous non-gaming laws (alcohol, smoking, environmental, employment/immigration, currency transactions, taxation, zoning/building, land use, marketing/advertising, lending, privacy, telemarketing, OFAC, FCPA, and anti-money laundering). Changes or differing interpretations could adversely affect operations.
  - Core regulatory requirements include: excluding unsuitable persons; robust accounting and internal controls; reliable recordkeeping and reporting; preventing fraud/cheating; licensing/registration of key employees and vendors; paying gaming taxes/fees; responsible gaming programs; and compliance with community benefits agreements.
  - Gaming regulators have broad discretion: they adopt rules, investigate and enforce, impose sanctions, assess suitability and grant licenses, collect and review reports, approve significant transactions (including M&A, change-of-control, securities and debt offerings), and establish/collect taxes and fees.

nodes.title: DESCRIPTION OF REGULATION AND LICENSING
nodes.heading:
Exhibit 99.1
DESCRIPTION OF REGULATION AND LICENSING
nodes.start_phrase: The gaming industry is highly regulated, and we must maintain our licenses and pay gaming taxes to continue our operations.
nodes.summary:
- Broad regulatory framework: Casinos are heavily regulated across jurisdictions, requiring ongoing licensing, tax payments, and compliance with changing laws that can materially affect operations.
- Non-gaming compliance: Operations are also subject to laws on alcohol, smoking, environment, employment/immigration, currency reporting, taxation, zoning/building, land use, marketing/advertising, lending, privacy, telemarketing, OFAC, FCPA, and AML.
- Regulator authority: Agencies interpret/enforce gaming laws, issue regulations, investigate participants, impose sanctions/fines, determine suitability, grant licenses, oversee major transactions, and collect taxes/fees.
- Licensing and suitability: Company, subsidiaries, key personnel, certain shareholders and debt holders must obtain licenses or findings of suitability; regulators have broad discretion to deny, condition, suspend, or revoke approvals.
- Suitability criteria: Character, integrity, financial stability, facility quality/investment, competitive and community impact, jurisdictional revenues, and workforce diversity/local hiring practices.
- Shareholder and debt holder oversight: Threshold reporting and suitability (e.g., Nevada 5% report, 10% suitability within 30 days), with institutional investor waivers (often up to 15%) subject to strict investment-only conditions.
- Consequences of unsuitability: Required severance of relationships; restrictions on dividends, voting, or remuneration to unsuitable persons; potential forced divestiture and disciplinary actions.
- Vendor, lender, and asset controls: Supplier licensing required; foreclosure/transfer of gaming assets requires prior approvals (e.g., NJ interim casino authorization); licenses are generally non-transferable and cannot be pledged.
- Violations and cross-jurisdiction risk: Noncompliance can lead to fines, license limits/suspension/revocation, appointment of trustees/conservators, forfeiture of earnings, and repercussions in other jurisdictions.
- Reporting/recordkeeping: Periodic financial/operational reports, inspections, federal CTRs and SARs, stock ledger maintenance, beneficial ownership disclosures, potential stock legends, and additional regulator-imposed restrictions.
- Transaction approvals: Prior notice/approval for material financings, securities offerings tied to gaming, changes of control, recapitalizations, exceptional stock repurchases, and anti-takeover responses; regulators can order rescission.
- Governance/compliance programs: Some jurisdictions require compliance committees and independent audit committee oversight of surveillance/internal audit functions.
- Taxes and fees: Significant license fees and gaming taxes based on gross revenues, device/table counts, and location; live entertainment taxes may apply; rates can change.
- Operational requirements: Local/minority/women/veteran procurement and workforce goals; hours and gaming position limits; Mississippi non-gaming infrastructure rules; Nevada cybersecurity regulation (risk assessment, responsible designee, annual review, incident reporting).
- Racetrack and VLT regulation: Separate, extensive racing and pari-mutuel oversight in NY and OH; VLT operations linked to maintaining live racing licenses.
- Online gaming and sports betting: Legalization and regulation across multiple states (NV poker; NJ iGaming/sports; MS on-prem sports; MI iGaming/sports; MD, OH, MA sports), with constraints on event types, branding limits, and timelines.
- Federal Wire Act developments: DOJ’s 2018 reinterpretation limiting non-sports wagering reversed by 2019 district court; 2021 First Circuit largely affirmed that the Wire Act applies only to sports-related interstate communications.
- Macau regulatory regime: MGM Grand Paradise holds a gaming concession (2023–2032) with strict approval requirements for share/asset transfers, control changes, capitalization, and governance; exclusive Macau jurisdiction applies.
- Macau concession terms: Potential reversion of casino premises/equipment without compensation at expiry; government redemption right from 2030 with compensation; unilateral termination for fundamental noncompliance.
- Macau financial obligations: Annual fixed and variable premiums per table/machine with minimums; 35% special gaming tax on GGR plus 2% and 3% levies; taxes calculated on GGR without credit loss deductions; land concessions with rent obligations.
- Macau tax incentives: Historical corporate income tax exemptions on casino profits granted and extended through December 31, 2022.
